provisions.label: preamble
provisions.text:
DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS FOR TRILOGY AT REDMOND RIDGE RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY

DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS is made this 30th day of November, 2001, by Trilogy at Redmond Ridge, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Declarant").

provisions.label: part-one
provisions.heading: Introduction to the Residential Community

noRule.note: Purpose of the Declaration.

provisions.text:
PART ONE: INTRODUCTION TO THE RESIDENTIAL COMMUNITY

Trilogy at Redmond Ridge, LLC, has established this Declaration to provide a governance structure and a flexible system of standards and procedures for the development, administration, maintenance, and preservation of the Trilogy at Redmond Ridge residential community.

provisions.label: article-1
provisions.heading: Creation of the Residential Community
provisions.text: Article 1 Creation of the Residential Community

provisions.heading: Purpose and Intent

noRule.note: Its text is in its counted paragraphs.

provisions.text: 1.1 Purpose and Intent.

provisions.label: 1.1/p1

noRule.note: Purpose of the plan of development and of creating the Association.

provisions.text: Declarant, as the owner of the real property described in Exhibit "A," intends by Recording this Declaration to create a general plan of development for the residential portions of the master planned community known as Trilogy at Redmond Ridge. This Declaration provides the Residential Community's overall development, administration, maintenance, and preservation, and provides a flexible and reasonable procedure for its future expansion. An integral part of the development plan is the creation of Trilogy at Redmond Ridge Residential Community Association, an association comprised of all owners of real property in the community, to own, operate, and/or maintain various common areas and Residential Community improvements and to administer and enforce this Declaration and the other Governing Documents.

provisions.label: 1.1/p2

noRule.note: The community is housing for persons 55 and over; the age requirements are encoded from 3.1(a).

provisions.text: Trilogy at Redmond Ridge is a community developed for residents 55 years of age or older, and accordingly is exempt from the payment of school impact fees pursuant to King County Code 21A.43.070(7). As such, the Residential Community will comply fully with the requirements for housing for persons age 55 and over, as set forth in the Federal Housing Amendments Act of 1988, 42 U.S.C. §3607(b)(2)(C) and (b)(3) as it hereafter may be amended.

provisions.label: 1.1/p3

noRule.note: The Declaration doesn't create a condominium.

provisions.text: This document does not and is not intended to create a condominium under Washington law.

provisions.heading: Binding Effect

noRule.note: Its text is in its counted paragraphs.

provisions.text: 1.2 Binding Effect

provisions.label: 1.2/p1

noRule.note: The Declaration governs and runs with the property; that's its document's governs: null.

provisions.text: This Declaration governs the property described in Exhibit "A," and any other property submitted to this Declaration in the future, all of which shall be owned, conveyed, and used subject to all of the provisions of this Declaration. This Declaration shall run with the title to such property and, except as otherwise specifically provided, shall bind anyone having any right, title, or interest in any portion of such property, their heirs, successors, successors-in-title, and assigns.

provisions.label: 1.2/p2
provisions.text: This Declaration shall be enforceable by Declarant, the Association, any Owner, and their respective legal representatives, heirs, successors, and assigns, perpetually to the extent permitted by law. If, however, the period for the enforcement of covenants running with the land is limited by law, this Declaration shall be enforceable as provided above for a period of 20 years. After such time, this Declaration shall be extended automatically for successive periods of 10 years each, unless an instrument signed by the requisite number of the then Owners, as set forth in Article 21, has been Recorded within the year preceding any extension agreeing to terminate this Declaration, in which case this Declaration shall be terminated as specified in such instrument. References in this paragraph, and elsewhere in this document, to this Declaration shall be deemed to refer to this Declaration as amended from time to time.

provisions.label: 1.2/p3
provisions.text: Notwithstanding the above, if any provision of this Declaration would be unlawful, void, or voidable by reason of applicability of the rule against perpetuities, such provision shall expire 21 years after the death of the last survivor of the now living descendants of Elizabeth II, Queen of the United Kingdom. Nothing in this Section shall be construed to permit termination of any easement created in this Declaration without the consent of the holder of such easement.

provisions.heading: Governing Documents

noRule.note: Its text is in its counted paragraphs.

provisions.text: 1.3 Governing Documents.

provisions.label: 1.3/p1
provisions.text:
The Residential Community's Governing Documents consist of the following, as each may be amended.
Declaration (Recorded) creates obligations which are binding upon the Association and all present and future owners of property in the Residential Community
Supplemental Declaration (Recorded) adds property to the Residential Community; may impose additional obligations or restrictions on such property
Articles of Incorporation (filed with the Secretary of State) establish the Association as a non-profit corporation under Washington law
By-Laws (Board adopts) govern the Association's internal affairs, such as voting rights, elections, meetings, officers, etc.
Residential Design Guidelines (Declarant adopts) establish architectural standards and guidelines for improvements and modifications to Units, including structures, landscaping, and other items
Use Restrictions (initial set attached as Exhibit "C") govern use of property and activities within the Residential Community
Board Rules and Regulations (Board adopts) establish rules, policies, and procedures for internal governance and Association activities, regulate operation and use of Common Area

provisions.label: 1.3/p2

noRule.note: Recording covenants needs the Declarant's (later the Board's) consent, as 10.5 says. A more restrictive Supplemental Declaration controls, which is how evaluation already works: every rule in force applies.

provisions.text: Any Supplemental Declaration may impose additional, more restrictive restrictions or provisions on any Neighborhood or other portions of the Residential Community, in which case, the more restrictive provisions will be controlling. The Association shall have standing and the power to enforce such standards. However, no Person shall Record any additional covenants, conditions, or restrictions affecting any portion of the Residential Community without Declarant's written consent, so long as Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant owns any property described in Exhibits "A" or "B." Thereafter, the Association's Board of Directors must consent. Any instrument Recorded without the required consent is void and of no force and effect.

provisions.label: 1.3/p3
provisions.text: If there are conflicts among Washington law, the Declaration, the Articles, and the By-Laws, Washington law, the Declaration, the Articles, and the By-Laws (in that order) shall prevail. If there is a conflict between the Governing Documents and any Neighborhood Association's covenants, restrictions, or policies, the Governing Documents will control.

provisions.label: 1.3/p4
provisions.text: The Governing Documents apply to all Owners and any occupants of a Unit. They also apply to tenants, guests, visitors, and invitees.

provisions.label: 1.3/p5

noRule.note: Severability.

provisions.text: If any court determines that any provision of this Declaration is invalid, or invalid as applied in a particular instance, such determination shall not affect the validity of other provisions or other applications of the provision.

provisions.label: article-2
provisions.heading: Concepts and Definitions
provisions.text: Article 2 Concepts and Definitions

provisions.label: article-2/p1

noRule.note: Undefined words have their ordinary meaning; capitalized terms are the defined terms below.

provisions.text: The terms used in the Governing Documents shall generally be given their natural, commonly accepted definitions unless otherwise specified. Capitalized terms shall be defined as set forth below.

provisions.label: article-2/affiliate
provisions.heading: Affiliate
provisions.text: "Affiliate": Any Person which (either directly or indirectly, through one or more intermediaries) controls, is in common control with, or is controlled by, another Person, and any Person that is a director, trustee, officer, co-venturer, subsidiary, or member of any of the foregoing. For the purposes of this definition, the term "control" means the direct or indirect power to direct or cause the direction of an entity's management or policies, whether through the ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise. For purposes of this Declaration, Declarant's Affiliates shall include, without limitation, its members Shea Homes, Inc. and The Quadrant Corporation.

provisions.label: article-2/area-of-common-responsibility
provisions.heading: Area of Common Responsibility
provisions.text: "Area of Common Responsibility": The Common Area, together with such other areas the Association has or assumes responsibility pursuant to the terms of this Declaration, any Supplemental Declaration, any Covenant to Share Costs, or other applicable covenants, contracts, or agreements.

provisions.label: article-2/articles-of-incorporation
provisions.heading: Articles of Incorporation
provisions.text: "Articles of Incorporation" or "Articles": The Articles of Incorporation of Trilogy at Redmond Ridge Residential Community Association, as filed with the Washington Secretary of State, as amended from time to time.

provisions.label: article-2/association
provisions.heading: Association
provisions.text: "Association": The Trilogy at Redmond Ridge Residential Community Association, a Washington nonprofit corporation, its successors or assigns.

provisions.label: article-2/base-assessment
provisions.heading: Base Assessment
provisions.text: "Base Assessment": The assessment levied on all Units subject to assessment under Article 8 to fund Common Expenses for the general benefit of all Units, as determined in accordance with Section 8.1.

provisions.label: article-2/board-of-directors
provisions.heading: Board of Directors
provisions.text: "Board of Directors" or "Board": The body responsible for administration of the Association, selected as provided in the By-Laws and serving as the board of directors under Washington corporate law.

provisions.label: article-2/board-rules-and-regulations
provisions.heading: Board Rules and Regulations
provisions.text: "Board Rules and Regulations": board-adopted rules and regulations which establish administrative procedures for internal Association governance and operating procedures for use of the Common Area and other property included within the Area of Common Responsibility.

provisions.label: article-2/builder
provisions.heading: Builder
provisions.text: "Builder": Any Person who purchases one or more Units for the purpose of constructing improvements for later sale to consumers, or who purchases one or more parcels of land within the Residential Community for further subdivision, development, and/or resale in the ordinary course of such Person's business.

provisions.label: article-2/by-laws
provisions.heading: By-Laws
provisions.text: "By-Laws": The By-Laws of Trilogy at Redmond Ridge Residential Community Association, as amended from time to time.

provisions.label: article-2/class-b-control-period
provisions.heading: Class "B" Control Period
provisions.intro: The Class "B" Control Period expires upon the first to occur of the following:
provisions.text: "Class "B" Control Period": The period of time during which the Class "B" Member is entitled to appoint a majority of the members of the Board.

provisions.label: article-2/class-b-control-period(a)
provisions.text: (a) when 100% of the total number of Units permitted by the Master Plan for the Residential Community, or such lower number of Units as Declarant may elect, have been improved with a dwelling for which a certificate of occupancy has been issued and have been conveyed to Class "A" Members other than Declarant, its Affiliates, or Builders;

provisions.label: article-2/class-b-control-period(b)
provisions.text: (b) the expiration of any five-year period during which title to no Unit is conveyed by Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant to a Class "A" Member,

provisions.label: article-2/class-b-control-period(c)
provisions.text: (c) December 31, 2021; or

provisions.label: article-2/class-b-control-period(d)
provisions.text: (d) when, in its discretion, the Class "B" Member so determines. Upon such termination by the Class B Member, Declarant may require in a Recorded document that so long as the Declarant, its Affiliates or any Builder owns any Unit, any or all actions for which the consent or approval of the Board of Directors is required under this Declaration may be taken only if such action is also consented to or approved by the Declarant.

provisions.label: article-2/common-area
provisions.heading: Common Area
provisions.text: "Common Area": All real and personal property, including easements, which the Association owns, leases, or otherwise holds possessory or use rights in for the common use and enjoyment of the Owners (and other Persons entitled to use and enjoy portions of such property pursuant to any Covenant to Share Costs), including, without limitation, a community center, entrance tracts, perimeter buffers, parks, surface water retention/detention tracts, landscape tracts, recreational vehicle storage areas, recreational facilities, and other tracts or parcels Declarant conveys to the Association. The term shall include the Limited Common Area, as defined below. The term shall not include property owned by any governmental entity unless the Association is the tenant with respect to such property.

provisions.label: article-2/common-expenses
provisions.heading: Common Expenses
provisions.text: "Common Expenses": The actual and estimated expenses which the Association incurs, or expects to incur, for the general benefit of all Owners, including any reasonable reserve, as the Board may find necessary and appropriate pursuant to the Governing Documents. The Common Expenses shall include the Association's share of expenses pursuant to any Covenant to Share Costs.

provisions.label: article-2/community-wide-standard
provisions.heading: Community-Wide Standard
provisions.text: "Community-Wide Standard": The standard of conduct, maintenance, or other activity generally prevailing throughout the Residential Community. Declarant initially shall establish such standard, which may contain objective elements, such as specific lawn or house maintenance requirements, and subjective elements, such as matters subject to the Board's or the DRC's (as defined in Article 4) discretion. The Community-Wide Standard may or may not be set out in writing and may evolve as development progresses and as the needs and demands of the Residential Community change.

provisions.label: article-2/covenant-to-share-costs
provisions.heading: Covenant To Share Costs
provisions.text: "Covenant To Share Costs": Any Recorded Declaration of Easements and Covenant to Share Costs, or similarly denominated instrument, which binds the Association and the Owners. A Covenant to Share Costs may create easements benefiting the Residential Community and other properties within or in the vicinity of Trilogy at Redmond Ridge and may obligate the Association and the owners of such other properties to share the costs of maintaining the property described in such Covenant to Share Costs.

provisions.label: article-2/declarant
provisions.heading: Declarant
provisions.text: "Declarant": Trilogy at Redmond Ridge, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, or any successor or assign who takes title to any portion of the property described in Exhibit "A" or "B" for the purpose of development and/or sale and who is designated as Declarant in a Recorded instrument executed by the immediately preceding Declarant, provided, upon such designation of a successor Declarant, all rights of the former Declarant in and to such status as "Declarant" under this Declaration shall cease, it being understood that as to all of the property now or hereafter subjected to this Declaration, there shall be only one "Declarant" at any one point in time.

provisions.label: article-2/governing-documents
provisions.heading: Governing Documents
provisions.text: "Governing Documents": A collective term referring to this Declaration and any applicable Supplemental Declaration, the By-Laws, the Articles, the Residential Design Guidelines, the Use Restrictions, and the Board Rules and Regulations, as each may be amended from time to time.

provisions.label: article-2/limited-common-area
provisions.heading: Limited Common Area
provisions.text: "Limited Common Area": A portion of the Common Area primarily benefiting one or more, but less than all, Neighborhoods or Owners, as more particularly described in Article 12.

provisions.label: article-2/master-plan
provisions.heading: Master Plan
provisions.text: "Master Plan": The land use plan for the Trilogy at Redmond Ridge (formerly known as Blakely Ridge) urban planned development, prepared pursuant to and in accordance with the UPD Permit, which includes (i) all of the property described in Exhibits "A" and "B," and (ii) additional property south of Novelty Hill Road that also is subject to the UPD Permit. Inclusion of property on the Master Plan shall not, under any circumstances, obligate Declarant to subject such property to this Declaration, nor shall the omission of property described in Exhibit "B" from the Master Plan bar its later submission to this Declaration as provided in Article 9.

provisions.label: article-2/member
provisions.heading: Member
provisions.text: "Member": A Person subject to membership in the Association pursuant to Section 6.2.

provisions.label: article-2/mortgage
provisions.heading: Mortgage
provisions.text: "Mortgage": A mortgage, a deed of trust, a deed to secure debt, or any other form of security instrument affecting title to any Unit. A "Mortgagee" shall refer to a beneficiary or holder of a Mortgage.

provisions.label: article-2/neighborhood
provisions.heading: Neighborhood
provisions.text:
"Neighborhood": A group of Units designated as a separate Neighborhood in accordance with Section 6.4(a). Units within a Neighborhood may share Limited Common Areas and/or receive benefits or services from the Association that are not provided to all Units. A Neighborhood may include more than one housing type and may include noncontiguous parcels of property. If the Association provides benefits or services to less than all Units within a particular Neighborhood, then the benefited Units shall constitute a sub-Neighborhood and the Association may levy Neighborhood Assessments against just those Units and their Owners for such benefits or services.

Where the context permits or requires, the term Neighborhood shall also refer to the Neighborhood Committee (established in accordance with the By-Laws) or Neighborhood Association, if any, having concurrent jurisdiction over the property within the Neighborhood. Neighborhood boundaries may be established and modified as provided in Section 6.4.

provisions.label: article-2/neighborhood-assessments
provisions.heading: Neighborhood Assessments
provisions.text: "Neighborhood Assessments": Assessments levied against Units in a particular Neighborhood to fund Neighborhood Expenses, as described in Section 8.2.

provisions.label: article-2/neighborhood-association
provisions.heading: Neighborhood Association
provisions.text: "Neighborhood Association": A condominium association or other owners association, if any, having concurrent jurisdiction (subject to this Declaration) with the Association over any Neighborhood.

provisions.label: article-2/neighborhood-committee
provisions.heading: Neighborhood Committee
provisions.text: "Neighborhood Committee": A committee which may be formed for any Neighborhood which does not have a Neighborhood Association and which is established in accordance with the By-Laws.

provisions.label: article-2/neighborhood-expenses
provisions.heading: Neighborhood Expenses
provisions.text: "Neighborhood Expenses": The actual and estimated expenses which the Association incurs or expects to incur for the benefit of Owners of Units within a particular Neighborhood, as may be authorized pursuant to this Declaration or in the Supplemental Declaration(s) applicable to such Neighborhood(s). Neighborhood Expenses may include a reasonable reserve for capital repairs and replacements and a reasonable administrative charge.

provisions.label: article-2/owner
provisions.heading: Owner
provisions.text: "Owner": One or more Persons who hold the record title to any Unit, but excluding in all cases any party holding an interest merely as security for the performance of an obligation. If a Unit is sold under a Recorded contract of sale, and the contract specifically so provides, the purchaser (rather than the fee owner) will be considered the Owner.

provisions.label: article-2/person
provisions.heading: Person
provisions.text: "Person": An individual, a corporation, a partnership, a trustee, or any other legal entity.

provisions.label: article-2/private-amenity
provisions.heading: Private Amenity(ies)
provisions.text: "Private Amenity(ies)": Real property and facilities located within, adjacent to, or in the vicinity of Trilogy at Redmond Ridge, which Persons other than the Association own and operate for recreational and related purposes. The Private Amenities may include, without limitation, any golf course or recreational center not owned by the Association which is so located and their related and supporting facilities and improvements.

provisions.label: article-2/record
provisions.heading: Record, Recording, Recorded
provisions.text: "Record," "Recording," or "Recorded": To file, the filing, or filed of record in the Public Real Estate Records of King County, Washington, or such other place which is designated as the official location for recording deeds and similar documents affecting title to real estate.

provisions.label: article-2/residential-design-guidelines
provisions.heading: Residential Design Guidelines
provisions.text: "Residential Design Guidelines": The architectural, design, and construction guidelines and review procedures adopted pursuant to Article 4, as they may be amended.

provisions.label: article-2/special-assessment
provisions.heading: Special Assessment
provisions.text: "Special Assessment": An assessment charged against all Owners or all Owners in a Neighborhood in accordance with Section 8.4.

provisions.label: article-2/specific-assessment
provisions.heading: Specific Assessment
provisions.text: "Specific Assessment": An assessment charged against a particular Unit or particular Units for Association expenses in accordance with Section 8.5.

provisions.label: article-2/supplemental-declaration
provisions.heading: Supplemental Declaration
provisions.text: "Supplemental Declaration": A Recorded instrument which subjects additional property to this Declaration, designates Neighborhoods, identifies Common Area and Limited Common Area, designates Voting Groups, and/or imposes additional restrictions and obligations on the land described.

provisions.label: article-2/residential-community
provisions.heading: Trilogy at Redmond Ridge, Residential Community
provisions.text: "Trilogy at Redmond Ridge" or "Residential Community": The real property described in Exhibit "A," together with such additional property, whether contiguous or noncontiguous, as is subjected to this Declaration in accordance with Article 9.

provisions.label: article-2/trrs
provisions.heading: Trilogy at Redmond Ridge Community Services, TRRS
provisions.text: "Trilogy at Redmond Ridge Community Services" or "TRRS": Trilogy at Redmond Ridge Community Services, a Washington nonprofit corporation, its successors or assigns, formed for the purpose of providing various community services to or for the benefit of the Residential Community.

provisions.label: article-2/unit
provisions.heading: Unit
provisions.text:
"Unit": A portion of the Residential Community, whether improved or unimproved, which may be independently owned and which is intended for development, use, and occupancy as an attached or detached residence for a single family. The term shall refer to the land, if any, which is part of the Unit as well as any improvements thereon. The boundaries of each Unit shall be shown on a Recorded plat; provided, in the case of a building containing multiple dwellings for independent sale (e.g., attached condominium, townhouse, or airspace units), each dwelling which may be sold independently shall be a separate Unit.

A parcel shall be deemed to be a single Unit until such time as a Recorded plat subdivides all or a portion of the parcel. After a plat is Recorded, the subdivided portion shall contain the number of Units shown, created, designated, or described on the plat. Any portion not subdivided shall continue to be a single Unit.

provisions.label: article-2/upd-permit
provisions.heading: UPD Permit
provisions.text: "UPD Permit": The Blakely Ridge Urban Planned Development Permit, DDES File No. L94UP002, as approved by King County Ordinance No. 12090, dated December 19, 1995, as set forth as Exhibit 3 to the Blakely Ridge Urban Planned Development Development Agreement between King County, Washington and Port Blakely Tree Farms Limited Partnership, as Recorded under King County Recording No. 9601090553, as such may be amended or modified from time to time.

provisions.label: article-2/use-restrictions
provisions.heading: Use Restrictions
provisions.text: "Use Restrictions": The initial Use Restrictions set forth in Exhibit "C," as they may be supplemented, modified, and repealed pursuant to Article 3.

provisions.label: article-2/voting-group
provisions.heading: Voting Group
provisions.text: "Voting Group": One or more Neighborhoods whose owners vote on a common slate for election of directors to the Board, as more particularly described in Section 6.4(b) or, if the context so indicates, the group of Members whose Units are represented thereby.

provisions.label: part-two
provisions.heading: Creation and Maintenance of Residential Community Standards

noRule.note: Why the community has standards for use, conduct, maintenance and architecture.

provisions.text:
PART TWO: CREATION AND MAINTENANCE OF RESIDENTIAL COMMUNITY STANDARDS

Established standards for use and conduct, maintenance, and architecture are what give the Residential Community its identity and make it a place that people want to call "home." This Declaration establishes procedures adopting, modifying, applying, and enforcing such standards while providing the flexibility for community standards to evolve as the Residential Community changes and grows.

provisions.label: article-3
provisions.heading: Use and Conduct
provisions.text: Article 3 Use and Conduct

noRule.note: Only the article heading.

provisions.heading: Restrictions on Use, Occupancy, and Alienation
provisions.text: Except as otherwise specifically provided, the restrictions set forth in this Section may be amended only in accordance with Article 20.

provisions.label: 3.1(a)
provisions.heading: Restrictions on Occupancy
provisions.text: The Units within the Residential Community are intended for the housing of persons 55 years of age or older. The provisions of this Section 3.1(a) are intended to be consistent with, and are set forth in order to comply with the Fair Housing Amendments Act, 42 U.S.C. §3601 et seq. (1988), as amended, the exemption set out in 42 U.S.C. §3607(b)(2)(C), and the regulations promulgated thereunder (collectively, as may be amended, the "Act") regarding discrimination based on familial status. Except as provided in Section 3.1(a)(i) below, each Unit, if occupied, must be occupied by at least one person 55 years of age or older. Except as provided in Section 3.1(a)(ii) below, no person under 18 years of age shall occupy or reside in a Unit. The Board, in its sole and absolute discretion, shall have the right and power to determine when a person "occupies or resides" in a Unit, provided that such determinations shall be consistent with Attachment 6 of the UPD Permit.

provisions.label: 3.1(a)(i)
provisions.text: To be in compliance with the Act, at least 80% of the occupied dwellings or residences (which may include attached or detached garages or other structures ancillary to the principal dwelling) within the Residential Community shall at all times have as a permanent occupant at least one person who is 55 years of age or older (the "Qualifying Permanent Resident"). (A dwelling or residence within the Residential Community is referred to individually as a "Residence.") In the event of the death or hospitalization or other prolonged absence of a person who was the sole Qualifying Permanent Resident of a Residence, or in the event of the dissolution of the Qualifying Permanent Resident's marriage, then at the Board's sole and absolute discretion, any person 18 years of age or older who occupied the Residence with such Qualifying Permanent Resident at the time he or she ceases to occupy the Unit may continue to occupy the Residence with no Qualifying Permanent Resident, unless such occupancy (A) would result in fewer than 80% of the occupied Residences being occupied by one person 55 years of age or older, or (B) considering other factors the Board deems appropriate, may jeopardize (whether at the time of the request or in the future) the Residential Community's status as "housing for older persons" under the Act.

provisions.label: 3.1(a)(i)/p2
provisions.text: The Board shall exercise its sole and absolute discretion based upon criteria that the Board shall determine as appropriate, including, without limitation, information then known to the Board concerning potential or pending changes in occupancy of other Residences within the Residential Community, the ages of the persons requesting such permission, the proximity to age 55 of those occupants of other Residences within the Residential Community then under such age, and any other information known to and deemed relevant by the Board in its sole discretion. Any request submitted to the Board pursuant to this Section shall be a written request setting forth the names and ages of all proposed residents and occupants of the Residence and such other information as the Board reasonably may require.

provisions.label: 3.1(a)(ii)
provisions.text: A person under 18 years of age may reside in a Residence as a guest of the occupants of the Residence for a period of not more than 60 days in any calendar year. By way of example rather than limitation, a 10 year old individual may temporarily reside in a Residence for 45 days, and the same or a different 10 year old individual may temporarily reside in the same Residence for a subsequent 15-day period. As such, the total number of days during any calendar year that any one or more individuals under 18 years of age may reside in a Residence pursuant to this Section shall not exceed 60 days.

provisions.label: 3.1(a)(iii)
provisions.text: Nothing in this Section is intended to restrict the ownership of or transfer of title to any Unit, provided, no Owner under the age of 55 may occupy a Residence unless the requirements of this Section are met nor shall any Owner permit occupancy of the Residence in violation of this Section. Owners shall be responsible for including a statement that the Units within the Residential Community are intended for the housing of persons 55 years of age or older, as set forth in this Section, in conspicuous type in any lease or other occupancy agreement or contract of sale relating to such Owner's Unit, which agreements or contracts shall be in writing and signed by the tenant or purchaser, and for clearly disclosing such intent to any prospective tenant, purchaser, or other potential occupant of the Unit. Every lease of a Unit shall provide that failure to comply with the requirements and restrictions of this Section shall constitute a default under the lease.

provisions.label: 3.1(a)(iv)
provisions.text: The inability of an Owner to occupy a Unit shall not relieve such Owner of assessment obligations under this Declaration.

noRule.note: Not occupying a Unit creates no exemption from assessments; the Article 8 assessment rules apply to every Owner regardless.

provisions.label: 3.1(a)(v)
provisions.text: In the event of any change in occupancy of any Residence, as a result of a transfer of title, a lease or sublease, a birth or death, change in marital status, vacancy, change in location of permanent residence, or otherwise, the Owner of the Residence shall immediately notify the Board in writing and provide to the Board the names and ages of all current occupants of the Residence and such other information as the Board may reasonably require to verify the age of each occupant. In the event that an Owner fails to notify the Board and provide all required information within 10 days after a change in occupancy occurs, the Association may levy monetary fines against the Owner and the Unit for each day after the change in occupancy occurs until the Association receives the required notice and information, regardless of whether the occupants continue to meet the requirements of this Article, in addition to all other remedies available to the Association under this Declaration and Washington law.

provisions.label: 3.1(a)(vi)
provisions.heading: Monitoring Compliance; Appointment of Attorney-in-Fact
provisions.text: The Association shall be responsible for maintaining age records on all occupants of Residences. The Board shall adopt policies, procedures, and rules to monitor and maintain compliance with this Section and the Act, including policies regarding visitors, updating of age records, the granting of exemptions to compliance, and enforcement. The Association shall periodically distribute such policies, procedures, and rules to the Owners and make copies available to Owners, their tenants and Mortgagees upon reasonable request. Each Owner and resident, as and when requested to do so by the Board, shall furnish the Board with the names and ages of all occupants of the Residence and such affidavits and other documents as the Board may request to verify the age of such occupants.

provisions.label: 3.1(a)(vi)/p2
provisions.text: The Association may enforce this Section 3.1(a) in any legal or equitable manner available, as the Board deems appropriate, including, without limitation, conducting a census of the occupants of Residences, requiring that copies of birth certificates or other proof of age for each occupant be provided to the Board on a periodic basis, and taking action to evict the occupants of any Residence which does not comply with the requirements and restrictions of this Section. Each Owner shall fully and truthfully respond to any Association request for information regarding the occupancy of Residences on his or her Unit which, in the Board's judgment, is reasonably necessary to monitor compliance with this Section. Each Owner hereby appoints the Association as its attorney-in-fact for the purpose of taking legal or equitable action to dispossess, evict, or otherwise remove the occupants of any Residence on his or her Unit as necessary to enforce compliance with this Section.

provisions.label: 3.1(a)(vi)/p3
provisions.text: Each Owner shall be responsible for ensuring compliance of its Unit with the requirements and restrictions of this Section, and the Association rules adopted hereunder, by itself and by its tenants and other occupants of its Unit. Each Owner, by acceptance of title to a Unit, agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold Declarant, its Affiliates, and the Association harmless from any and all claims, losses, damages, and causes of action which may arise from failure of such Owner's Unit to so comply.

provisions.label: 3.1(a)/p2
provisions.text: Anything herein contained to the contrary notwithstanding, Declarant, so long as the Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant owns any property set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B," and thereafter, the Board, may amend the provisions of this Section 3.1(a) to the extent that it deems it necessary or appropriate, without the approval of the Owners, in order to comply with the exemption requirements under the Act or any regulations now or hereafter issued therefore, as they may be amended from time to time, with respect to "housing for older persons." Any such amendments are subject to prior approval by King County or its successor jurisdiction.

provisions.label: 3.1(b)
provisions.heading: Residential and Related Uses
provisions.intro: An Owner or another resident of the Unit may conduct business activities on such Unit only if the business activity:
provisions.text: Units shall be used primarily for residential and related purposes.

provisions.label: 3.1(b)(i)
provisions.text: Is not apparent or detectable by sight, sound, or smell from outside of a permitted structure;

provisions.label: 3.1(b)(ii)
provisions.text: complies with applicable zoning requirements and is otherwise allowed under the UPD Permit;

provisions.label: 3.1(b)(iii)
provisions.text: does not involve regular visitation of the Unit by clients, customers, suppliers or other business invitees, or door-to-door solicitation within the Residential Community; and

provisions.label: 3.1(b)(iv)
provisions.text: is consistent with the residential character of the Residential Community and does not constitute a nuisance, or a hazardous or offensive use, or threaten the security or safety of others, as determined in the Board's sole discretion.

provisions.label: 3.1(b)/p2
provisions.text: "Business" shall have its ordinary, generally accepted meaning and shall include, without limitation, any occupation, work, or activity undertaken on an ongoing basis which involves providing goods or services to Persons other than the family of the producer and for which the producer receives a fee, compensation, or other form of consideration, regardless of whether (i) such activity is engaged in full or part time; (ii) such activity is intended to or does generate a profit; or (iii) a license is required.

provisions.label: 3.1(b)/p3
provisions.text: This Section shall not apply to restrict Declarant's or its Affiliates' activities, nor shall it restrict the activities of Persons Declarant approves with respect to the development and sale of property within Trilogy at Redmond Ridge. This Section also shall not apply to the operation of Private Amenities, or to Association or TRRS activities related to the provision of services or to operating and maintaining the Residential Community, including any recreational and other amenities which the Association owns or operates.

provisions.label: 3.1(b)/p4
provisions.text: Leasing a Residence for residential purposes is not a "business" within the meaning of this Subsection.

noRule.note: Leasing is never a business-activity subject, so the business rules never reach it; leasing has its own rules in 3.1(c).

provisions.label: 3.1(c)
provisions.heading: Leasing
provisions.text: For purposes of this Declaration, "leasing" is the regular, exclusive occupancy of a dwelling by any Person other than the Owner, for which the Owner receives any consideration or benefit, including a fee, service, or gratuity. The principal dwelling on the Unit may be leased only in its entirety (e.g., separate rooms within the same dwelling may not be separately leased); provided, a detached "in-law suite" or "guest house" may be independently leased, provided the requirements for accessory dwelling units set forth in the UPD Permit are met.

provisions.label: 3.1(c)/p2
provisions.text: All leases shall be in writing and shall have a term of at least six months, except that either or both of these requirements may be waived (i) with the Board's prior written consent, or (ii) as Declarant authorizes in a Supplemental Declaration for Units located within certain Neighborhoods. All leases must require that tenants and all occupants of the leased Unit are bound by and obligated to comply with the Governing Documents, provided, the Governing Documents shall apply regardless of whether such a provision is specifically set forth in the lease. The restrictions on lease terms set forth in this paragraph shall not apply to Units Declarant or its Affiliates own.

provisions.label: 3.1(c)/p3
provisions.text: Within ten days of a lease being signed, an Owner shall notify the Board or the Association's managing agent of the lease and provide any additional information the Board may reasonably require. The Owner must give the tenant copies of the Governing Documents. In addition to this sub-section (c), the Association may adopt Use Restrictions, and the Board may adopt reasonable Board Rules and Regulations, governing leasing and subleasing.

provisions.label: 3.1(d)
provisions.heading: Occupants Bound
provisions.text: Every Owner shall cause anyone occupying or visiting his or her Unit to comply with the Governing Documents and shall be responsible for all violations and losses they cause to the Area of Common Responsibility, notwithstanding the fact that such Persons also are responsible for complying and may be sanctioned for any violation.

provisions.label: 3.1(e)
provisions.heading: Subdivision of a Unit and Time-Sharing
provisions.text: Units may not be subdivided or their boundary lines changed except with the Board's prior written approval, provided, Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant may subdivide, change the boundary line of, and replat any Unit they own without the consent of the Board or any other Person. In addition, for so long as Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant owns any portion of the Residential Community, Declarant or its Affiliates may convert Units into Common Area without the consent of the Board or any other Person.

provisions.label: 3.1(e)/p2
provisions.text: The use of any Unit for operation of a timesharing, fraction-sharing, or similar program whereby the right to exclusive use of the Unit rotates among participants in the program on a fixed or floating time schedule over a period of years is prohibited, except that Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant may operate such a program or permit other developers to operate such a program without the consent of the Board or any other Person. Any Unit which is divided into timeshare interests shall be deemed a single Unit (i.e., separate timeshare interests shall not constitute separate Units) for voting and assessment purposes under the Governing Documents.

provisions.heading: Framework for Regulation
provisions.text: As part of the general plan of development for Trilogy at Redmond Ridge, the Governing Documents establish a framework of covenants, easements, and restrictions, which includes the initial Use Restrictions set forth in Exhibit "C." Within that framework, the Board and the Members must be able to respond to unforeseen problems and changes affecting the Residential Community. This Article establishes procedures for modifying and expanding the Use Restrictions to respond to such changes.

noRule.note: Purpose of the procedures for changing the Use Restrictions.

provisions.heading: Authority to Enact Use Restrictions
provisions.text: 3.3 Authority to Enact Use Restrictions

noRule.note: Only the section heading; its text is in its lettered items.

provisions.label: 3.3(a)
provisions.text: Subject to the terms of the UPD Permit, this Article, and the Board's duty to exercise business judgment and reasonableness on behalf of the Association and its Members, the Board may change (i.e., modify, cancel, limit, create exceptions to, or add to) the Use Restrictions. The Board shall conspicuously publish notice concerning any such proposed change at least five business days prior to the Board meeting at which such action is to be considered. Members shall have a reasonable opportunity to be heard at a Board meeting prior to such action being taken.

provisions.label: 3.3(a)/p2
provisions.text: A change to the Use Restrictions under this Section 3.3(a) shall become effective, after compliance with the distribution requirements set forth in Section 3.3(c) below, provided, after termination of the Class "B" Control Period, and prior to the effective date under Section 3.3(c), any change may be disapproved at a meeting by Members representing more than 50% of the Association's Class "A" votes and by the Class "B" Member, if any. The Board shall have no obligation to call a meeting of the Members to consider disapproval except upon receipt of a petition as required for special meetings in the By-Laws. Upon receipt of such petition prior to the effective date of any Board action under this Section 3.3(a), the proposed action shall not become effective until after such meeting is held, and then subject to the outcome of such meeting.

provisions.label: 3.3(b)
provisions.text: Alternatively, Members representing more than 50% of the Association's Class "A" votes may vote to adopt Use Restrictions which modify, cancel, limit, create exceptions to, or expand the Use Restrictions then in effect. Such action shall require a meeting called for such purpose and shall require the approval of the Class "B" Member, if any.

provisions.label: 3.3(c)
provisions.text: Prior to any action taken under this Section 3.3 becoming effective, the Board shall send a copy of the new or changed Use Restrictions to each Owner. The effective date shall be at least 30 days following distribution to Owners. The Association shall provide, without cost, a copy of the Use Restrictions then in effect to any requesting Member or Mortgagee.

provisions.label: 3.3(d)
provisions.text: Nothing in this Section 3.3 shall authorize the Board or the Members to modify, repeal, or expand the Residential Design Guidelines or other provisions of this Declaration. In the event of a conflict between the Residential Design Guidelines and the Use Restrictions, the Residential Design Guidelines shall control. In the event of a conflict between the Use Restrictions and any provision within this Declaration (exclusive of the Use Restrictions), the Declaration provision shall control.

provisions.label: 3.3(e)
provisions.text: The procedures required under this Section 3.3 shall not apply to the enactment and enforcement of reasonable Board Rules and Regulations (i.e., administrative issues, regulations governing the use of the Common Area, etc.) unless the Board chooses in its discretion to submit to such procedures. Examples of such Board Rules and Regulations shall include, but not be limited to, hours of operation of a recreational facility, use of private streets, and the method of allocating or reserving use of a facility (if permitted) by particular individuals at particular times. The Board shall exercise business judgment in the enactment, amendment, and enforcement of Board Rules and Regulations.

provisions.heading: Owners' Acknowledgment and Notice to Purchasers
provisions.text: Each Owner, by accepting a deed, acknowledges and agrees that the use, enjoyment, and marketability of his or her Unit is limited and affected by the Use Restrictions and Board Rules and Regulations, which may change from time to time. All Unit purchasers are on notice that the Board or the Association membership may have adopted changes to the Use Restrictions and the Board Rules and Regulations and that such changes may not be set forth in a Recorded document. Copies of the current Use Restrictions and Board Rules and Regulations may be obtained from the Association.

noRule.note: Owners' acknowledgment and notice that the Use Restrictions and Board Rules may change without a Recorded document.

provisions.heading: Protection of Owners and Others
provisions.intro: Except as may be set forth in this Declaration (either initially or by amendment) or in the initial Use Restrictions set forth in Exhibit "C," the Association's actions with respect to Use Restrictions and Board Rules and Regulations must comply with the following:

provisions.label: 3.5(a)
provisions.heading: Similar Treatment
provisions.text: Similarly situated Owners shall be treated similarly; provided, the Use Restrictions and Board Rules and Regulations may vary by Neighborhood.

provisions.label: 3.5(b)
provisions.heading: Displays
provisions.text: The Association may not abridge Owners' rights to display religious and holiday signs, symbols, and decorations on their Units of the kinds normally displayed in single-family residential neighborhoods, except that the Association may adopt time, place, and manner restrictions with respect to such displays.

provisions.label: 3.5(b)/p2
provisions.text: The Association shall not regulate the content of political signs; however, it may regulate the time, place, and manner of posting such signs (including design criteria).

provisions.label: 3.5(b)/p3
provisions.text: Notwithstanding the above, King County ordinances may apply to limit Owners' rights with respect to any such displays.

noRule.note: King County ordinances may limit display rights; ordinances rank above the Declaration in the precedence clause.

provisions.label: 3.5(c)
provisions.heading: Household Composition
provisions.text: The Association shall not interfere with any Owner's freedom to determine the composition of his/her household, except as set forth in Section 3.1(a) of this Declaration, and except that the Association may require that all occupants be members of a single housekeeping unit and it may impose and enforce reasonable occupancy limits based upon Unit size, fair use of the Common Area, and compliance with King County ordinances.

provisions.label: 3.5(d)
provisions.heading: Activities Within Dwellings
provisions.text: The Association shall not interfere with activities carried on within a dwelling, except it may prohibit activities not normally associated with residential property, and it may restrict or prohibit activities that create monetary costs for the Association or other Owners, that create a danger to anyone's health or safety, that generate excessive noise or traffic, that create unsightly conditions visible outside the dwelling, or that are an unreasonable source of annoyance.

provisions.label: 3.5(e)
provisions.heading: Alienation
provisions.text: The Association shall not prohibit leasing (except for the purpose of complying with the provisions of Section 3.1(a) of this Declaration) or transfer of any Unit, or require the Association's or the Board's consent prior to leasing or transferring a Unit. The Association may require that Owners use Association-approved lease forms (or include specific lease terms) and may impose a reasonable review or administrative fee on the lease or transfer of any Unit. In addition, among other things, Section 3.1(c) imposes a minimum lease term.

provisions.label: 3.5(f)
provisions.heading: Abridging Rights
provisions.text: The Association may not require an Owner to dispose of personal property that was in or on a Unit in compliance with previous rules. This exemption shall apply only during the period of such Owner's ownership of the Unit and shall not apply to subsequent Owners who take title to the Unit after adoption of the rule.

provisions.label: 3.5(g)
provisions.heading: Reasonable Rights To Develop
provisions.text: No Use Restriction, Board Rule or Regulation, or action by the Association or Board shall unreasonably impede Declarant's or its Affiliates' right to develop the Residential Community nor the rights of TRRS to provide services to the Residential Community.

provisions.label: 3.5(h)
provisions.heading: Interference with Private Amenities
provisions.text: The Association may not interfere with the use, ownership, appearance, or operation of any Private Amenity.

provisions.label: 3.5(i)
provisions.heading: Compliance With the UPD Permit
provisions.text: No Use Restriction, Board Rule or Regulation, or action by the Association or Board shall be in conflict with the requirements and conditions set forth in the UPD Permit.

provisions.label: 3.5/p2
provisions.text: The limitations in Subsections (a) through (f) of this Section shall only limit the authority exercised under Section 3.3; they shall not apply to amendments to this Declaration adopted in accordance with Article 20.

provisions.label: exhibit-c
provisions.heading: Initial Use Restrictions
provisions.text: EXHIBIT "C" Initial Use Restrictions

noRule.note: Only the exhibit heading.

provisions.label: p1
provisions.text: The purpose of the Use Restrictions and the Residential Design Guidelines is not to anticipate all acceptable or unacceptable behavior in advance and eliminate all improvements or activities which fall outside of "the norm." In fact, it is expressly intended that the Reviewer under Article 4, and the Board, as appropriate, have discretion to approve or disapprove items, to exercise judgment in interpreting standards, and to enforce or not enforce technical violations of the Governing Documents, based upon aesthetic or other considerations consistent with the established guidelines. As such, while something may be approved or permitted for one Unit under one set of circumstances, the same thing may be disapproved for another Unit under a different set of circumstances. The exercise of discretion in approvals or enforcement shall not be construed as a waiver of approval or enforcement rights, nor shall it estop the Board from taking enforcement action in any appropriate circumstances.

noRule.note: Purpose of the Use Restrictions, the Reviewer's and Board's discretion, and non-waiver; the discretion that changes outcomes is encoded from (a).

provisions.label: p2
provisions.text: Subject to the above, the following restrictions shall apply to all of the Residential Community until such time as they are amended, modified, repealed, or limited pursuant to Article 3 of the Declaration.

noRule.note: The restrictions govern the whole community until changed under Article 3; that's the document's governs: null and its editions.

provisions.label: a
provisions.heading: Restricted Activities
provisions.intro: The following activities are prohibited within the Residential Community unless expressly authorized by, and then subject to Board Rules and Regulations and such conditions as may be imposed by, the Board:

provisions.label: a(i)
provisions.text: Parking of commercial vehicles (even if owned by the Owner or occupant of the Unit), recreational vehicles, mobile homes, boats or other watercraft, or other oversized vehicles, stored vehicles, or inoperable vehicles in places other than enclosed garages or in areas the Board designates as vehicle storage areas within Trilogy at Redmond Ridge, provided that such vehicles may be temporarily parked elsewhere between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. for purposes of loading and unloading;

provisions.label: a(ii)
provisions.text: Storing, repairing, or maintaining vehicles or equipment of any type on any part of a Unit except in an enclosed garage;

provisions.label: a(iii)
provisions.text: Capturing, trapping, injuring, or killing of wildlife, except in circumstances posing an imminent threat to personal safety or except as required or permitted by any applicable governmental authority;

provisions.label: a(iv)
provisions.text: Chasing, injuring, or killing of wildlife by pets of Owners or occupants of Units within the Residential Community;

provisions.label: a(v)
provisions.text: Raising, breeding, or keeping of animals, livestock, or poultry of any kind, except that a reasonable number of dogs, cats, or other usual and common household pets may be permitted in a Unit. However, those pets which are permitted to roam free, or, in the sole discretion of the Board, make objectionable noise, endanger the health or safety of, or constitute a nuisance or inconvenience to others shall be removed upon the Board's request. If the pet owner fails to honor such request, the Board may remove the pet. Pets shall be kept on a leash or otherwise confined in a manner acceptable to the Board whenever outside the dwelling and pet owners shall properly dispose of any waste their animals produce on the Common Area;

provisions.label: a(vi)
provisions.text: Obstruction or rechanneling of drainage flows after location and installation of drainage swales, storm sewers, or storm drains, except that Declarant and the Association shall have such right; provided, the exercise of such right shall not materially diminish the value of or unreasonably interfere with the use of any Unit without the Owner's consent; provided, further, the exercise of such right can be performed only in a manner consistent with the UPD Permit and with prior approval by King County;

provisions.label: a(vii)
provisions.text: Conversion of any carport, garage, attic, or other unfinished space, other than a basement, to finished space for use as an apartment or other integral part of the living area on any Unit. Any request to enclose a garage must include plans for a replacement garage on the Unit. If approval of a garage enclosure is granted by the Reviewer in accordance with Article 4, such approval may be conditional on the construction of a replacement garage;

provisions.label: a(viii)
provisions.text: Any activities, including implementation of any surface water management plan by non-governmental entities, which would have an adverse impact on the quality or quantity of existing water supplies. Adverse impacts shall include, but shall not be limited to, increases or decreases in water flow rates, levels, or volumes, increases or decreases in sedimentation, or diminishment of water quality below existing standards;

provisions.label: a(ix)
provisions.text: Any garage sale, moving sale, rummage sale, or similar activity;

provisions.label: a(x)
provisions.text: Any construction, erection, placement, or modification of any thing, permanently or temporarily, on the outside portions of the Unit, whether such portion is improved or unimproved, except in strict compliance with the provisions of Article 4 of the Declaration and the Residential Design Guidelines. This shall include, without limitation, signs, swing sets and other sports and play equipment, clotheslines, fountains, birdbaths and lawn statuary; flag poles and ornamentation; garbage cans; woodpiles, above-ground swimming pools, hot tubs or spas; docks, piers and similar structures; and hedges, walls, dog runs, animal pens, fences of any kind, and satellite dishes and antennas, except that:

provisions.label: a(x)(1)
provisions.text: an antenna designed to receive direct broadcast satellite services, including direct-to-home satellite services, that is one meter or less in diameter;

provisions.label: a(x)(2)
provisions.text: an antenna designed to receive video programming services via multipoint distribution services, including multichannel multipoint distribution services, instructional television fixed services, and local multipoint distribution services, that is one meter or less in diameter or diagonal measurement; and

provisions.label: a(x)(3)
provisions.text: an antenna that is designed to receive television broadcast signals,

provisions.label: a(x)/p2
provisions.text: (collectively, "Permitted Antennas") shall be permitted on Units, subject to such reasonable requirements as to location and screening as may be set forth in the Residential Design Guidelines, consistent with applicable law, in order to minimize obtrusiveness as viewed from streets and adjacent property. Declarant and/or the Association shall have the right, without obligation, to erect an aerial, satellite dish, or other apparatus for a master antenna, cable, or other communication system for the benefit of all or a portion of the Residential Community, should any master system or systems be utilized by the Association and require such exterior apparatus;

provisions.label: a(xi)
provisions.text: Storage of items outside of the dwelling or enclosed garage, including portable play equipment and temporary storage bins; and

provisions.label: a(xii)
provisions.text: Gardens, planters, and flower beds are permitted if neatly maintained in a manner consistent with the Community-Wide Standard and in compliance with the UPD Permit and the Residential Design Guidelines.

provisions.label: b
provisions.heading: Prohibited Conditions
provisions.intro: The following shall be prohibited within the Residential Community:

provisions.label: b(i)
provisions.text: Plants, animals, devices, or other things of any sort whose activities or existence in any way is noxious, dangerous, unsightly, unpleasant, or of a nature as may diminish or destroy the enjoyment of the Residential Community;

provisions.label: b(ii)
provisions.text: Structures, equipment, or other items on the exterior portions of a Unit which have become rusty, dilapidated, or otherwise fallen into disrepair;

provisions.label: b(iii)
provisions.text: Sprinkler or irrigation systems or wells of any type which draw upon water from lakes, creeks, streams, rivers, ponds, wetlands, canals, or other ground or surface waters within the Residential Community, except that Declarant and its designees shall have the exclusive right to draw water from such sources and to reduce the level of such bodies of water, if and to the extent allowed by the UPD Permit;

provisions.label: b(iv)
provisions.text: Open-air burning or the use of wood stoves or "zero-clearance" fireplaces in any residence or building, provided, outdoor cooking facilities, such as barbecues, are permissible subject to King County and other state, regional and local laws; and

provisions.label: b(v)
provisions.text: Any activity by an Owner or occupant in violation of the UPD Permit restrictions governing sensitive areas and perimeter buffers, or otherwise removing, improving, or distributing vegetation, fauna, or other activities in such areas.

provisions.label: article-4
provisions.heading: Architecture and Landscaping
provisions.text: Article 4 Architecture and Landscaping

provisions.heading: General

noRule.note: Its text is in its counted paragraphs.

provisions.text: 4.1 General

provisions.label: 4.1/p1
provisions.text: No structure or thing shall be placed, erected, or installed upon any Unit within the Residential Community and no improvements or other work (including staking, clearing, excavation, grading and other site work, exterior alterations of existing improvements, or planting or removal of landscaping) shall take place within the Residential Community, except in compliance with, and pursuant to approval under, this Article and the Residential Design Guidelines. (Activities within the scope of this Article are referred to as "Work.")

provisions.label: 4.1/p2
provisions.text: No approval shall be required to repaint the exterior of a structure in accordance with an already approved color scheme. Any Owner may remodel, paint, or redecorate the interior of his or her Unit without approval. However, modifications to the interior of screened porches, patios, and similar portions of a Unit visible from outside the structure and modifications to enclose garages as living space shall be subject to approval.

provisions.label: 4.1/p3

noRule.note: Approval doesn't replace UPD Permit or King County approvals; the portal doesn't evaluate governmental permits.

provisions.text: Approval under this Article and the Residential Design Guidelines is not a substitute for any approvals or reviews required under the UPD Permit or otherwise by King County or any other municipality or governmental agency or entity having jurisdiction over architectural or construction matters.

provisions.label: 4.1/p4
provisions.text: This Article shall not apply to Declarant's activities nor shall this Article apply to activities of any [illegible] of Declarant, governmental entity or public utility.

provisions.heading: Design Review

noRule.note: Its text is in its lettered points.

provisions.text: 4.2 Design Review.

provisions.label: 4.2(a)
provisions.heading: By Declarant
provisions.text: (a) By Declarant. Declarant shall have exclusive authority to administer and enforce architectural controls and to review and act upon all applications for architectural and other improvements within the Residential Community. Declarant's rights under this Article shall continue until 100% of the Units permitted under the Master Plan for the Residential Community, or such lower number of Units as Declarant may elect, have been conveyed to Class "A" Members other than Declarant, any Affiliate of Declarant, or a Builder, and have been improved with a dwelling for which a certificate of occupancy has been issued. Declarant may designate one or more Persons to act on its behalf in reviewing any application. In reviewing and acting upon any request for approval, Declarant or its designee acts solely in Declarant's interest and owes no duty to any other Person.

provisions.label: 4.2(a)/p2
provisions.text: Declarant may from time to time, delegate or assign all or any portion of its rights under this Article to any other Person or committee, including a design review committee which the Board appoints ("DRC"). Any such delegation shall be in writing, shall specify the delegated responsibilities, and shall be subject to (i) Declarant's right to revoke such delegation at any time and reassume its prior jurisdiction, and (ii) Declarant's right to veto any decision which it determines, in its discretion, to be inappropriate or inadvisable for any reason. So long as Declarant has any rights under this Article, the jurisdiction of other entities shall be limited to such matters as Declarant specifically delegates.

provisions.label: 4.2(b)
provisions.heading: Design Review Committee
provisions.text: (b) Design Review Committee. Upon delegation by Declarant or upon expiration or termination of Declarant's rights under this Article, the Association, acting through the DRC, shall assume jurisdiction over architectural matters within the Residential Community. The DRC, when appointed, shall consist of at least three, but not more than seven, persons who shall serve and may be removed and replaced in the Board's discretion. The members of the DRC need not be Members of the Association or representatives of Members, and may, but need not, include architects, engineers, or similar professionals, who may be compensated in such manner and amount, if any, as the Board may establish.

provisions.label: 4.2(b)/p2

noRule.note: Subcommittees of the DRC are the DRC; the committee party covers them.

provisions.text: The DRC may be broken into or may form subcommittees to preside over particular areas of review (i.e., a new construction subcommittee and a modifications subcommittee). Any reference herein to the DRC should be deemed to include a reference to any such subcommittee.

provisions.label: 4.2(b)/p3
provisions.text: Unless and until such time as Declarant delegates all or a portion of its reserved rights to the DRC or Declarant's rights under this Article terminate, the Association shall have no jurisdiction over architectural matters.

provisions.label: 4.2(c)
provisions.heading: Reviewer
provisions.text: (c) Reviewer. For purposes of this Article, the entity having jurisdiction in a particular case shall be referred to as the "Reviewer."

provisions.label: 4.2(d)
provisions.heading: Fees, Assistance
provisions.text: (d) Fees, Assistance. The Reviewer may establish and charge reasonable fees for review of applications hereunder and may require such fees to be paid in full prior to review of any application. Such fees may include the reasonable costs incurred in having any application reviewed by architects, engineers, or other professionals. Declarant and the Association may employ architects, engineers, or other persons as deemed necessary to perform the review. The Board may include the compensation of such persons in the Association's annual operating budget as a Common Expense.

provisions.heading: Guidelines and Procedures

noRule.note: Its text is in its lettered points.

provisions.text: 4.3 Guidelines and Procedures

provisions.label: 4.3(a)
provisions.heading: Residential Design Guidelines
provisions.text: (a) Residential Design Guidelines. Declarant may prepare the initial Residential Design Guidelines, which may contain general provisions applicable to all of the Residential Community as well as specific provisions which vary from Neighborhood to Neighborhood. The Residential Design Guidelines are not the exclusive basis for decisions of the Reviewer and compliance with the Residential Design Guidelines does not guarantee approval of any application.

provisions.label: 4.3(a)/p2
provisions.text: Declarant shall have sole and full authority to amend the Residential Design Guidelines as long as Declarant, any Affiliate of Declarant, or any Builder owns any property described in Exhibits "A" or "B." Declarant's right to amend shall continue even if its reviewing authority is delegated to the DRC, unless Declarant also delegates its amendment authority to the DRC. Upon termination or delegation of Declarant's right to amend, the DRC may amend the Residential Design Guidelines with the Board's consent.

provisions.label: 4.3(a)/p3
provisions.text: Amendments to the Residential Design Guidelines shall be prospective only. They shall not require modifications to or removal of structures previously approved once the approved construction or modification has begun. However, any new work on such structures must comply with the Residential Design Guidelines as amended. Subject to the Community-Wide Standard, there is no limit to the scope of amendments to the Residential Design Guidelines, and such amendments may remove requirements previously imposed or otherwise make the Residential Design Guidelines less restrictive. Notwithstanding the above, the Residential Design Guidelines, and all amendments, are subject to and must be in compliance with the UPD Permit.

provisions.label: 4.3(a)/p4
provisions.text: The Reviewer shall make the Residential Design Guidelines available to Owners and Builders who seek to engage in development or construction within the Residential Community. In Declarant's discretion, such Residential Design Guidelines may be Recorded, in which event the Recorded version, as it may unilaterally be amended from time to time, shall control in the event of any dispute as to which version of the Residential Design Guidelines was in effect at any particular time.

provisions.label: 4.3(b)
provisions.heading: Procedures
provisions.text: (b) Procedures. No Work shall commence on any portion of the Community until an application for approval has been submitted to and approved by the Reviewer. Such application shall include plans and specifications ("Plans") showing site layout, structural design, exterior elevations, exterior materials and colors, landscaping, drainage, exterior lighting, irrigation, and other features of proposed construction, as applicable. The Residential Design Guidelines and the Reviewer may require the submission of such additional information as may be reasonably necessary to consider any application.

provisions.label: 4.3(b)/p2
provisions.text: In reviewing each submission, the Reviewer may consider any factors it deems relevant, including, without limitation, harmony of external design with surrounding structures and environment. Decisions may be based on purely aesthetic considerations. Each Owner acknowledges that determinations as to such matters are purely subjective and opinions may vary as to the desirability and/or attractiveness of particular improvements.

provisions.label: 4.3(b)/p3
provisions.text: The Reviewer shall respond in writing to the applicant at the address specified in the application. The response may (i) approve the application, with or without conditions, (ii) approve a portion of the application and disapprove other portions, or (iii) disapprove the application. The Reviewer may, but shall not be obligated to, specify the reasons for any objections and/or offer suggestions for curing any objections.

provisions.label: 4.3(b)/p4
provisions.text: No approval shall be inconsistent with the Residential Design Guidelines unless a variance is granted pursuant to Section 4.5.

provisions.label: 4.3(b)/p5
provisions.text: Notice shall be deemed to have been given at the time the envelope containing the response is deposited with the U.S. Postal Service. Personal delivery of such written notice shall, however, be sufficient and shall be deemed to have been given at the time of delivery to the applicant.

provisions.label: 4.3(b)/p6
provisions.text: Until expiration of Declarant's rights under this Article, the DRC shall notify Declarant in writing within three business days after the DRC has approved any application relating to proposed Work. The notice shall be accompanied by a copy of the application and any additional information which Declarant may require. Declarant shall have 10 days after receipt of such notice to veto any such action, in its sole discretion, by written notice to the DRC and the applicant.

provisions.label: 4.3(b)/p7
provisions.text: If construction does not commence on a project for which Plans have been approved within one year after the date of approval, such approval shall be deemed withdrawn and it shall be necessary for the Owner to reapply for approval before commencing the proposed Work. Once construction is commenced, it shall be diligently pursued to completion. All Work shall be completed within one year of commencement unless otherwise specified in the notice of approval or unless the Reviewer grants an extension in writing, which it shall not be obligated to do. If approved Work is not completed within the required time, it shall be considered nonconforming and shall be subject to enforcement action by the Association, Declarant or any aggrieved Owner.

provisions.label: 4.3(b)/p8
provisions.text: Unless otherwise installed by Declarant or a Builder, the initial home purchaser shall install landscaping on a Unit, pursuant to an approved landscaping plan, within 90 days of the date that title to such Unit is transferred to such home purchaser.

provisions.label: 4.3(b)/p9
provisions.text: Declarant or the Board, with Declarant's consent, by resolution, may exempt certain activities from the application and approval requirements of this Article, provided such activities are undertaken in strict compliance with the requirements of such resolution. For example, Builders may submit and receive pre-approval of landscaping or other plans for general application. Such pre-approved plans shall not require resubmission prior to use on a particular Unit.

provisions.heading: No Waiver of Future Approvals

noRule.note: Approving one application doesn't bind the Reviewer on similar ones; each request is evaluated on its own.

provisions.text:
4.4 No Waiver of Future Approvals.

Each Owner acknowledges that the persons reviewing applications under this Article will change from time to time and that opinions on aesthetic matters, as well as interpretation and application of the Residential Design Guidelines, may vary accordingly. In addition, each Owner acknowledges that it may not always be possible to identify objectionable features of proposed Work until the Work is completed, at which time it may be unreasonable to require changes to the improvements involved. However, the Reviewer may refuse to approve similar proposals in the future. Approval of applications or Plans shall not be deemed to constitute a waiver of the right to withhold approval as to any similar applications, Plans, or other matters subsequently or additionally submitted for approval.

provisions.heading: Variances
provisions.text:
4.5 Variances.

The Reviewer may authorize variances from compliance with any of its guidelines and procedures when circumstances such as topography, natural obstructions, hardship, or aesthetic or environmental considerations require, but only in accordance with duly adopted rules and regulations. Such variances may only be granted, however, when unique circumstances dictate and no variance shall (a) be effective unless in writing; (b) be contrary to this Declaration, or (c) estop the Reviewer from denying a variance in other circumstances. A variance requires Declarant's written consent for so long as Declarant, any Affiliate of Declarant, or any Builder owns any property described in Exhibits "A" or "B" and, thereafter, requires the Board's written consent.

provisions.heading: Limitation of Liability

noRule.note: Its text is in its counted paragraphs.

provisions.text: 4.6 Limitation of Liability

provisions.label: 4.6/p1

noRule.note: Review is aesthetic, creates no duty to anyone, and doesn't vouch for structural soundness, code compliance or comparable quality.

provisions.text: This Article establishes standards and procedures as a mechanism for maintaining and enhancing the overall aesthetics of the Residential Community. The standards and procedures do not create any duty to any Person. Review and approval of any application pursuant to this Article may be based on purely aesthetic considerations. The Reviewer is not responsible for the structural integrity or soundness of approved construction or modifications, for compliance with building codes and other governmental requirements, or for ensuring that every dwelling is of comparable quality, value, or size, of similar design, or aesthetically pleasing or otherwise acceptable to other Owners.

provisions.label: 4.6/p2
provisions.text: Declarant, its Affiliates, the Association, the Board, any committee, or member of any of the foregoing shall not be held liable for soil conditions, drainage or other general site work, any defects in plans revised or approved hereunder, or any injury, damages, or loss arising out of the manner or quality of approved construction on or modifications to any Unit. In all matters, the Board, the DRC, and any members thereof shall be defended and indemnified by the Association as provided in Section 7.6.

provisions.heading: Certificate of Approval
provisions.text:
4.7 Certificate of Approval

Any Owner may request that the Reviewer issue a certificate of approval certifying that there are no known violations on his or her Unit of this Article or the Residential Design Guidelines. The Association shall either grant or deny such request within 30 days after receipt of a written request and may charge a reasonable administrative fee for issuing such certificates.
