The Residential Community and its Governing Documents must be able to adapt to these changes while protecting the things that make Trilogy at Redmond Ridge unique.

noRule.note: Why the community and its documents must be able to change.

provisions.label: article-18
provisions.heading: Changes in Ownership of Units
provisions.text: Any Owner, other than Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant, desiring to sell or otherwise transfer title to his or her Unit shall give the Board at least seven days' prior written notice of the name and address of the purchaser or transferee, the date of such transfer of title, and such other information as the Board may reasonably require. Each transferee of a Unit shall, within seven days of taking title to a Unit, confirm that the information previously provided by the transferor is complete and accurate. The transferor shall continue to be jointly and severally responsible with the transferee for all obligations of the Owner of the Unit, including assessment obligations, until the date upon which such notice is received by the Board, notwithstanding the transfer of title. At the request of TRRS, the Association shall provide TRRS with the name, address, telephone number, and e-mail address (if available) of each new Owner and the forwarding address of any former Owner.

provisions.label: article-19
provisions.heading: Changes in Common Area
provisions.text: Article 19 Changes in Common Area

provisions.heading: Condemnation
provisions.text: 19.1 Condemnation

noRule.note: Its text is in its counted paragraphs.

provisions.label: 19.1/p1
provisions.text: If any part of the Common Area shall be taken (or conveyed in lieu of and under threat of condemnation by the Board acting on the written direction of Members representing at least 67% of the Association's Class "A" votes and of Declarant, so long as Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant owns property described in Exhibit "A" or "B") by any authority having the power of condemnation or eminent domain, each Owner shall be entitled to written notice of such taking or conveyance prior to disbursement of any condemnation award or proceeds from such conveyance. Such award or proceeds shall be payable to the Association to be disbursed as follows

provisions.label: 19.1/p2
provisions.text: If the taking or conveyance involves a portion of the Common Area on which improvements have been constructed, the Association shall restore or replace such improvements on the remaining land included in the Common Area to the extent available, unless within 60 days after such taking Declarant, so long as Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant owns any property described in Exhibit "A" or "B," and Members representing at least 67% of the Association's Class "A" votes shall otherwise agree. Any such construction shall be in accordance with plans approved by the Board. The provisions of Section 7.3(c) regarding funds for restoring improvements shall apply.

provisions.label: 19.1/p3
provisions.text: If the taking or conveyance does not involve any improvements on the Common Area, or if a decision is made not to repair or restore, or if net funds remain after any such restoration or replacement is complete, then such award or net funds shall be disbursed to the Association and used for such purposes as the Board shall determine.

noRule.note: Where an award not spent on restoration goes; its use is the Board's to determine.

provisions.heading: Partition
provisions.text: Except as permitted in this Declaration, the Common Area shall remain undivided, and no Person shall bring any action to partition of any portion of the Common Area without the written consent of all Owners and Mortgagees. This Section shall not prohibit the Board from acquiring and disposing of tangible personal property nor from acquiring and disposing of real property which may or may not be subject to this Declaration.

provisions.heading: Transfer or Dedication of Common Area
provisions.text: 19.3 Transfer or Dedication of Common Area

noRule.note: Its text is in its counted paragraphs.

provisions.label: 19.3/p1
provisions.text: Declarant or its Affiliates shall convey each Common Area to the Association within one (1) year after completion of the improvements thereon. The Common Area shall include, without limitation, a community park with a total of no less than 11.5 acres.

provisions.label: 19.3/p2
provisions.text: The Association may transfer, dedicate, or grant easements over portions of the Common Area to King County, Washington, or to any other local, state, or federal governmental or quasi-governmental entity without a vote of the Owners.

provisions.label: article-20
provisions.heading: Amendment of Declaration
provisions.text: Article 20 Amendment of Declaration

provisions.heading: By Declarant
provisions.text: 20.1 By Declarant

noRule.note: Its text is in its counted paragraphs.

provisions.label: 20.1/p1
provisions.text: In addition to specific amendment rights granted elsewhere in this Declaration, until conveyance of the first Unit to a Person other than an Affiliate of Declarant or a Builder, Declarant may unilaterally amend this Declaration for any purpose. Thereafter, Declarant may unilaterally amend this Declaration if such amendment is necessary (a) to bring any provision into compliance with any applicable governmental statute, rule, regulation, or judicial determination, (b) to enable any reputable title insurance company to issue title insurance coverage on the Units, (c) to enable any institutional or governmental lender, purchaser, insurer or guarantor of mortgage loans, including, for example, the Federal National Mortgage Association or Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation, to make, purchase, insure or guarantee mortgage loans on the Units, or (d) to satisfy the requirements of any local, state or federal governmental agency. However, any such amendment shall not adversely affect the title to any Unit unless the Owner shall consent in writing.

provisions.label: 20.1/p2
provisions.text: In addition, so long as Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant owns property described in Exhibit "A" or "B" for development as part of the Residential Community, Declarant may unilaterally amend this Declaration for any other purpose, provided the amendment has no material adverse effect upon any right of any Owner or unless such Owner shall consent in writing.

provisions.heading: By Members
provisions.text: 20.2 By Members

noRule.note: Its text is in its counted paragraphs.

provisions.label: 20.2/p1
provisions.text: Except as otherwise specifically provided above and elsewhere in this Declaration, this Declaration may be amended only by the affirmative vote or written consent, or any combination thereof, of Members representing 67% of the Association's Class "A" votes, including 67% of the Class "A" votes held by Members other than Declarant, and Declarant's consent, so long as Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant owns any property described in Exhibits "A" or "B." In addition, the approval requirements set forth in Article 16 shall be met, if applicable.

provisions.label: 20.2/p2
provisions.text: Notwithstanding the above, the percentage of votes necessary to amend a specific clause shall not be less than the prescribed percentage of affirmative votes required for action to be taken under that clause.

provisions.heading: Validity and Effective Date
provisions.text: 20.3 Validity and Effective Date

noRule.note: Its text is in its counted paragraphs.

provisions.label: 20.3/p1
provisions.text: No amendment may remove, revoke, or modify any right or privilege of Declarant without Declarant's written consent or any right or privilege of the Class "B" Member without the Class "B" Member's written consent (or the assignee of such right or privilege). No amendment may remove, revoke, or modify, or be in contravention of, any UPD Permit condition or requirement except as expressly approved by King County.

provisions.label: 20.3/p2
provisions.text: If an Owner consents to any amendment to this Declaration or the By-Laws, it will be conclusively presumed that such Owner has the authority to consent, and no contrary provision in any Mortgage or contract between the Owner and a third party will affect the validity of such amendment.

noRule.note: An Owner's consent to an amendment is presumed authorized.

provisions.label: 20.3/p3
provisions.text: Any amendment shall become effective upon Recording, unless a later effective date is specified in the amendment. Any procedural challenge to an amendment must be made within six months of its Recordation or such amendment shall be presumed to have been validly adopted. In no event shall a change of conditions or circumstances operate to amend any provisions of this Declaration.

provisions.heading: Exhibits
provisions.text: Exhibits "A" and "B" attached to this Declaration are incorporated by this reference and amendment of such exhibits shall be governed by this Article. Exhibit "C" is incorporated by reference and may be amended pursuant to Sections 20.1 and 20.2, or as provided in Article 3.

noRule.note: Exhibits A and B are amended like the Declaration; Exhibit C (the Use Restrictions, a document of its own) under 20.1, 20.2 or Article 3.

provisions.label: article-21
provisions.heading: Termination of Declaration
provisions.text: Subject to the terms and conditions of the UPD Permit, this Declaration may be terminated at any time if such termination is approved by the affirmative vote or written consent, or any combination thereof, of Owners representing 67% or more of the Association's Class "A" votes, including 67% of the Class "A" votes held by Members other than Declarant, and Declarant's consent, so long as Declarant or any Affiliate of Declarant owns any property described in Exhibits "A" or "B" and by the holders of first Mortgages on Units the Owners of which have 67% or more of the Class "A" votes in the Association. If the necessary votes and consents are obtained, the Board shall cause to be Recorded a Certificate of Termination, duly signed by the President or Vice President and attested by the Secretary or Assistant Secretary of the Association, with their signatures acknowledged. Thereupon this Declaration shall have no further force and effect, and the Association shall be dissolved pursuant to the terms set forth in its Articles.

provisions.label: execution
provisions.text: IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned Declarants have executed this Declaration the date and year first written above.

noRule.note: The execution clause; the signature blocks and notarial acknowledgments that follow are left out.

provisions.label: exhibit-a
provisions.heading: Land Initially Submitted

provisions.text: The Declaration established the DRC as the party responsible for carrying out the functions of the Reviewer regarding architectural matters. The DRC's role is to implement and interpret these RDGs as they pertain to design review applications.

Any change to the exterior of the Unit must comply with the RDGs. ALL EXTERIOR CHANGES REQUIRE DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE (DRC) APPROVAL UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED. DRC approval means that before work commences owners are required to submit a written DRC Application packet to obtain DRC approval. Compliance is required for guidelines noted as COMPLIANCE ONLY; however, DRC pre-approval is not required. Guidelines noted as PROHIBITED describes a condition that may not be violated, and deviation from which cannot be approved.

Owners are encouraged to consult with any neighbor who may be affected by the Work they intend to perform. The Reviewer reserves the right to require that proposed changes be disclosed to the affected neighbor(s). Some examples may include exterior lighting, fences, selected screens, lattices, detached structures, etc.

noRule.note: When the DRC meets to review applications; no requirement on anyone.

provisions.text: The DRC will conduct reviews of applications during regular meetings or at other times deemed appropriate.
In general, applications are reviewed within 30 days of receipt. Applications must be completed before they are reviewed.
When an application has been approved, the Association will notify the Owner in writing within 5 business days. Work shall not begin until the Owner has received approval from the Reviewer.

The notification will be delivered to the applicant by Management within five (5) business days of the DRC disapproval by hand, mail, electronic transmission, including facsimile or electronic mail. Management shall develop and shall include in the notification instructions, required dates and times, and forms, if any, needed for the appeal.

These RDGs are intended to be comprehensive. If, however, a desired change is not covered in the RDGs, or if there is doubt regarding how to comply with the Guidelines, per the Declaration the DRC retains approval jurisdiction over the proposed change.

provisions.label: 3.2/p1

provisions.text: Applications may be mailed or delivered to the following address: Trilogy at Redmond Ridge Residential Community Association Attn: Design Review Committee 23215 NE Greens Crossing Road Redmond, Washington 98053

noRule.note: The address applications may be emailed to.

provisions.text: Or may be emailed to: rca@hoamco.com
Permits, approvals, and requirements of King County and other jurisdictions outside of the Association are the sole responsibility of the Owner.

Reviewer approval of an owner proposal reflects a DRC determination of compliance of the proposed change to the current version of the Residential Design Guidelines and does not assure compliance with King County Code or any other applicable laws or regulations. The Reviewer has no authority to approve applications that, in the determination of the Reviewer, may violate other community Governing documents or applicable laws or regulations.

Applications that, in the determination of the Reviewer, appear to require a King County approved variance or permit will be eligible for architectural value review only. If accepted for architectural value, the application will be held for final approval pending receipt of King County approval or guidance that such approval is not required. Such architectural value acceptance does not constitute approval, and the project shall not begin until final approval is granted.

noRule.note: The guidelines may be stricter than King County's requirements.

provisions.text: The requirements set forth in the Declaration and these RDGs may be more restrictive than those of King County. Plans approved by the county may or may not be approved by the Reviewer.
The current version of the Design Review Committee Application Packet is available at the Association Office, or on the Design Review Committee webpage of the Community Website.

Owners submitting plans or drawings for approval to the Reviewer are responsible for the accuracy of all information contained in such plans or drawings, such as the location of all Unit boundaries, easements, and drainage as shown on the recorded plot plan or in any other instrument. It is recommended that the owner's submissions include photos.

noRule.note: The DRC and Association Staff are available to discuss proposed work.

provisions.text: The DRC and Association Staff are available to discuss proposed work prior to the submission of a design review application.
The Association reserves the right to conduct inspections of the work before, during and after construction. The Owner will be advised in writing prior to inspection.
"Impervious surfaces" are those that water cannot pass through or penetrate, including the residence, sidewalks, driveways, and patios.

The Reviewer will require impervious surface calculations to be submitted with each request for approval of improvements if such improvements will add to the impervious surface of a Unit. The Association Staff can help with this calculation.

provisions.label: 3.6/p1
provisions.text: Guidelines that include "shall" or shall not" require a variance before DRC approval can be granted. Since the Declaration states that a variance requires the Board's written consent, the Board is identified as the Reviewer for variances. Thus, if the DRC believes that a variance is justified, they may request it from the Board. If they do not believe a variance is appropriate, they retain the authority to deny the homeowner's request. The homeowner has the right to appeal a DRC decision to the Board of Directors.

provisions.label: 3.6/p2
provisions.text: The Reviewer reserves the right at its sole discretion to waive or vary any of the procedures or standards set forth herein, as provided in the Declaration. Approval by the Reviewer of any application hereunder shall not relieve the applicant of the obligation to comply fully with all governmental requirements applicable to the submittal, whether or not such requirements were brought to the attention of the reviewer.

provisions.heading: Fences, Gates, and Walls
provisions.text: A consultation with Association Staff is encouraged. Owners should be aware that King County may have specific code requirements for fences and walls. The Design Review Committee's approval does not assure compliance with King County Code. Replacement of fences and gates on a like for like basis requires DRC APPROVAL.

provisions.heading: Wood Fence Styles
provisions.text: Wood fences and gates shall consist of vertical boards, horizontal rails, and post caps. Horizontal boards are not permitted. Tall, consecutive sections of lattice shall not be used as a material or style for wood fencing. See Exhibits K, L and M for the specific approved wood fence styles. See RDG 5.5 for limitations on use of lattice on wood fences. See RDG 6.12 for guidelines on Landscape Screenings, Lattices, Trellises, Arbors, and Pergolas.

provisions.heading: Composite Fence Styles
provisions.text: Composite fence can be a combination of a polymer and non-polymer additives. The fence should be a K style. Other styles may be considered on a case-by-case basis.

provisions.heading: Metal Fence Styles
provisions.text: Metal fences and gates shall be 2-rail or 3-rail open metal view fencing with a maximum 4-inch picket spacing. A 3-rail open metal view fence with closer pickets in the bottom half of the fence is also allowed. No other alternatives will be considered. See Exhibit N for the specific approved metal fence styles. See RDG 5.7 for additional guidelines for fencing abutting the golf course.
Invisible underground fences are not permitted.
Horizontal style fences are not permitted

provisions.heading: Fence Materials
provisions.text: Only wood, composite, and open metal view fencing materials may be used for enclosing yards and creating privacy. No other materials, including vinyl, are permitted.

provisions.heading: Wood Fence Materials
provisions.text: Posts, stringers, or K-Banding shall be cedar or pressure-treated material.

provisions.text: All above grade portions of newly installed or replacement wood fences shall be stained. If only fence sections are replaced, they shall match the other sections for uniformity.

provisions.label: 5.4.1(ii)

provisions.heading: Re-staining Existing Wood Fences
provisions.text: When re-staining becomes necessary or required by the Association for maintenance, wood fences shall be re-stained using a solid or semi-transparent stain color approved by the Design Review Committee per RDG 5.4.1.ii, and 5.4.1.iii.

provisions.label: 5.4.2(iv)

provisions.heading: Metal Fence Color
provisions.text: All open metal view fences shall have a flat black powder coat finish.

provisions.heading: Wood and Composite Fence Height Limitations

provisions.label: 5.5.1(i)
provisions.text: The maximum height of fences constructed along or on Unit boundary lines or return fences from the side yard boundary to the house, is 72 inches (6 feet), and the minimum height of any fence constructed on a Unit is 40 inches.

provisions.label: 5.5.1(ii)
provisions.text: The lattice component on any fence shall not exceed 18 inches and the total height of the fence and lattice shall not exceed 90 inches (7½ feet). Only standard 2-inch diagonal or square lattice shall be approved. See Exhibit O for approved lattice styles.

provisions.label: 5.5.1(iii)
provisions.text: Arbors may be added to the top of fences, but the total height of fence, lattice and arbor combinations shall not exceed 96 inches (8 feet).

provisions.label: 5.5.2(i)
provisions.text: The height of metal fences constructed along or on a Unit boundary, including boundaries shared with the golf course, shall be between 4 feet and 6 feet. Variations from this height may be considered by the Reviewer for specific circumstances.

provisions.heading: Fences to Separate Units
provisions.text: Side and rear yard boundary fences may be placed: either on the boundary line (property line) that separates neighboring Units, or that separates a Unit and adjacent Common Area; or fences may be placed along the boundary line but totally within the boundary of a Unit.

provisions.label: 5.6.1(i)
provisions.heading: Boundary Line Fences
provisions.intro: Side and rear yard boundary fences placed on boundary lines that separate neighboring Units or fences that are attached to fences on other Units, require the approval of the neighboring Unit Owner in the DRC application packet stipulating the following:

provisions.label: 5.6.1(i)(a)
provisions.text: That the neighboring Unit Owner approves the placement and height of the fence and the materials to be used.

provisions.label: 5.6.1(i)(b)
provisions.text: That the neighboring Unit Owner understands and agrees that the fence constitutes a "party structure" as described in Declaration 13.1 and that the Owner will be responsible for maintenance and repair of a portion of the fence; and

provisions.label: 5.6.1(i)(c)
provisions.text: That the neighboring Unit Owner understands and agrees that the new fence will attach to an existing fence and may require joint maintenance responsibility among the Owners.

provisions.label: 5.6.1(ii)
provisions.heading: Non-Boundary Line Fences
provisions.intro: The DRC application packet from any Owner electing to build a Non-Boundary Line fence shall stipulate the following:
provisions.text: If a neighboring Unit Owner does not approve a fence being placed on the boundary line, then the Owner desiring the fence may construct it alongside the boundary lines of his/her Unit. This is a Non-Boundary Line Fence. As such, all elements must be entirely within his or her property.

provisions.label: 5.6.1(ii)(a)
provisions.text: That the fence is not a "party structure" as described in Declaration 13.1, and

provisions.label: 5.6.1(ii)(b)
provisions.text: That the Owner will be responsible for maintenance and repair of both sides of the fence.

provisions.heading: Fences within Front Yards
provisions.intro: Applications for front yard fences will be evaluated in terms of their compatibility with the overall appearance of the streetscape. The following parameters apply to fences constructed within front yards:

provisions.label: 5.6.2(i)
provisions.text: Placement of front yard fences should consider curved streetscapes and other aesthetic details and must not interfere with a driver's ability to see objects in the roadway. Refer to RDG 5.8.4 below.

provisions.label: 5.6.2(ii)
provisions.text: Front yard fences and fences constructed between side yard fences and the house should be placed no less than 5 feet behind the nearest front corner of the house. Windows and utilities may require other setbacks. Other considerations will be case-by-case.

provisions.label: 5.6.2(iii)
provisions.text: In cases of uniquely shaped Units, uncommon placement of the home and/ or driveway on the Unit, or unusual orientation of the home to adjacent homes, the Reviewer will determine the front, side, and rear yards of the Unit.

provisions.label: 5.6.2(iv)
provisions.text: Any areas maintained by the Association should remain accessible.
Any fence installed on or along a boundary line between a Unit and the golf course shall be an open metal view fence.

Side yard fences on Units that abut the golf course shall be open metal view fences from at least the point where the Unit abuts the golf course to a point 10 feet from the golf course boundary. A greater distance may be required by the Reviewer to accommodate view corridors.

provisions.heading: Boundary Line Locations
provisions.text: Verifying the location of Unit boundary lines prior to construction of fences is the sole responsibility of the Owner(s) constructing the fences.

provisions.heading: Easements
provisions.text: Unless otherwise prohibited on a recorded plat or other recorded document, an Owner may construct fences within utility easements. However, if removal or alteration of the fence is required by the utility company to exercise its rights under the easement, any such removal or alteration shall be at the sole expense of the Owner. Plot plans should be examined to see if there are driver or pedestrian sight line restrictions.

provisions.heading: Fencing Installed Near Sidewalks, Streets and/ or Driveways

noRule.note: The Reviewer's power to require plantings, horizontal deviations and a 3 to 5 foot set-back for fences near sidewalks, streets and driveways; each it imposes is a condition of approval.

provisions.text: The Reviewer may require that fencing installed near sidewalks and/ or driveways be located such that plantings may be required to soften the appearance of the fence. The reviewer may also require that new fencing along streets in the public view be built with horizontal deviations to prevent long, uninterrupted lengths of fencing and provide areas for plantings. A set-back of 3 to 5 feet may be required for visibility, aesthetics, or other safety reasons.

provisions.heading: Visibility
provisions.text: The Reviewer will consider the impact of a proposed fence to driver visibility. Adverse impact may require modification to the application before it can be approved or could result in denial of the application.

provisions.heading: Maintenance

noRule.note: Points to the Board Rules and Regulations, Article 4.2.3, for fence maintenance standards; that document isn't uploaded.

provisions.text: See the Trilogy Board Rules and Regulations, Article 4.2.3, for maintenance standards for fences.

provisions.heading: Disputes

noRule.note: Party structure disputes go through Declaration Article 14, as Declaration 13.1 already says; encoded there.

provisions.text: If a dispute between Owners arises with respect to the maintenance, repair or replacement of a party structure, the dispute shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of Declaration Article 14.

provisions.heading: Gates for Wood and Composite Fences
provisions.text: Gates on wood and composite fences shall coordinate with the adjacent fence types and be substantially the same height as the adjoining fence.
Wood or composite gates may have lattice or arbor on top, but the total height may not exceed 7.5 feet (90 inches) and with an arbor no more than 8 feet (96 inches). See Exhibits K, L and M.

provisions.heading: Gates for Metal Fences
provisions.text: Gates on metal view fences shall match the material and color of the metal fence and be substantially the same height as the adjoining fence. See Exhibit N.

provisions.heading: Gates for Courtyard Entries
provisions.text: Material for front courtyard entry gates shall be limited to Open View Metal fencing (Exhibit N). Other metal options will be reviewed on an individual basis. Size and style will be considered in relation to the style of the home.
Fences between Units and Common Areas shall not be altered by an Owner to install a gate.

A screen is defined as a fixed, flat, protective partition shielding an area from view, from heat or drafts, from light, or providing privacy and shall not be on a property line. A screen may be used as an architectural feature. Homeowners may erect a wide variety of screening devices for aesthetic privacy or shading purposes. Owners must get the approval of the Association Staff or Design Review Committee, prior to submitting a proposal and application.
Screens may be constructed with wood, composite, or metal materials. The colors for screens shall follow the guidelines outlined in Article 5.4.
Screens may not exceed 16 feet in length or 8 feet in height. The DRC shall consider exceptions to these dimensions based on the lot, the size of the house, or surrounding properties.
Wood or composite material utilized for screening may be used horizontally if the area is under 16 feet in length. Anything beyond 16 feet must use vertical planks.

provisions.heading: Utility Screening (Air Conditioners, Generators, Heat Pumps, and Garbage Cans)

provisions.text: Garbage cans shall be screened by fencing or landscaping to not be visible from neighbors, street, or golf course.

Screens may not be placed forward of the front corner of the house for typical lot configuration. Exceptions may be considered in unusual situations where the placement of the house on a given lot may pose a unique challenge. Total concealment from the street view is mandatory from all angles.

Small wooden screening devices intended to conceal trash cans, AC units, generators, or heat pumps can be stained with a stain that complies with Article 5.4, or a solid or semi-transparent color that matches the body color of the house. Metal and composite materials will be considered.
Materials and designs for screening devices shall be compatible with the home.
Shrubbery shall also be considered acceptable concealment but must provide concealment from street view from all angles.
Screening around public utilities is prohibited.

provisions.heading: Structures Detached from Residences, Gazebos and Pergolas

provisions.text: Proposals for structures detached from residences and gazebos require approval. Prior to submitting an application, the Reviewer recommends that the Owner meet with the Association Staff. It is also recommended that the Owner research King County codes. Approval does not assure compliance with King County Codes.

provisions.intro: Plans and specifications, including the following, shall be provided to the Reviewer:
provisions.text: Proposed structures shall be compatible with the materials, and color of the residence and be conservative in color, design and scale.

provisions.label: 7.13.2(i)
provisions.text: A site plan showing the location of the structure and the distances to any boundary lines and other structures on the property.

provisions.label: 7.13.2(ii)
provisions.text: Materials.

provisions.label: 7.13.2(iii)
provisions.text: Colors.

provisions.label: 7.13.2(iv)
provisions.text: Dimensions and elevations.
Examples of the proposed material are usually required. Wood is preferred; however, other materials will be considered. The materials and the design should be compatible with the home.
Structures shall not have solid walls including glass; however, screening will be considered.

Prior to submitting a Design Review Application for patios, porches, and decks, an owner must ensure that such additions or improvements will not result in a violation of the maximum percentage of impervious surface coverage set forth in RDG 3.5.

Building around the engineered walls requires special attention if the deck extends into the 5-foot easement from the wall. Anchoring of decks should be avoided within the easement area. Design for decks within the easement area should provide for cantilever of the deck over the easement area.

A proposed patio cover or deck cover attached to a residence shall be compatible with the materials and colors of the residence. Patio and deck covers should be conservative in color, design, and scale. Plans and specifications including a site plan showing the location of the patio or deck cover and distances to Unit boundary lines and other structures on the Unit materials; colors; and elevations must be submitted to the Reviewer. See RDG 7.21 (External Remodeling) for requests proposing changes to the Unit roofline.

Appropriate materials for patio floors include concrete, pavers, brick, or rock set in a full mortar base. Concrete patio floors may be coated with "cool decking" (a slip resistant topping applied over a stronger concrete base).
Decks are recommended to be constructed of wood or composite materials with a color that complements the residence color.
Patio and deck enclosures shall not have solid walls, including glass; however, screening will be considered.

Owners are encouraged to screen the open areas under decks more than 6 feet above the ground with landscaping and/ or lattice. If installed, lattice must conform to those styles shown in Exhibit O. The Reviewer may also require additional provisions to reduce the visual impact of the lattice screening.

Front and back-porch porch handrails and railings (including posts and balusters) must be metal, wood, or a composite material, and feature vertical balusters. Metal railings or handrails must be black. Wood staining or composite materials must match the body or trim exterior color of the home.

Deck railings (including posts and balusters) at the back or side of the home shall be metal, wood, tempered glass or composite material and finished in a wood-color stain that matches or is compatible with the deck color and the house color palette.
Black metal balusters to support wood deck railings and between railing posts that complement surrounding materials and wood color will be considered by the Reviewer.

rules.title: Termination at a renewal Recorded in the year before it
rules.statement: If the law limits how long covenants running with the land can be enforced, terminating the {{declaration}} at the end of its 20-year term or a 10-year extension needs an instrument signed by the {{owner:plural}} Article 21 requires, Recorded within the year before that extension.

rules.title: Any Owner may enforce the Declaration
rules.statement: Any {{owner}}, and the Owner's legal representatives, heirs, successors and assigns, may enforce the {{declaration}}, perpetually to the extent the law permits.

rules.title: The Declarant may enforce the Declaration
rules.statement: The {{declarant}}, and its legal representatives, successors and assigns, may enforce the {{declaration}}, perpetually to the extent the law permits.

rules.title: Easements survive termination without their holder's consent
rules.statement: Terminating the {{declaration}} doesn't terminate an {{easement}} it created without the consent of that easement's holder.

rules.title: Board consents may also need the Declarant's consent
rules.statement: Once the {{class-b-member}} ends the Class "B" Control Period, if the {{declarant}} so requires in a Recorded document, an action that needs the {{board}}'s consent or approval under the {{declaration}} may be taken, while the Declarant, an {{affiliate}} or a {{builder}} owns any {{lot}}, only if the Declarant also consents to or approves it.

rules.title: Section 3.1 changes only by amending the Declaration
rules.statement: The restrictions in Section 3.1 can be amended only as an amendment to the {{declaration}} under Article 20, unless Section 3.1 specifically provides otherwise; {{use-restrictions}} under 3.3 can't change them.

rules.title: Each occupied Unit has someone 55 or older
rules.statement: Each occupied {{residence}} must be occupied by at least one person 55 years of age or older.

rules.title: No one under 18 lives in a Unit
rules.statement: No {{minor}} may occupy or reside in a {{residence}}, except as a guest under 3.1(a)(ii).

rules.title: Occupancy determinations follow UPD Permit Attachment 6
rules.statement: The {{board}}'s determinations of when a person occupies or resides in a {{lot}} must be consistent with Attachment 6 of the {{upd-permit}}.

rules.title: Only the Declarant, and later the Board, amends 3.1(a) for the Act
rules.statement: An amendment of 3.1(a) without the {{owner:plural}}' approval, to keep the exemption for housing for older persons, must be made by the {{declarant}} while it or an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibits A and B, and after that by the {{board}}.

rules.title: King County approves 3.1(a) amendments first
rules.statement: An amendment of 3.1(a) for the housing for older persons exemption needs {{king-county}}'s prior approval.

rules.title: 80 percent of occupied Residences have a Qualifying Permanent Resident
rules.statement: At all times, at least 80 percent of the {{community.occupied-residences}} must have a {{qualifying-permanent-resident}}.

rules.title: A surviving occupant stays only with the Board's permission
rules.statement: When a {{residence}}'s sole {{qualifying-permanent-resident}} dies, is hospitalized or otherwise absent for a long time, or their marriage is dissolved, an occupant 18 or older who lived with them may stay without one only with the {{board}}'s permission, given in its sole and absolute discretion, and only if the community stays at 80 percent and the occupancy, considering other factors the Board deems appropriate, wouldn't jeopardize the community's status as housing for older persons under the Act, now or in the future.

of.text: the occupancy, considering other factors the Board deems appropriate, wouldn't jeopardize the community's status as housing for older persons under the Act, at the time of the request or in the future

rules.title: Ask for the surviving-occupant permission in writing
rules.statement: A request for the {{board}}'s permission for an occupant to stay in a {{residence}} without a {{qualifying-permanent-resident}} must be a written {{occupancy-permission-request}} giving the names and ages of all proposed residents and occupants, and any other information the Board reasonably requires.

mustState: the names of all proposed residents and occupants of the Residence
the ages of all proposed residents and occupants of the Residence

rules.title: Guests under 18 at most 60 days a year
rules.statement: Persons under 18 may reside in a {{residence}} as guests of its occupants for at most 60 days in total in any calendar year.

rules.title: Leases state the community is for persons 55 and over
rules.statement: Each {{lease}} must state in conspicuous type that the {{lot:plural}} are intended for the housing of persons 55 years of age or older, and must be in writing and signed by the {{tenant}}.

mustState: a statement, in conspicuous type, that the Units within the Residential Community are intended for the housing of persons 55 years of age or older

rules.title: Leases make breaking the age rules a default
rules.statement: Each {{lease}} must provide that failing to comply with the age requirements and restrictions of 3.1(a) is a default under the lease.

mustState: failure to comply with the requirements and restrictions of Section 3.1(a) is a default under the lease

rules.title: Contracts of sale state the community is for persons 55 and over
rules.statement: Each {{contract-of-sale}} for a {{lot}} must state in conspicuous type that the Units are intended for the housing of persons 55 years of age or older, and must be in writing and signed by the purchaser.

mustState: a statement, in conspicuous type, that the Units within the Residential Community are intended for the housing of persons 55 years of age or older
the contract is signed by the purchaser

rules.title: Disclose the 55-or-older intent to prospective occupants
rules.statement: An {{owner}} must clearly disclose to any prospective {{tenant}}, purchaser or other potential {{occupant}} of the {{lot}} that the Units are intended for the housing of persons 55 years of age or older.

check.question: Did the Owner clearly disclose to every prospective tenant, purchaser or other potential occupant of the Unit that the Units are intended for the housing of persons 55 years of age or older?

rules.title: Report a change in occupancy within 10 days
rules.statement: When the occupancy of a {{residence}} changes, its {{owner}} must notify the {{board}} in writing, with the names and ages of all current occupants, immediately and in any case within 10 days.

rules.title: Association keeps age records
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must maintain age records on all occupants of {{residence:plural}}.

check.question: Does the Association maintain age records on all occupants of Residences?

rules.title: Board adopts age-compliance policies
rules.statement: The {{board}} must adopt policies, procedures and rules to monitor and maintain compliance with 3.1(a) and the Act, covering visitors, updating age records, exemptions and enforcement.

check.question: Has the Board adopted policies, procedures and rules to monitor and maintain compliance with Section 3.1(a) and the Act, covering visitors, updating of age records, granting of exemptions, and enforcement?

rules.title: Association distributes the age-compliance policies
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must periodically distribute its age-compliance policies, procedures and rules to the {{owner:plural}}.

check.question: Has the Association periodically distributed its age-compliance policies, procedures and rules to the Owners?

rules.title: Copies of the age-compliance policies on request
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must make copies of its age-compliance policies, procedures and rules available to {{owner:plural}}, their {{tenant:plural}} and {{mortgagee:plural}} on reasonable request.

check.question: Did the Association make a copy of its age-compliance policies, procedures and rules available in response to the reasonable request?

rules.title: Give the Board occupants' names and ages on request
rules.statement: When the {{board}} asks, each {{owner}} and resident must give it the names and ages of all occupants of the {{residence}}, with the affidavits and other documents it asks for to verify their ages.

check.question: Has the Owner given the Board the names and ages of all occupants of the Residence, and the affidavits and other documents the Board requested to verify their ages?

rules.title: Answer occupancy questions fully and truthfully
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must fully and truthfully answer any request from the {{organization}} for information about who occupies the {{residence:plural}} on the {{lot}} that the {{board}} judges reasonably necessary to monitor compliance with 3.1(a).

check.question: Did the Owner fully and truthfully respond to the Association's request for information about the occupancy of the Residences on the Unit?

rules.title: Units used primarily as residences
rules.statement: Each {{lot}} must be used primarily for residential and related purposes.

check.question: Is the Unit used primarily for residential and related purposes?

rules.title: Businesses not detectable from outside
rules.statement: A {{business-activity}} on a {{lot}} must not be apparent or detectable by sight, sound or smell from outside a permitted structure.

check.question: Is the business activity undetectable by sight, sound and smell from outside the permitted structure it's in?

rules.title: Businesses comply with zoning and the UPD Permit
rules.statement: A {{business-activity}} on a {{lot}} must comply with applicable zoning requirements and be otherwise allowed under the {{upd-permit}}.

check.question: Does the business activity comply with applicable zoning requirements, and is it otherwise allowed under the UPD Permit?

rules.title: No business visitors or door-to-door solicitation
rules.statement: A {{business-activity}} on a {{lot}} must not involve regular visits by clients, customers, suppliers or other business invitees, or door-to-door solicitation in the community.

rules.title: Businesses keep the residential character
rules.statement: A {{business-activity}} on a {{lot}} must be consistent with the community's residential character and must not be a nuisance or a hazardous or offensive use, or threaten the security or safety of others, as the {{board}} determines in its sole discretion.

check.question: Is the business activity consistent with the residential character of the community, and free of nuisance, hazardous or offensive use, and threats to the security or safety of others?

rules.title: Declarant, amenity and Association activities exempt
rules.statement: Section 3.1(b) doesn't restrict the activities of the {{declarant}} or its {{affiliate:plural}}, {{declarant-approved-developer:plural}}, the operation of {{private-amenity:plural}}, or {{organization}} and {{trrs}} services and operations.

rules.title: Principal dwelling leased only in its entirety
rules.statement: The principal dwelling on a {{lot}} may be leased only in its entirety, not by separate rooms; a detached in-law suite or guest house may be leased on its own.

rules.title: Leased guest houses meet the UPD Permit's accessory dwelling rules
rules.statement: A detached in-law suite or guest house may be leased on its own only if it meets the {{upd-permit}}'s requirements for accessory dwelling units.

check.question: Does the detached in-law suite or guest house meet the UPD Permit's requirements for accessory dwelling units?

rules.title: Leases in writing
rules.statement: Every {{lease}} must be in writing.

rules.title: Leases at least six months
rules.statement: Every {{lease}} must have a {{lease-registration.term}} of at least six months.

rules.title: A lease not in writing needs the Board's prior written consent
rules.statement: A {{lease}} that isn't in writing is allowed only with the {{board}}'s prior written consent waiving that requirement.

rules.title: A lease under six months needs the Board's prior written consent
rules.statement: A {{lease}} with a {{lease-registration.term}} under six months is allowed only with the {{board}}'s prior written consent waiving that requirement.

rules.title: Leases bind tenants to the Governing Documents
rules.statement: Every {{lease}} must require that {{tenant:plural}} and all occupants of the leased {{lot}} are bound by and must comply with the {{governing-documents}}; they apply even if a lease leaves this out.

mustState: tenants and all occupants of the leased Unit are bound by and obligated to comply with the Governing Documents

rules.title: Declarant's Units exempt from the lease requirements
rules.statement: Leases of {{lot:plural}} the {{declarant}} or its {{affiliate:plural}} own needn't be in writing, run six months, or include the Governing Documents clause.

rules.title: Declarant's Units exempt from the minimum lease term
rules.statement: Leases of {{lot:plural}} the {{declarant}} or its {{affiliate:plural}} own needn't run six months.

rules.title: Report a lease within 10 days
rules.statement: Within ten days after a {{lease}} is signed, the {{owner}} must notify the {{board}} or the {{managing-agent}} of it and give any additional information the Board reasonably requires.

rules.title: Give the tenant the Governing Documents
rules.statement: The {{owner}} must give the {{tenant}} copies of the {{governing-documents}}.

rules.title: No subdividing a Unit or moving its boundaries without the Board's prior written approval
rules.statement: A {{lot}} must not be subdivided, or its boundary lines changed, without the {{board}}'s prior written approval.

rules.title: Declarant may subdivide its own Units
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} may subdivide, change the boundary lines of, and replat any {{lot}} it owns without the consent of the {{board}} or anyone else.

rules.title: No time-sharing
rules.statement: A {{lot}} must not be used to operate a {{timeshare-program}}.

rules.title: Declarant may run a time-share program
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} may operate a {{timeshare-program}} without the consent of the {{board}} or anyone else.

rules.title: Other developers run a time-share program only with the Declarant's or an Affiliate's permission
rules.statement: Another developer may operate a {{timeshare-program}} only with the permission of the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}}, which needs no consent of the {{board}} or anyone else.

rules.title: Notice of a Use Restrictions change five business days ahead
rules.statement: The {{board}} must conspicuously publish notice of a proposed change to the {{use-restrictions}}, or of a proposed designation of {{voting-group:plural}}, at least five business days before the Board {{meeting}} that will consider it.

rules.title: Members heard before a Use Restrictions change
rules.statement: Before the {{board}} acts on a change to the {{use-restrictions}} or a designation of {{voting-group:plural}}, {{members}} must have a reasonable opportunity to be heard at a Board {{meeting}}.

check.question: Did Members have a reasonable opportunity to be heard at a Board meeting before the Board acted on the change or designation?

rules.title: Disapproving a Board change needs more than 50 percent, after the Class "B" Control Period
rules.statement: A disapproval of a Board change to the {{use-restrictions}}, or of a Board designation of {{voting-group:plural}}, needs a {{meeting}} after the Class "B" Control Period, before the change or designation takes effect, and the votes of {{members}} holding more than 50 percent of the Class "A" votes.

rules.title: Members adopt Use Restrictions by more than 50 percent
rules.statement: Use Restrictions the {{members}} adopt need the votes of Members holding more than 50 percent of the Class "A" votes, at a {{meeting}} called for that purpose.

rules.title: Members' Use Restrictions need the Class "B" Member's approval
rules.statement: During the Class "B" Control Period, Use Restrictions the {{members}} adopt also need the approval of the {{class-b-member}}.

rules.title: Copies of the Use Restrictions without cost
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must give a copy of the {{use-restrictions}} in effect, without cost, to any {{members}} or {{mortgagee}} who asks.

rules.title: Existing personal property may stay for the current Owner
rules.statement: An {{owner}} need not dispose of personal property that was in or on the {{lot}} in compliance with earlier rules because of {{use-restrictions}} or {{board-rules}} adopted after the Owner took title, for as long as that Owner owns the Unit.

appliesWhen.text: the personal property was in or on the Unit, in compliance with the rules then in effect, before the rule it breaks was adopted

rules.title: Daily fines for an unreported occupancy change
rules.statement: If an {{owner}} doesn't report a change in occupancy within 10 days, the {{organization}} may fine the Owner and the {{lot}} for each day after the change until it receives the notice and information.

rules.title: Legal action to enforce the age restrictions
rules.statement: The {{organization}} may enforce 3.1(a) in any legal or equitable manner the {{board}} deems appropriate, including a census of occupants, periodic proof of each occupant's age, and, as each {{owner}}'s attorney-in-fact, action to evict or remove the occupants of a {{residence}} that doesn't comply.

rules.title: Owners indemnify for age-restriction violations
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must indemnify, defend and hold the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}} and the {{organization}} harmless from any {{claim}}, loss or damage arising from the {{lot}}'s failure to comply with 3.1(a) and the rules adopted under it.

check.question: If the Claim arises from the Owner's Unit failing to comply with 3.1(a) or the rules adopted under it, has the Owner indemnified, defended and held the Declarant, its Affiliates and the Association harmless from it?

rules.title: Owners answer for losses their occupants and visitors cause to the Area of Common Responsibility
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must answer for all losses that anyone occupying or visiting the {{lot}} causes to the {{area-of-common-responsibility}}, even though that Person is also responsible for them.

rules.title: Business judgment in changing the Use Restrictions
rules.statement: The {{board}} must exercise business judgment and reasonableness on behalf of the Association and its {{members}} in changing the {{use-restrictions}}.

check.question: Has the Board exercised business judgment and reasonableness on behalf of the Association and its Members in changing the Use Restrictions?

rules.title: Call a disapproval meeting on petition
rules.statement: On receiving a petition, as the By-Laws require for special meetings, the {{board}} must call a {{meeting}} of the {{members}} to consider disapproving a Board change to the {{use-restrictions}} or a Board designation of {{voting-group:plural}}; otherwise it needn't call one.

check.question: For every petition received, as the By-Laws require for special meetings, to consider disapproving a Board change to the Use Restrictions or a Board designation of Voting Groups, did the Board call a meeting of the Members?

rules.title: A petition holds a Board change until the disapproval meeting
rules.statement: If a petition for a {{meeting}} to consider disapproving a {{board}} change to the {{use-restrictions}}, or a Board designation of {{voting-group:plural}}, is received before its effective date, the change or designation doesn't take effect until after the meeting is held, and then only as the meeting's outcome allows.

rules.title: Send each Owner the changed Use Restrictions
rules.statement: Before any new or changed {{use-restrictions}} under 3.3, or a designation of {{voting-group:plural}}, take effect, the {{board}} must send a copy of them to each {{owner}}.

check.question: Before each new or changed Use Restriction adopted under Section 3.3, and each designation of Voting Groups, took effect, did the Board send a copy of it to each Owner?

rules.title: A Use Restrictions change takes effect at least 30 days after distribution
rules.statement: A new or changed {{use-restrictions}} adopted under Section 3.3, or a designation of {{voting-group:plural}}, takes effect no earlier than 30 days after the {{board}} sends a copy of it to the {{owner:plural}}.

rules.title: Business judgment in Board Rules
rules.statement: The {{board}} must exercise business judgment in enacting, amending and enforcing {{board-rules}}.

check.question: Has the Board exercised business judgment in enacting, amending and enforcing the Board Rules and Regulations?

rules.title: Similarly situated Owners treated similarly
rules.statement: {{use-restrictions}} and {{board-rules}} the {{organization}} adopts under 3.3 must treat similarly situated {{owner:plural}} similarly, though they may vary by {{neighborhood}}.

check.question: Do the Use Restrictions and Board Rules adopted under Section 3.3 treat similarly situated Owners similarly, varying only by Neighborhood?

rules.title: No abridging religious and holiday displays
rules.statement: {{use-restrictions}} and {{board-rules}} the {{organization}} adopts under 3.3 must not abridge {{owner:plural}}' rights to display on their {{lot:plural}} religious and holiday signs, symbols and decorations of the kinds normally displayed in single-family residential neighborhoods; they may only restrict the time, place and manner of such displays.

rules.title: No regulating political signs' content
rules.statement: {{use-restrictions}} and {{board-rules}} the {{organization}} adopts under 3.3 must not regulate the content of political signs; they may regulate only the time, place and manner of posting them, including design criteria.

rules.title: No interfering with household composition
rules.statement: {{use-restrictions}} and {{board-rules}} the {{organization}} adopts under 3.3 must not interfere with an {{owner}}'s freedom to determine the composition of the household, except as 3.1(a) provides, by requiring that all {{occupant:plural}} be members of a single housekeeping unit, and by occupancy limits 3.5(c) allows.

rules.title: Occupancy limits based on the stated grounds
rules.statement: Occupancy limits in {{use-restrictions}} and {{board-rules}} the {{organization}} adopts under 3.3 must be based on {{lot}} size, fair use of the {{common-area}}, and compliance with King County ordinances.

rules.title: Occupancy limits reasonable
rules.statement: Occupancy limits in {{use-restrictions}} and {{board-rules}} the {{organization}} adopts under 3.3 must be reasonable.

check.question: Are the occupancy limits in the Use Restrictions and Board Rules adopted under Section 3.3 reasonable?

rules.title: No interfering with activities within dwellings
rules.statement: {{use-restrictions}} and {{board-rules}} the {{organization}} adopts under 3.3 must not interfere with activities carried on within a dwelling, except to prohibit activities not normally associated with residential property, and to restrict or prohibit activities that create monetary costs for the Association or other {{owner:plural}}, endanger anyone's health or safety, generate excessive noise or traffic, create unsightly conditions visible outside the dwelling, or are an unreasonable source of annoyance.

check.question: Do the Use Restrictions and Board Rules adopted under Section 3.3 restrict activities within dwellings only where the activities aren't normally associated with residential property, create monetary costs for the Association or other Owners, endanger anyone's health or safety, generate excessive noise or traffic, create unsightly conditions visible outside the dwelling, or are an unreasonable source of annoyance?

rules.title: No prohibiting leasing or transfer
rules.statement: {{use-restrictions}} and {{board-rules}} the {{organization}} adopts under 3.3 must not prohibit leasing a {{lot}}, except to comply with 3.1(a), or transferring one.

rules.title: No consent required to lease or transfer
rules.statement: {{use-restrictions}} and {{board-rules}} the {{organization}} adopts under 3.3 must not require the Association's or the {{board}}'s consent before a {{lot}} is leased or transferred.

rules.title: Lease and transfer fees reasonable
rules.statement: Any review or administrative fee the {{organization}} imposes on the lease or transfer of a {{lot}} must be reasonable.

check.question: Is any review or administrative fee the Association imposes on this lease or transfer of the Unit reasonable?

rules.title: No unreasonably impeding development
rules.statement: No {{use-restrictions}}, {{board-rules}} or action of the {{organization}} or the {{board}} may unreasonably impede the right of the {{declarant}} or its {{affiliate:plural}} to develop the {{community}}.

check.question: Do the Use Restrictions, Board Rules and actions of the Association and the Board leave the right of the Declarant and its Affiliates to develop the Residential Community unimpeded, or impede it only reasonably?

rules.title: No unreasonably impeding TRRS's services
rules.statement: No {{use-restrictions}}, {{board-rules}} or action of the {{organization}} or the {{board}} may unreasonably impede the rights of {{trrs}} to provide services to the {{community}}.

check.question: Do the Use Restrictions, Board Rules and actions of the Association and the Board leave TRRS's rights to provide services to the Residential Community unimpeded, or impede them only reasonably?

rules.title: No interfering with Private Amenities
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must not interfere with the use, ownership, appearance or operation of any {{private-amenity}}.

rules.title: Rules and actions consistent with the UPD Permit
rules.statement: No {{use-restrictions}}, {{board-rules}} or action of the {{organization}} or the {{board}} may conflict with the requirements and conditions of the {{upd-permit}}.

rules.title: An authorized restricted activity follows the Board's rules and conditions
rules.statement: An activity (a) restricts that the {{board}} expressly authorized remains subject to the {{board-rules}} and to the conditions the Board imposes on the authorization.

rules.title: Restricted vehicles parked outside garages or storage areas only with the Board's authorization
rules.statement: A commercial, recreational, oversized, stored or inoperable {{vehicle}}, mobile home or boat may be parked anywhere but an enclosed garage or an area the {{board}} designates as a vehicle storage area only if the Board expressly authorizes it.

rules.title: Loading and unloading 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.
rules.statement: A restricted {{vehicle}} may be parked elsewhere temporarily for loading and unloading between 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.

rules.title: Vehicle storage and repair outside an enclosed garage only with the Board's authorization
rules.statement: Vehicles or equipment of any type may be stored, repaired or maintained on a {{lot}} outside an enclosed garage only if the {{board}} expressly authorizes it.

rules.title: No capturing, trapping, injuring or killing wildlife without the Board's authorization
rules.statement: No one may capture, trap, injure or kill wildlife in the community unless the {{board}} expressly authorizes it.

rules.title: Wildlife may be taken for safety or as authorities allow
rules.statement: Wildlife may be captured, trapped, injured or killed when it poses an imminent threat to personal safety, or as a governmental authority requires or permits.

rules.title: Pets don't chase, injure or kill wildlife without the Board's authorization
rules.statement: A {{pet}} of an {{owner}} or {{occupant}} must not chase, injure or kill wildlife unless the {{board}} expressly authorizes it.

rules.title: No raising, breeding or keeping animals without the Board's authorization
rules.statement: No one may raise, breed or keep {{animal:plural}}, livestock or poultry of any kind in the community unless the {{board}} expressly authorizes it.

rules.title: Household pets permitted
rules.statement: Dogs, cats and other usual and common household {{pet:plural}} may be kept in a {{lot}}.

rules.title: A reasonable number of pets
rules.statement: A {{lot}} may have only a reasonable number of dogs, cats and other household {{pet:plural}}.

check.question: Is the number of dogs, cats and other household pets kept in the Unit reasonable?

rules.title: Pets don't roam free
rules.statement: A {{pet}} must not be permitted to roam free; one that is must be removed when the {{board}} asks.

rules.title: Pets aren't noisy, dangerous or a nuisance
rules.statement: A {{pet}} must not, in the {{board}}'s sole discretion, make objectionable noise, endanger the health or safety of others, or be a nuisance or inconvenience to others; one that does must be removed when the Board asks.

check.question: Is the pet free of objectionable noise, and does it neither endanger the health or safety of others nor constitute a nuisance or inconvenience to others?

rules.title: Pets leashed or confined outside
rules.statement: Whenever a {{pet}} is outside the dwelling, it must be on a leash or otherwise confined in a manner acceptable to the {{board}}.

rules.title: Clean up pet waste on the Common Area
rules.statement: Pet owners must properly dispose of any waste their {{pet:plural}} produce on the {{common-area}}.

rules.title: No obstructing or rechanneling drainage without the Board's authorization
rules.statement: No one may obstruct or rechannel drainage flows once drainage swales, storm sewers or storm drains have been located and installed, unless the {{board}} expressly authorizes it.

rules.title: Declarant and Association may alter drainage
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} and the {{organization}} may obstruct or rechannel drainage flows, within the limits below.

rules.title: Declarant's and Association's drainage work respects Units and the UPD Permit
rules.statement: When the {{declarant}} or the {{organization}} obstructs or rechannels drainage flows, it must not materially diminish the value or unreasonably interfere with the use of any {{lot}} without its {{owner}}'s consent, and must act consistently with the {{upd-permit}}.

check.question: Does the drainage work avoid materially diminishing the value of, or unreasonably interfering with the use of, any Unit without its Owner's consent, and conform to the UPD Permit?

rules.title: Declarant's and Association's drainage work needs King County's prior approval
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} or the {{organization}} may obstruct or rechannel drainage flows only with {{king-county}}'s prior approval.

rules.title: No converting garages, carports or attics into living space without the Board's authorization
rules.statement: A carport, garage, attic or other unfinished space, other than a basement, must not be converted to finished space for use as an apartment or other part of the living area of a {{lot}} unless the {{board}} expressly authorizes it.

rules.title: Garage enclosures include a replacement garage
rules.statement: Any request to enclose a garage must include {{plans}} for a replacement garage on the {{lot}}.

mustState: a replacement garage on the Unit

rules.title: Garage enclosures need the Reviewer's approval under Article 4 or the Board's authorization
rules.statement: A garage may be enclosed only with the {{committee}}'s approval under Article 4, which may be conditional on building a replacement garage, or the {{board}}'s express authorization.

rules.title: No harm to existing water supplies without the Board's authorization
rules.statement: No activity, including a non-governmental surface water management plan, may adversely affect the quality or quantity of existing water supplies unless the {{board}} expressly authorizes it.

rules.title: No garage sales without the Board's authorization
rules.statement: No one may hold a {{garage-sale}}, moving sale, rummage sale or similar activity unless the {{board}} expressly authorizes it.

rules.title: Nothing on the outside of a Unit without Article 4 approval or the Board's authorization
rules.statement: Nothing may be built, erected, placed or modified, permanently or temporarily, on the outside of a {{lot}} except in strict compliance with Article 4 and the {{residential-design-guidelines}}, with the {{committee}}'s approval, unless the {{board}} expressly authorizes it.

rules.title: Permitted Antenna: direct broadcast satellite services
rules.statement: A Permitted Antenna, one meter or less in diameter or diagonal measurement, designed to receive direct broadcast satellite services, is permitted on a {{lot}}, subject to the Residential Design Guidelines' reasonable location and screening requirements.

rules.title: Permitted Antenna: video programming via multipoint distribution services
rules.statement: A Permitted Antenna, one meter or less in diameter or diagonal measurement, designed to receive video programming via multipoint distribution services, is permitted on a {{lot}}, subject to the Residential Design Guidelines' reasonable location and screening requirements.

rules.title: Permitted Antenna: television broadcast signals
rules.statement: A Permitted Antenna, designed to receive television broadcast signals, is permitted on a {{lot}}, subject to the Residential Design Guidelines' reasonable location and screening requirements.

rules.title: Declarant and Association may erect master antenna apparatus
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} and the {{organization}} may, without obligation, erect an aerial, satellite dish or other apparatus for a master antenna, cable or other communication system serving all or part of the community.

rules.title: Items stored outside the dwelling or garage only with the Board's authorization
rules.statement: Items, including portable play equipment and temporary storage bins, may be stored outside the dwelling or an enclosed garage only if the {{board}} expressly authorizes it.

rules.title: Gardens permitted if neatly maintained
rules.statement: Gardens, planters and flower beds are permitted without the approval (a)(x) requires, but only if neatly maintained, consistent with the {{community-wide-standard}}, and in compliance with the {{upd-permit}} and the {{residential-design-guidelines}}.

check.question: Is the garden, planter or flower bed neatly maintained in a manner consistent with the Community-Wide Standard, and in compliance with the UPD Permit and the Residential Design Guidelines?

rules.title: Gardens neatly maintained, as well as approved
rules.statement: Gardens, planters and flower beds must be neatly maintained, consistent with the {{community-wide-standard}}, and in compliance with the {{upd-permit}} and the {{residential-design-guidelines}}, besides having the {{committee}}'s or the {{board}}'s approval that (a)(x) requires.

check.question: Is the garden, planter or flower bed neatly maintained in a manner consistent with the Community-Wide Standard, and in compliance with the UPD Permit and the Residential Design Guidelines?

rules.title: Nothing noxious, dangerous or unsightly
rules.statement: A {{lot}} must have no plants, animals, devices or other things whose activities or existence are noxious, dangerous, unsightly or unpleasant, or may diminish or destroy the enjoyment of the community.

check.question: Is the Unit free of plants, animals, devices or other things whose activities or existence are noxious, dangerous, unsightly, unpleasant, or of a nature that may diminish or destroy the enjoyment of the community?

rules.title: Nothing rusty or dilapidated outside
rules.statement: Structures, equipment and other items on the outside of a {{lot}} must not be rusty, dilapidated or otherwise in disrepair.

check.question: Is the item free of rust and dilapidation, and otherwise in good repair?

rules.title: No drawing on community waters
rules.statement: No sprinkler or irrigation system or well may draw water from the lakes, creeks, streams, ponds, wetlands or other ground or surface waters in the community.

rules.title: Declarant and its designees may draw on community waters as the UPD Permit allows
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} and its designees have the exclusive right to draw water from those sources and to lower their levels, to the extent the {{upd-permit}} allows.

rules.title: No open-air burning
rules.statement: No one may do open-air {{burning}} in the community.

rules.title: No wood stoves or zero-clearance fireplaces
rules.statement: No one may use a wood stove or "zero-clearance" {{fireplace}} in any residence or building.

rules.title: Barbecues and other outdoor cooking permitted
rules.statement: Outdoor cooking facilities, such as barbecues, are permitted, subject to {{king-county}} and other state, regional and local laws.

rules.title: No disturbing sensitive areas and perimeter buffers
rules.statement: No {{owner}} or {{occupant}} may act in violation of the {{upd-permit}}'s restrictions on sensitive areas and perimeter buffers, or remove, improve or disturb vegetation or fauna in them.

rules.title: Board may remove a pet
rules.statement: If a pet owner doesn't remove a {{pet}} that roams free or is a nuisance when the {{board}} asks, the Board may remove the pet.

rules.title: Work needs the Reviewer's prior written approval
rules.statement: No {{work}} may be done on a {{lot}} or in the {{community}} without the {{committee}}'s prior written approval, including work on a screened porch or patio visible from outside, enclosing a garage, and removing trees or shrubs from the landscape strip next to a {{lot}}.

rules.title: Repainting in approved colors and interior work need no approval
rules.statement: An {{owner}} may repaint the exterior in an already approved color scheme, and remodel, paint or redecorate the interior of a {{lot}}, without approval.

rules.title: Article 4 doesn't apply to the Declarant
rules.statement: Article 4, and the {{residential-design-guidelines}} adopted under it, don't apply to {{work}} by the {{declarant}}, an {{affiliate}}, a {{governmental-entity}} or a {{public-utility}}.

rules.title: A delegation of design review is in writing and names the responsibilities
rules.statement: A {{design-review-delegation}} by the {{declarant}} takes effect only in writing, and only if it specifies the delegated responsibilities.

mustState: the delegated responsibilities

rules.title: The DRC has three to seven members
rules.statement: The Design Review Committee, when appointed, must consist of at least three and at most seven persons, who serve and may be removed and replaced in the {{board}}'s discretion.

rules.title: Review fee paid before review
rules.statement: When the {{committee}} requires its review fee paid in full before review, an {{architectural-application}} isn't reviewed until the fee is paid.

rules.title: Review fees must be reasonable
rules.statement: Any fee the {{committee}} charges for reviewing an {{architectural-application}}, including the costs of having it reviewed by architects, engineers or other professionals, must be reasonable.

check.question: Is any fee the Reviewer charged for reviewing this application, including the costs of review by architects, engineers or other professionals, reasonable?

rules.title: Only the Declarant amends the guidelines while it owns property
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}}, an {{affiliate}} or a {{builder}} owns property in Exhibit "A" or "B", and unless the {{declarant}} has delegated its amendment authority to the DRC, an amendment to the {{residential-design-guidelines}} takes effect only if the {{declarant}} makes it.

rules.title: DRC amendments to the guidelines need the Board's consent
rules.statement: An amendment the {{committee}} makes to the {{residential-design-guidelines}} takes effect only with the {{board}}'s consent.

rules.title: Guideline amendments don't reach approved Work already begun
rules.statement: {{work}} the {{committee}} approved, whose construction began before an amendment to the {{residential-design-guidelines}}, needn't be modified or removed to meet that amendment; new work on it must meet the guidelines as amended.

rules.title: The Design Guidelines comply with the UPD Permit
rules.statement: The {{residential-design-guidelines}} and every amendment to them must comply with the {{upd-permit}}.

rules.title: Reviewer makes the guidelines available
rules.statement: The {{committee}} must make the {{residential-design-guidelines}} available to {{owner:plural}} and {{builder:plural}} who seek to engage in development or construction within the {{community}}.

rules.title: Applications include Plans
rules.statement: An {{architectural-application}} must include {{plans}} showing, as applicable, the site layout, structural design, exterior elevations, exterior materials and colors, landscaping, drainage, exterior lighting, irrigation and other features of the proposed construction.

mustState: Shows the site layout of the proposed construction, as applicable
Shows the structural design, as applicable
Shows the exterior elevations, as applicable
Shows the exterior materials and colors, as applicable
Shows the landscaping, as applicable
Shows the drainage, as applicable
Shows the exterior lighting, as applicable
Shows the irrigation, as applicable
Shows the other features of the proposed construction, as applicable

rules.title: Applications include required additional information
rules.statement: An {{architectural-application}} must include the additional information the {{residential-design-guidelines}} or the {{committee}} require as reasonably necessary to consider it.

check.question: Does the application include the additional information the Residential Design Guidelines or the Reviewer asked for as reasonably necessary to consider it?

rules.title: Work in harmony with its surroundings
rules.statement: Proposed {{work}} must be in harmony of external design with surrounding structures and environment, as the {{committee}} judges on any factors it deems relevant, including purely aesthetic ones; complying with the {{residential-design-guidelines}} doesn't guarantee approval.

check.question: Is the proposed Work in harmony of external design with the surrounding structures and environment, and acceptable on the aesthetic and other factors the Reviewer deems relevant?

rules.title: Reviewer responds in writing, with no time limit
rules.statement: The {{committee}} must respond in writing to the {{applicant}} at the address in the {{architectural-application}}, approving it with or without conditions, approving part, or disapproving it. No time limit is set, and nothing is deemed if it doesn't respond.

rules.title: DRC notifies the Declarant of approvals within 3 business days
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} holds design review rights, the {{committee}} must notify the {{declarant}} in writing, with a copy of the {{architectural-application}}, within 3 business days after approving it.

rules.title: A Declarant veto counts only within 10 days
rules.statement: The {{declarant}}'s veto of the {{committee}}'s approval of an {{architectural-application}}, in its sole discretion, takes effect only by written notice within 10 days after it receives the DRC's notice of the approval.

rules.title: Approval withdrawn if construction doesn't start within a year
rules.statement: An {{approval}} of {{work}} by the {{committee}} is deemed withdrawn if construction doesn't commence within one year after the date of approval, and the {{owner}} must reapply before commencing.

rules.title: Work completed within a year of starting
rules.statement: {{work}} must be completed, every element of it, within one year after construction commences, unless the notice of approval or a written extension from the {{committee}} gives another date.

rules.title: Construction diligently pursued
rules.statement: Once construction of {{work}} commences, it must be diligently pursued to completion.

check.question: Has construction been diligently pursued toward completion since it commenced?

rules.title: Aggrieved Owners may enforce against late Work
rules.statement: Approved {{work}} not completed within the required time is nonconforming, and any aggrieved {{owner}} may take enforcement action against it.

rules.title: Initial purchaser landscapes within 90 days
rules.statement: Unless the {{declarant}} or a {{builder}} installed it, the initial home purchaser of a {{lot}} must install landscaping under an approved landscaping plan within 90 days after title transfers to them.

rules.title: Activities exempted by resolution need no application
rules.statement: {{work}} the {{declarant}}, or the {{board}} with the Declarant's consent, has exempted by resolution, done in strict compliance with that resolution, or built to a plan a {{builder}} had pre-approved for general application, needs no application or approval.

rules.title: Variances need the Declarant's written consent while it owns property
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}}, an {{affiliate}} or a {{builder}} owns property in Exhibit "A" or "B", a variance for {{work}} takes effect only with the {{declarant}}'s written consent.

rules.title: Variances need the Board's written consent afterwards
rules.statement: Once neither the {{declarant}}, an {{affiliate}} nor a {{builder}} owns property in Exhibit "A" or "B", a variance for {{work}} takes effect only with the {{board}}'s written consent.

rules.title: Certificate of approval granted or denied within 30 days
