rules.statement: The {{organization}} must grant or deny an {{owner}}'s written {{certificate-request}} for a certificate of approval (no known violations of Article 4 or the {{residential-design-guidelines}} on the {{lot}}) within 30 days after receiving it.

rules.title: A certificate of approval estops enforcement of known conditions
rules.statement: Once a certificate of approval is issued for a {{lot}}, the {{organization}} can't enforce Article 4 or the {{residential-design-guidelines}} against {{work}} on it whose condition the {{organization}} had notice of on the certificate's date.

rules.title: Owners maintain their Units to the Community-Wide Standard
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must maintain, repair and replace as necessary the {{lot}}, including its structures, landscaping and other improvements, consistently with the {{governing-documents}} and the {{community-wide-standard}}, except any portion that's Area of Common Responsibility or whose maintenance the {{organization}} or a {{neighborhood-association}} has assumed.

check.question: Leaving aside any portion that's Area of Common Responsibility or that the Association or a Neighborhood Association maintains, are the Unit's structures, landscaping and other improvements maintained, repaired and replaced as needed, consistently with the Governing Documents and the Community-Wide Standard?

rules.title: Owners maintain and water the adjacent landscape strip
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must maintain and irrigate the landscaping on adjacent Common Area or public right-of-way between the {{lot}} boundary and the nearest wall, fence, curb or water's edge, unless it's designated Area of Common Responsibility.

check.question: Is the landscaping between the Unit boundary and the nearest wall, fence, curb or water's edge on the adjacent Common Area or right-of-way maintained and irrigated?

rules.title: Neighborhood Associations maintain their property
rules.statement: A {{neighborhood-association}} must maintain its common property, and any other property it's responsible for, consistently with the {{governing-documents}} and the {{community-wide-standard}}.

check.question: Is the Neighborhood Association's common property, and other property it's responsible for, maintained consistently with the Governing Documents and the Community-Wide Standard?

rules.title: Owners insure their Units at full replacement cost
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must carry property insurance for the full replacement cost of all insurable improvements on the {{lot}}, less a reasonable deductible, unless the {{organization}} or the {{neighborhood-association}} carries it.

rules.title: Rebuild damaged structures, or clear and landscape
rules.statement: After damage to or destruction of structures on a {{lot}}, the {{owner}} must promptly and diligently repair or reconstruct them consistently with the original construction or plans approved under Article 4, or clear the {{lot}} and keep it neat, attractive and landscaped to the {{community-wide-standard}}.

check.question: Since the damage, is the Owner promptly and diligently repairing or reconstructing the structures consistently with the original construction or plans approved under Article 4, or has the Unit been cleared and kept in a neat, attractive, landscaped condition consistent with the Community-Wide Standard?

rules.title: Neighborhood Associations repair, insure and rebuild their property
rules.statement: A {{neighborhood-association}} must repair and replace its common property to the {{community-wide-standard}}, insure it at full replacement cost, and after damage rebuild it or clear and landscape it, as Section 5.4 requires of an {{owner}}.

check.question: Does the Neighborhood Association repair and replace its common property to the Community-Wide Standard, carry property insurance on it at full replacement cost, and after any damage promptly rebuild it or clear and landscape it?

rules.title: Reviewer may grant variances from its guidelines
rules.statement: When unique circumstances such as topography, natural obstructions, hardship, or aesthetic or environmental considerations require, the {{committee}} may authorize a written variance from the {{residential-design-guidelines}}, but only in accordance with duly adopted rules and regulations, and never one contrary to the {{declaration}}.

of.text: the variance is authorized in accordance with duly adopted rules and regulations

rules.title: No liability for site work, plan defects or approved construction
rules.statement: No one may hold the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}}, the {{organization}}, the {{board}}, any committee, or any of their members liable for soil conditions, drainage or other general site work, defects in plans revised or approved under Article 4, or injury, damage or loss arising from the manner or quality of approved construction on or modifications to a {{lot}}.

rules.title: Certificate of approval fee must be reasonable
rules.statement: Any administrative fee the {{organization}} charges for issuing a certificate of approval on a {{certificate-request}} must be reasonable.

check.question: Is any administrative fee the Association charged for issuing the certificate of approval reasonable?

rules.title: Association may remove the violation and charge the Owner
rules.statement: If an {{owner}} doesn't cure a violation of Article 4 or the {{residential-design-guidelines}}, or restore the {{lot}}, within the time the written request gives, the {{organization}} may enter, remove the violation, restore the property, and assess the cost against the {{lot}} as a Specific Assessment.

rules.title: Interest on self-help costs at the Board's rate
rules.statement: The cost of removing an Article 4 or {{residential-design-guidelines}} violation bears interest at the rate the {{board}} establishes, not more than the maximum rate the law then allows.

rules.title: Association may remove or complete unfinished work
rules.statement: If approved {{work}} isn't commenced and diligently pursued to completion by its deadline, the {{organization}}, after notice and an opportunity to be heard under the {{by-laws}}, may enter the {{lot}}, remove or complete the incomplete work, and assess the cost against the {{lot}} and its {{owner}} as a Specific Assessment.

rules.title: Noncompliant contractors may be excluded
rules.statement: A {{contractor}}, subcontractor, agent, employee or other invitee of an {{owner}} who doesn't comply with Article 4 and the {{residential-design-guidelines}} may be excluded from the {{community}}, after notice and a hearing under the {{by-laws}}.

rules.title: No liability for excluding a noncompliant contractor or invitee
rules.statement: No one may hold the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}}, the {{organization}}, or their officers and directors liable for excluding an {{owner}}'s {{contractor}}, subcontractor, agent, employee or other invitee from the {{community}} under 4.8.

rules.title: Declarant may enforce when the Association doesn't
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}}, an {{affiliate}} or a {{builder}} owns property in Exhibit "A" or "B", if in the Declarant's discretion the {{organization}} fails to enforce Article 4 in a reasonable time, the {{declarant}} may remove the violation, restore the property, assess the cost against the violating {{owner}} as a Specific Assessment, and assert the Association's lien rights for it under Article 8.

rules.title: Legal and equitable remedies for Article 4
rules.statement: The {{organization}} may pursue all legal and equitable remedies to enforce Article 4, the {{residential-design-guidelines}} and the {{committee}}'s decisions, without the alternative dispute resolution of Article 14.

rules.title: Declarant's legal and equitable remedies for Article 4
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} may pursue all legal and equitable remedies to enforce Article 4, the {{residential-design-guidelines}} and the {{committee}}'s decisions, including against approved {{work}} not completed in time, without the alternative dispute resolution of Article 14.

rules.title: Designated Neighborhood costs paid through Neighborhood Assessments
rules.statement: Where a {{supplemental-declaration}} so designates, the {{owner:plural}} in a {{neighborhood}} must pay, through Neighborhood Assessments, the costs of operating, maintaining and insuring the portions of the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} within or next to the Neighborhood that it designates, whoever owns them and even if the Association does the maintenance.

rules.title: Assigning costs to a Neighborhood by agreement or resolution
rules.statement: The {{board}}'s assignment of costs of the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} to the {{owner:plural}} in a {{neighborhood}} takes effect only under an agreement with those Owners or with a {{neighborhood-association}}, or by a resolution based on a perceived need or a failure to comply with the {{community-wide-standard}}.

rules.title: Similarly situated Neighborhoods treated the same
rules.statement: Without specific agreements, the {{board}} must treat similarly situated {{neighborhood:plural}} the same when it assigns costs of the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} to them.

check.question: Where no specific agreement applies, were the Area of Common Responsibility costs assigned to this Neighborhood the same as those assigned to similarly situated Neighborhoods?

rules.title: Premiums for insurance the Association obtains for Owners are assessed
rules.statement: If the {{organization}} obtains insurance coverage on behalf of {{owner:plural}}, the premiums must be levied as a Neighborhood Assessment, when the coverage is provided to all {{lot:plural}} in the {{neighborhood}}, or otherwise as a Specific Assessment against the benefited Unit and its Owner.

rules.title: The Owner pays rebuilding costs insurance doesn't cover
rules.statement: When structures on a {{lot}} are damaged or destroyed, the {{owner}} must pay any costs of repairing, reconstructing or clearing the {{lot}} that insurance proceeds don't cover.

rules.title: Who exercises a non-individual Owner's membership
rules.statement: The membership rights of an {{owner}} that isn't an individual may be exercised only by its officer, director, partner or trustee, or by an individual it designates in a written instrument given to the Association's {{secretary}}.

rules.title: Membership passes only with title to the Unit
rules.statement: The rights and obligations of a {{members}} other than the {{declarant}} can be transferred only with ownership of the Member's {{lot}}, and only to the new owner; any other transfer is void, and every transfer of ownership transfers the membership.

rules.title: One vote per Unit
rules.statement: A {{lot}} has at most one vote, however many {{class-a-member:plural}} own it.

rules.title: No vote for property exempt from assessment
rules.statement: No vote counts for property that is {{lot.exempt-from-assessment}}.

rules.title: The Class "B" Member doesn't vote
rules.statement: No vote is cast or counted for the {{class-b-member}}.

rules.title: Co-Owners' vote suspended if disputed
rules.statement: If more than one Person seeks to cast a {{lot}}'s vote and its co-{{owner:plural}} didn't advise the Secretary in writing before the vote how it's cast, the Unit's vote is suspended.

rules.title: A voting representative votes only as the Neighborhood Association provides
rules.statement: A voting representative may exercise the voting rights of {{members}} who are also subject to a {{neighborhood-association}} only if and to the extent that association's governing documents provide.

mustState: Members' voting rights may be exercised by a voting representative
the representation extends to the matter on which the Unit's vote was cast

rules.title: No vote for a Unit the Association owns after foreclosure
rules.statement: No vote counts for a {{lot}} while the {{organization}} owns it after foreclosure.

rules.title: Combining Neighborhoods needs a majority of their Units
rules.statement: The {{board}} can combine two or more {{neighborhood:plural}} only with the consent of {{owner:plural}} of more than half of the {{lot:plural}} in the affected Neighborhoods.

rules.title: Only the Declarant, and later the Board, re-designates Neighborhoods
rules.statement: Creating {{neighborhood:plural}}, re-designating their boundaries or combining them, by Supplemental Declaration or amendment, must be done by the {{declarant}} while it or an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibits "A" or "B", and after that by the {{board}}.

rules.title: Neighborhood services need a majority of its Units
rules.statement: A request for a higher level of service or special services for a {{neighborhood}} takes effect with the vote or written consent of {{owner:plural}} of more than half of the {{lot:plural}} in it; the {{organization}} then provides them and assesses their cost to those Units as a Neighborhood Assessment.

rules.title: The administrative charge on Neighborhood services is reasonable
rules.statement: An administrative charge the {{board}} includes in the cost of a {{neighborhood}}'s higher level of service or special services, assessed as a Neighborhood Assessment, must be reasonable.

check.question: Is any administrative charge included in the cost of the Neighborhood's requested or special services reasonable?

rules.title: The same administrative charge per Unit for the same service
rules.statement: An administrative charge on a {{neighborhood}}'s higher level of service or special services must apply at the same rate per {{lot}} to all Neighborhoods receiving the same service.

rules.title: No more Voting Groups than Class A directors
rules.statement: A designation of {{voting-group:plural}} is valid only if their number doesn't exceed the number of directors the {{class-a-member:plural}} elect under the By-Laws.

rules.title: Voting Groups only after the Class "B" Control Period
rules.statement: The {{board}} may designate {{voting-group:plural}} only after the Class "B" Control Period ends.

rules.title: Each Voting Group votes on its own slate
rules.statement: In an election of directors, the {{members}} in each {{voting-group}} must vote on a separate slate of candidates.

rules.title: Each Voting Group elects an equal number of directors
rules.statement: Each {{voting-group}} is entitled to elect an equal number of directors.

rules.title: Voting Groups established by a Recorded Supplemental Declaration
rules.statement: The {{board}} can establish {{voting-group:plural}} only by Recording a {{supplemental-declaration}} that identifies each Voting Group, by legal description or other means, so that the {{lot:plural}} in each can easily be determined.

mustState: identifies each Voting Group by legal description or other means, so the Units within each can easily be determined
evidence that it was Recorded, such as its recording number and date

rules.title: Association accepts property the Declarant transfers
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must accept personal property and fee title, leasehold or other interests in real property described in Exhibits "A" or "B" that the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}} or their designees transfer to it.

rules.title: Association transfers back Common Area conveyed in error
rules.statement: On the written request of the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}}, the {{organization}} must transfer back any unimproved portion of the {{common-area}} originally conveyed to it for no consideration, to the extent it was conveyed in error or is needed to make minor adjustments in property.

rules.title: Association manages, operates and controls the Common Area
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must manage, operate and control the {{common-area}}, subject to the covenants, easements and restrictions in the deed or other instrument that transferred it to the Association.

check.question: Is the Association managing, operating and controlling the Common Area, subject to the covenants, easements and restrictions in the instrument that transferred it?

rules.title: Common Area rules reasonable
rules.statement: The rules the {{board}} adopts regulating use of the {{common-area}} must be reasonable.

check.question: Are the rules the Board adopted regulating use of the Common Area reasonable?

rules.title: Association maintains the Area of Common Responsibility
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must maintain the {{area-of-common-responsibility}}, including the Common Area, landscaping in public rights-of-way, other property assigned to it and its portions of the public trail system, in accordance with the {{community-wide-standard}} and the {{upd-permit}}.

check.question: Is the Area of Common Responsibility maintained in accordance with the Community-Wide Standard and the UPD Permit?

rules.title: Association maintains front-yard and street-side landscaping
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must maintain, replace, water, trim, weed, fertilize and otherwise care for the {{association-maintained-landscaping}}, with the frequency and in the manner the {{board}} sets.

check.question: Is the Association Maintained Unit Landscaping cared for with the frequency and in the manner the Board has set, apart from plantings an Owner or resident installed?

rules.title: Owner planting in Association-maintained landscaping needs the Board's consent
rules.statement: An {{owner}} or resident must not plant or install flowers, plants or other landscaping where {{association-maintained-landscaping}} is located without the {{board}}'s prior written consent.

rules.title: Owner maintains landscaping enclosed by an approved fence
rules.statement: Once an {{owner}} encloses side or rear yard {{association-maintained-landscaping}} with an approved fence or wall, the Owner must maintain the landscaping within the enclosed area.

check.question: Is the landscaping within the enclosed area of the Unit maintained?

rules.title: The Association needn't maintain owner-planted landscaping
rules.statement: The {{organization}} isn't required to maintain flowers, plants or other landscaping an {{owner}} or resident planted or installed, even where {{association-maintained-landscaping}} is located.

rules.title: Maintaining property it doesn't own needs a Board determination
rules.statement: The {{organization}} may maintain property it doesn't own, such as {{lot:plural}}, property dedicated to the public, or property of a {{neighborhood-association}}, only if the {{board}} determines that the maintenance is necessary or desirable to maintain the {{community-wide-standard}}.

rules.title: No Association liability for property it doesn't own, absent negligence
rules.statement: No one may hold the {{organization}} liable for damage or injury occurring on, or arising out of the condition of, property it doesn't own, except to the extent it was negligent in performing its maintenance responsibilities.

check.question: Was the Association negligent in performing its maintenance responsibilities for the property the Claim concerns?

rules.title: Common facilities kept in continuous operation
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must keep the facilities and equipment in the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} in continuous operation, except for periods the {{board}} decides are needed for maintenance or repairs.

check.question: Are the facilities and equipment within the Area of Common Responsibility in continuous operation, apart from periods the Board determined were needed for maintenance or repairs, or a discontinuance the Members approved?

rules.title: Discontinuing operation needs 67 percent of Class A votes
rules.statement: Discontinuing operation of facilities in the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} needs the written agreement of {{class-a-member:plural}} holding at least 67 percent of all Class "A" votes.

rules.title: Discontinuing operation needs the Class B Member's written agreement
rules.statement: During the Class "B" Control Period, discontinuing operation of facilities in the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} also needs the written agreement of the {{class-b-member}}.

rules.title: Reducing the Area of Common Responsibility needs the Declarant
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibit "A" or "B", the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} can be reduced, by amendment or otherwise, only with the Declarant's prior written approval.

rules.title: Area of Common Responsibility costs are a Common Expense
rules.statement: The costs of maintaining, repairing and replacing the parts of the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} that aren't {{limited-common-area}} must be a Common Expense, though the {{organization}} may seek reimbursement from their owners or others responsible for them under the {{declaration}}, a {{supplemental-declaration}}, a {{covenant-to-share-costs}}, or other Recorded covenants or agreements.

rules.title: Blanket property insurance at full replacement cost
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must keep blanket property insurance covering the full replacement cost of the insurable improvements on the {{common-area}} and within the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} it has assumed responsibility for.

rules.title: General liability insurance of at least $1,000,000
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must keep commercial general liability insurance on the {{area-of-common-responsibility}}, insuring the Association and its {{members}}, with limits of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence.

rules.title: Workers compensation insurance where law requires it
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must keep workers compensation and employers liability insurance if and to the extent law requires it.

appliesWhen.text: the law requires the Association to carry workers compensation or employers liability insurance

rules.title: Directors and officers liability coverage
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must keep directors and officers liability coverage.

rules.title: Fidelity coverage of at least one-sixth of assessments plus reserves
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must keep commercial crime insurance, including fidelity insurance on everyone who handles Association funds, of at least one-sixth of the {{community.annual-base-assessments}} plus {{community.reserves-on-hand}}.

rules.title: Nearest equivalent coverage when insurance isn't reasonably available
rules.statement: Where a coverage Section 7.3(a) requires isn't reasonably available, the {{organization}} must instead keep the most nearly equivalent coverage that is reasonably available, and every other required coverage.

check.question: Does the Association carry each coverage Section 7.3(a) requires, or, for each one that isn't reasonably available, the most nearly equivalent coverage that is reasonably available?

rules.title: Fidelity policies waive the volunteer exclusion
rules.statement: A fidelity {{insurance-policy}} must waive all defenses based on the exclusion of Persons serving without compensation.

rules.title: Additional insurance the Board finds advisable
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must obtain and keep the additional insurance the {{board}}, in its business judgment, determines advisable, or the most nearly equivalent coverage that's reasonably available.

rules.title: Neighborhood property insurance when a Supplemental Declaration requires it
rules.statement: If a Supplemental Declaration so specifies, the {{organization}} must insure the insurable improvements in the {{neighborhood}} as Section 7.3(a)(i) requires, with a certificate of insurance for each insured Owner on request.

rules.title: Insurance premiums are Common Expenses
rules.statement: Premiums for insurance on the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} must be Common Expenses, except premiums allocated among Persons other than {{owner:plural}} under a {{covenant-to-share-costs}} or other Recorded agreement, premiums for property insurance on {{lot:plural}} in a {{neighborhood}}, and premiums for insurance on a {{limited-common-area}} assessed as 7.3(a)/p3 allows.

rules.title: Neighborhood Unit property insurance is a Neighborhood Expense
rules.statement: Premiums for property insurance on {{lot:plural}} within a {{neighborhood}} must be a Neighborhood Expense.

rules.title: Insurance reviewed every year
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must have the sufficiency of its insurance coverage reviewed once a year.

rules.title: Insurance reviewed by qualified Persons
rules.statement: The annual insurance review must be done by one or more qualified Persons, at least one familiar with insurable replacement costs in the King County, Washington area.

mustState: the sufficiency of the Association's insurance coverage was reviewed
the reviewers are qualified, and at least one is familiar with insurable replacement costs in the King County, Washington area

rules.title: Policies provide certificates of insurance
rules.statement: Every Association {{insurance-policy}} must provide for a certificate of insurance to the Association and, on request, to each Member insured.

rules.title: Owners answer for insured losses they cause
rules.statement: An {{owner}} must not cause an insured loss through negligence or willful misconduct, by the Owner or the Owner's guests, invitees or lessees.

check.question: Was the insured loss free of negligence or willful misconduct by the Owner or the Owner's guests, invitees or lessees?

rules.title: Policies written with a qualified insurer
rules.statement: Every {{insurance-policy}} the Board obtains must be written with a company authorized to do business in Washington that meets FNMA's requirements, or another agency's the Board deems appropriate.

rules.title: Policies in the Association's name as trustee
rules.statement: Every {{insurance-policy}} the Board obtains must be written in the name of the Association as trustee for the benefited parties.

rules.title: Policies not in contribution with Owners' insurance
rules.statement: Every {{insurance-policy}} the Board obtains must not be brought into contribution with insurance that Owners, occupants or their Mortgagees buy individually.

rules.title: Policies carry an inflation guard
rules.statement: Every {{insurance-policy}} the Board obtains must contain an inflation guard endorsement.

rules.title: Agreed amount endorsement with co-insurance
rules.statement: An {{insurance-policy}} with a co-insurance clause must include an agreed amount endorsement.

rules.title: Each Owner an insured as a Member
rules.statement: Every {{insurance-policy}} the Board obtains must make each {{owner}} an insured for liability arising from the Owner's interest in the Common Area as a Member.

rules.title: Waiver of subrogation against Owners
rules.statement: Every {{insurance-policy}} the Board obtains must waive subrogation against any {{owner}} or member of an Owner's household.

rules.title: No cancellation without a demand to cure
rules.statement: Every {{insurance-policy}} the Board obtains must preclude cancellation, invalidation, suspension or non-renewal because of individual Owners, or of a curable defect, without prior written demand to the Association and a reasonable time to cure.

rules.title: No cancellation for an Owner's acts
rules.statement: Every {{insurance-policy}} the Board obtains must preclude cancellation, invalidation or a condition to recovery because of an individual Owner's act or omission, unless the Owner acted for the Association.

rules.title: Waiver of subrogation for the Board, staff and Owners
rules.statement: The {{board}} should secure policies that waive subrogation as to claims against the Board, officers, employees, manager, Owners and their tenants, servants, agents and guests.

rules.title: Insurer waives repair instead of cash
rules.statement: The {{board}} should secure policies that waive the insurer's rights to repair and reconstruct instead of paying cash.

rules.title: 30 days' notice of cancellation
rules.statement: The {{board}} should secure policies that require at least 30 days' prior written notice to the Association of cancellation, substantial modification or non-renewal.

rules.title: Cross liability provision
rules.statement: The {{board}} should secure policies with a cross liability provision.

rules.title: Not rebuilding needs 75 percent of Class A votes
rules.statement: A decision not to repair or rebuild damaged {{common-area}} improvements needs {{class-a-member:plural}} holding at least 75 percent of all Class "A" votes; otherwise they must be repaired or rebuilt in a timely manner.

rules.title: Not rebuilding needs the Class B Member's agreement
rules.statement: During the Class "B" Control Period, a decision not to repair or rebuild damaged {{common-area}} improvements also needs the {{class-b-member}}.

rules.title: Insurance shortfall assessed without a vote
rules.statement: The {{board}} may levy a Special Assessment to cover an insurance shortfall on those responsible for the premiums without a vote of the {{members}}.

rules.title: Neighborhood Associations act within the time the notice sets
rules.statement: A {{neighborhood-association}} must take the action the {{organization}} requires in a written notice within the reasonable time the notice sets.

rules.title: Comply with the UPD Permit and King County law
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must comply with the restrictions and requirements of the {{upd-permit}} and other applicable King County laws.

check.question: Do the Unit and its use comply with the restrictions and requirements of the UPD Permit and other applicable King County laws?

rules.title: Sensitive Area standards
rules.statement: The {{owner}} of a {{lot}} in a Sensitive Area must abide by the {{upd-permit}}'s Sensitive Area standards, including its non-disturbance, buffer and setback requirements.

check.question: Does the Unit meet the UPD Permit's Sensitive Area standards, including its non-disturbance, buffer and setback requirements?

rules.title: Common Expense budget prepared 60 days before the fiscal year
rules.statement: The {{board}} must prepare the {{budget}} of Common Expenses at least 60 days before each fiscal year begins.

rules.title: Neighborhood budgets prepared 60 days before the fiscal year
rules.statement: The {{board}} must prepare a separate {{budget}} for each {{neighborhood}} expected to incur Neighborhood Expenses at least 60 days before each fiscal year begins.

rules.title: What the Common Expense budget includes
rules.statement: The {{budget}} of Common Expenses must include the estimated Common Expenses with reserve contributions and Covenant to Share Costs expenses, and the sources and amounts of funds to cover them.

mustState: the estimated Common Expenses for the coming year
the amounts to be collected as reserves, as determined in the reserve budget
Association expenses under any Covenant to Share Costs
the sources and estimated amounts of funds to cover the expenses, including the amount to be generated by Base and Special Assessments

rules.title: What a Neighborhood budget includes
rules.statement: A {{neighborhood}}'s {{budget}} must include its estimated Neighborhood Expenses, any services its Owners approved under Section 6.4(a), reserve contributions, and the sources and amounts of funds to cover them.

mustState: the estimated Neighborhood Expenses for the coming year
the costs of additional or higher-level services the Neighborhood's Owners approved under Section 6.4(a)
the amounts to be collected as reserves, as determined in the reserve budget
the sources and estimated amounts of funds to cover the expenses, including the amount to be generated by Neighborhood and Special Assessments

rules.title: Declarant subsidies shown as a line item
rules.statement: A {{budget.declarant-subsidy}} must be disclosed as a line item in the income portion of the {{budget}}.

mustState: the Declarant's subsidy, as a line item in the income portion

rules.title: Budget or Special Assessment sent within 30 days of adoption
rules.statement: Within 30 days after adopting a final {{budget}} of Common Expenses, a revised one, or a Special Assessment, the {{board}} must send each {{owner}} subject to it the budget or the amount, and notice of a meeting to consider ratification.

rules.title: Neighborhood budget sent in the 30 days before the fiscal year
rules.statement: The {{board}} must send each {{owner}} in the {{neighborhood}} its final {{budget}}, the Neighborhood Assessment and notice of a ratification meeting within the 30 days before the fiscal year begins.

rules.title: Neighborhood budget sent at least 30 days before the fiscal year
rules.statement: The {{board}} must send each {{owner}} in the {{neighborhood}} its final {{budget}}, the Neighborhood Assessment and notice of a ratification meeting at least 30 days before the fiscal year begins.

rules.title: Neighborhood budget sent within 30 days of adoption
rules.statement: Within 30 days after adopting a {{neighborhood}}'s final {{budget}}, the {{board}} must send each {{owner}} in it the budget, the Neighborhood Assessment and notice of a ratification meeting.

rules.title: Ratification meeting 14 to 60 days after mailing
rules.statement: A {{meeting}} to consider ratifying a budget, a Neighborhood budget or a Special Assessment must be held at least 14 and at most 60 days after the materials are mailed.

rules.title: Budget ratified unless 67 percent of Class A votes and Class B disapprove
rules.statement: The {{budget}} and Base Assessment are ratified unless {{class-a-member:plural}} holding at least 67 percent of all Class "A" votes, in person or by proxy, disapprove at the meeting, and the {{class-b-member}}, if any, also disapproves; a quorum isn't needed.

rules.title: Neighborhood budget ratified unless 67 percent of its Units and Class B disapprove
rules.statement: A {{neighborhood}}'s budget and Neighborhood Assessment are ratified unless {{owner:plural}} of at least 67 percent of the {{lot:plural}} the assessment applies to, in person or by proxy, disapprove at the meeting, and the {{class-b-member}}, if any, also disapproves; a quorum isn't needed.

rules.title: Benefit-based levy by petition of a majority of Owners
rules.statement: A petition to levy a {{neighborhood}}'s structure maintenance, insurance and replacement reserve costs in proportion to benefit needs the signatures of more than half of the {{owner:plural}} in the Neighborhood.

rules.title: Special Assessment ratified unless 67 percent of its Units disapprove
rules.statement: A Special Assessment is ratified unless {{owner:plural}} of at least 67 percent of the {{lot:plural}} subject to it, in person or by proxy, disapprove at the meeting; a quorum isn't needed.

rules.title: Reserves held in separate accounts
rules.statement: The {{board}} must deposit all reserves, including reserve contributions under Section 8.11, in separate Reserve Accounts not commingled with other Association funds.

rules.title: Reserves spent only for their purpose
rules.statement: The {{board}} must not spend reserve funds for any purpose other than the one they were collected for.

rules.title: Two signatures to withdraw reserves
rules.statement: A {{reserve-withdrawal}} needs the signatures of two Board members, or of one Board member and an {{officer}} who isn't on the Board.

rules.title: Reserve study updated every five years
rules.statement: The {{board}} must obtain a {{reserve-study}} and update it at least once every five years.

rules.title: What the reserve study includes
rules.statement: The {{reserve-study}} must identify the major Common Area components with less than 30 years of useful life left, their remaining life, the cost to repair or replace them, and the annual contribution needed after existing reserves.

mustState: the major components of the Common Area the Association must repair, replace, restore or maintain that have a remaining useful life of less than 30 years
the probable remaining useful life of each identified component
an estimate of the cost of repair, replacement, restoration or maintenance of the identified components during and at the end of their useful life
an estimate of the total annual contribution needed to defray those costs, after subtracting total reserve funds as of the study's date

rules.title: Assessments paid when due
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must pay each {{assessment}} by its {{assessment.due-on}}, the date the Board sets; the Base Assessment and any Neighborhood Assessment are due in advance on the first day of the fiscal year unless the Board provides otherwise. Non-use of the Common Area or services, abandonment or set-off doesn't excuse payment.

rules.title: Certificate of assessment payment on request
rules.statement: On an {{owner}}'s written request, the {{organization}} must furnish a certificate signed by an {{officer}} stating whether an assessment has been paid.

mustState: whether the assessment has been paid

rules.title: Declarant may fund the deficit instead of paying assessments
rules.statement: During the Class "B" Control Period, the {{declarant}} needn't pay Base or Neighborhood Assessments on Units it or an {{affiliate}} owns in a year for which its {{community.declarant-election}} is to fund the budget deficit.

rules.title: Declarant funds the deficit when it so elects
rules.statement: In a year for which the {{declarant}} elected to fund the deficit, it must pay at least the difference between the Association's actual expenditures, not counting reserves, and the assessments levied on all other Units, in cash or in kind.

rules.title: No assessment on a Unit the Association owns after foreclosure
rules.statement: No {{assessment}} may be levied on a {{lot}} while the {{organization}} owns it after foreclosure.

rules.title: Buyer at foreclosure not liable for earlier assessments
rules.statement: The {{owner}} who acquires a {{lot}} by foreclosure of the first Mortgage isn't personally liable for assessments that fell due before acquiring title; they remain the defaulting Owner's obligation.

rules.title: No Base, Neighborhood or Special Assessments on exempt property
rules.statement: No Base, Neighborhood or Special {{assessment}} may be levied on property that is {{lot.exempt-from-assessment}}: Common Area, property accepted by a government or utility, or a Neighborhood Association's common property.

rules.title: Exemptions granted to 501(c) owners
rules.statement: A Person qualifying under Section 501(c) of the Internal Revenue Code that owns a {{lot}} for purposes listed there needn't pay Base, Neighborhood or Special Assessments once the {{declarant}} or the {{organization}} grants it an exemption.

rules.title: Working capital contribution of one-half percent
rules.statement: An {{owner}} who first buys a fully improved {{lot}} from the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} must pay the {{organization}} one-half percent of the {{title-transfer.sales-price}} as a working capital contribution.

rules.title: Working capital contribution paid on becoming Owner
rules.statement: The working capital contribution must be paid immediately on becoming the {{owner}} of the {{lot}}.

rules.title: Reserve contribution of $300
rules.statement: An {{owner}} who first buys a fully improved {{lot}} from the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} must pay the {{organization}} a reserve contribution of $300.

rules.title: Reserve contribution paid on becoming Owner
rules.statement: The reserve contribution must be paid immediately on becoming the {{owner}} of the {{lot}}.

rules.title: Transfer fee in the amount the Board sets
rules.statement: Each new {{owner}} must pay the {{organization}}, or its managing agent if the Board directs, the {{community.transfer-fee}}.

rules.title: Transfer fee paid on becoming Owner
rules.statement: The transfer fee must be paid immediately on becoming the {{owner}} of a {{lot}}.

rules.title: Transfer fee approximates the cost of a transfer
rules.statement: The {{community.transfer-fee}} must reasonably approximate the Association's administrative cost of a transfer.

check.question: Does the transfer fee reasonably approximate the Association's administrative cost of transferring a Unit?

rules.title: Fines for violations of the Governing Documents
rules.statement: The {{board}} may impose a reasonable fine, in the amount its range of penalties sets, assessed first against the violator and, if the violator doesn't pay in time, against the {{owner}}.

rules.title: Fines are a lien on the Unit
rules.statement: A fine imposed for a violation is a lien on the violator's {{lot}}.

rules.title: Suspension of voting rights
rules.statement: The {{board}} may suspend an {{owner}}'s right to vote.

rules.title: Suspension of voting rights for a Base Assessment over 90 days delinquent
rules.statement: Once an {{owner}} is more than 90 days delinquent in paying a Base Assessment, the {{board}} may suspend the Owner's right to vote without a hearing.

rules.title: Suspension of recreational facility use
rules.statement: The {{board}} may suspend a Person's right to use the {{recreational-facility:plural}} in the {{common-area}}.

rules.title: Suspension of recreational facility use for a charge over 30 days delinquent
rules.statement: Once an {{owner}} is more than 30 days delinquent in paying an {{assessment}} or other charge owed the Association, the {{board}} may suspend the right to use the {{recreational-facility:plural}} in the {{common-area}} without a hearing.

rules.title: Common Area facilities barred for debts to TRRS
rules.statement: On notice from {{trrs}} that an {{owner}} owes it money, the {{organization}} may bar the Owner, and anyone claiming a right through the Owner, from the Common Area facilities until the amount is paid.

rules.title: Suspension of Association services
rules.statement: The {{board}} may suspend services the Association provides to the {{owner}} or the {{lot}}.

rules.title: Suspension of Association services for a charge over 30 days delinquent
rules.statement: Once an {{owner}} is more than 30 days delinquent in paying an {{assessment}} or other charge owed the Association, the {{board}} may suspend services the Association provides to the Owner or the {{lot}} without a hearing.

rules.title: Self-help on a Unit in a non-emergency
rules.statement: The {{board}} may abate a violation on a {{lot}} that isn't an emergency, including removing personal property that violates the Governing Documents.

rules.title: Removal of an unapproved structure
rules.statement: The {{board}} may require an {{owner}} to remove a structure built in violation of Article 4 and restore the {{lot}} at the Owner's expense, and if the Owner doesn't, may enter, remove it and restore the property without trespass.

rules.title: Noncompliant contractors excluded
rules.statement: Without liability to any Person, the {{board}} may bar a {{contractor}} of an {{owner}} who doesn't comply with Article 4 and the {{residential-design-guidelines}} from further activities in the {{community}}.

rules.title: Cost of bringing a Unit into compliance
rules.statement: The {{board}} may levy a Specific Assessment on a {{lot}} for the costs of bringing it into compliance, or caused by the conduct of the {{owner}}, occupants or their guests, contractors or invitees.

rules.title: Deductible charged to a negligent Owner
rules.statement: The {{board}} may assess the full deductible of an insured loss caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of an {{owner}}, or the Owner's guests, invitees or lessees, against the Owner and the {{lot}} as a Specific Assessment.

rules.title: Policies carry only a reasonable deductible
rules.statement: An {{insurance-policy}} the Association obtains may contain only a reasonable deductible.

check.question: Is the policy's deductible, if it has one, reasonable?

rules.title: An insured loss's deductible is charged like the premiums
rules.statement: On an insured loss, the deductible must be treated as a Common Expense or a Neighborhood Expense in the same manner as the premiums for that coverage, unless the {{board}} assesses it against a negligent {{owner}} as a Specific Assessment.

rules.title: Common Area policies benefit the Association and its Members
rules.statement: Every {{insurance-policy}} on the {{common-area}} must be for the benefit of the {{organization}} and its {{members}}.

rules.title: Neighborhood policies benefit its Owners and their Mortgagees
rules.statement: Every {{insurance-policy}} secured on behalf of a {{neighborhood}} must be for the benefit of the {{owner:plural}} in the Neighborhood and their {{mortgagee:plural}}, as their interests may appear.

rules.title: Board files and adjusts insurance claims after damage
rules.statement: When Common Area or other property the {{organization}} must insure is damaged or destroyed, the {{board}} or its authorized agent must file and adjust all insurance claims.

rules.title: Estimates of restoration cost obtained
rules.statement: When Common Area or other property the {{organization}} must insure is damaged or destroyed, the {{board}} or its authorized agent must obtain estimates of the cost of restoring it to substantially its condition before the damage, allowing for changes building codes require.

mustState: the cost of repairing or restoring the damaged property to substantially the condition in which it existed before the damage, allowing for changes or improvements building codes require

rules.title: Restoration estimates reliable and detailed
rules.statement: The estimates the {{board}} or its authorized agent obtains of the cost of restoring damaged property the {{organization}} must insure must be reliable and detailed.

check.question: Are the estimates obtained of the cost of repairing or restoring the damaged property reliable and detailed?

rules.title: Unrestored property cleared of debris
rules.statement: If damaged {{common-area}} improvements won't be restored and no alternative improvements are authorized, the {{organization}} must clear the affected property of all debris and ruins.

check.question: Has the affected property been cleared of all debris and ruins?

rules.title: Unrestored property kept neat and landscaped
rules.statement: If damaged {{common-area}} improvements won't be restored and no alternative improvements are authorized, the {{organization}} must then maintain the affected property in a neat and attractive, landscaped condition consistent with the {{community-wide-standard}}.

check.question: Is the affected property maintained in a neat and attractive, landscaped condition consistent with the Community-Wide Standard?

rules.title: Mortgagees take no part in deciding whether to restore
rules.statement: No {{mortgagee}} may take part in deciding whether damaged or destroyed {{common-area}} improvements are repaired or reconstructed.

rules.title: Surplus insurance proceeds kept in a capital improvements account
rules.statement: Insurance proceeds left after paying for repair or reconstruction, or after a necessary and appropriate settlement, must be retained by the {{organization}} for the benefit of its {{members}} or the Persons entitled to use the damaged property, and placed in a capital improvements account; any affected {{lot}}'s {{mortgagee}} may enforce this.

rules.title: Self-help on a Unit in an emergency
rules.statement: In an emergency, the {{board}} may abate a violation on a {{lot}} without notice or a hearing.

rules.title: Towing vehicles that violate parking rules
rules.statement: The {{board}} may tow a {{vehicle}} that violates the parking rules and regulations, without notice or a hearing.

rules.title: Towing vehicles that violate parking rules in an emergency
rules.statement: In an emergency, the {{board}} may tow a {{vehicle}} that violates the parking rules and regulations, without notice or a hearing.

rules.title: Self-help on the Common Area
rules.statement: The {{board}} may abate a violation on the {{common-area}} at any time, without notice or a hearing.

rules.title: Suit for damages or an injunction
rules.statement: The {{board}} may sue for damages, or in equity to stop or prevent a violation, or both, without the By-Laws procedures.

rules.title: Association performs neglected Owner maintenance
rules.statement: If an {{owner}} fails to perform maintenance, the {{organization}} may, after reasonable notice and an opportunity to cure except in an emergency, perform it and assess its costs against the {{lot}} and the Owner as a Specific Assessment.

rules.title: Notice of violation Recorded for neglected Owner maintenance
rules.statement: If an {{owner}} fails to perform maintenance, the {{organization}} may, after reasonable notice and an opportunity to cure except in an emergency, Record a notice of violation against the {{lot}}.

rules.title: Association performs neglected Neighborhood Association maintenance
rules.statement: If a {{neighborhood-association}} fails to perform maintenance, the {{organization}} may, after reasonable notice and an opportunity to cure except in an emergency, perform it and assess the costs as a Specific Assessment against all {{lot:plural}} in the {{neighborhood}}.

rules.title: Association recovers its enforcement costs
rules.statement: If the {{organization}} prevails in an action to enforce the Governing Documents, it may recover all costs reasonably incurred, including attorneys' fees and court costs.

rules.title: Enforcement decisions not arbitrary or capricious
rules.statement: Whether to pursue enforcement action in a particular case is the {{board}}'s decision, but the Board must not be arbitrary or capricious in taking enforcement action.

check.question: Is the Board's decision whether to take enforcement action in this case neither arbitrary nor capricious?

rules.title: Board members meet the By-Laws' standards
rules.statement: In exercising the {{organization}}'s rights and powers, making decisions on its behalf (including whether to take legal action) and conducting its affairs, {{board}} members must meet the standards set in the {{by-laws}}.

check.question: Have the Board members exercised the Association's rights and powers, made its decisions and conducted its affairs in accordance with the standards set forth in the By-Laws?

rules.title: Officers meet the By-Laws' standards
rules.statement: In exercising the {{organization}}'s rights and powers, making decisions on its behalf (including whether to take legal action) and conducting its affairs, the Association's {{officer:plural}} must meet the standards set in the {{by-laws}}.

check.question: Have the Association's officers exercised its rights and powers, made its decisions and conducted its affairs in accordance with the standards set forth in the By-Laws?

rules.title: Indemnify officers, directors and committee members in proceedings
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must indemnify every {{officer}}, director and committee member against all damages and expenses, including counsel fees, reasonably incurred in any action, suit or other proceeding (including a settlement the then {{board}} approved) to which they're a party because they are or were an officer, director or committee member, limited to actions for which their liability is limited under 7.6 and Washington law.

check.question: Has the Association indemnified every officer, director and committee member against the damages and expenses, including counsel fees, they reasonably incurred in any proceeding (including a settlement the then Board approved) to which they were a party because of that position, for every action for which their liability is limited under Section 7.6 and Washington law?

rules.title: Hold officers, directors and committee members harmless on good-faith commitments
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must indemnify and forever hold each {{officer}}, director and committee member harmless from all liability to others on account of any contract, commitment or action made or taken in good faith on behalf of the Association.

check.question: Has the Association indemnified and held each officer, director and committee member harmless from all liability to others on account of any contract, commitment or action they made or took in good faith on behalf of the Association?

rules.title: Officers, directors and committee members not liable for mistakes of judgment
rules.statement: No one may hold an {{officer}}, director or committee member liable for a mistake of judgment, negligent or otherwise, except for their own individual willful misfeasance, malfeasance, misconduct or bad faith.

check.question: Does the mistake of judgment the Claim rests on involve the officer's, director's or committee member's own willful misfeasance, malfeasance, misconduct or bad faith?

rules.title: Officers and directors not personally liable on good-faith commitments
rules.statement: No one may hold an {{officer}} or director personally liable on a contract or other commitment made, or an action taken, in good faith on behalf of the {{organization}}, except to the extent they're also {{members}}.

check.question: Was the contract, commitment or action the Claim rests on made or taken other than in good faith?

rules.title: Veto Neighborhood actions only on the stated grounds
rules.statement: The {{organization}} may veto an action taken or contemplated by a {{neighborhood-committee}} or {{neighborhood-association}} only if the {{board}} reasonably determines it to be adverse to the interests of the Association or its {{members}} or inconsistent with the {{community-wide-standard}}.

check.question: Was every action of a Neighborhood Committee or Neighborhood Association that the Association vetoed one the Board reasonably determined to be adverse to the interests of the Association or its Members or inconsistent with the Community-Wide Standard?

rules.title: Require Neighborhood Association action only within its responsibilities
rules.statement: Any specific action the {{organization}} requires a {{neighborhood-association}} to take, such as specific maintenance, repairs or aesthetic changes, or items and expenditures in its proposed budget, must be in connection with the Neighborhood Association's obligations and responsibilities.

rules.title: Association acts for a Neighborhood Association that doesn't
rules.statement: If a {{neighborhood-association}} doesn't take a required action in time, the {{organization}} may take it on its behalf and levy Specific Assessments for the costs plus an administrative charge.

rules.title: Services in the Base Assessment only if provided to all Units
rules.statement: The {{board}} may include the costs of services and facilities the {{organization}} provides in the Base Assessment only if they're provided to all {{lot:plural}}; the costs of those provided to fewer than all Units may be charged as use or service fees or assessed as a Neighborhood or Specific Assessment.

rules.title: The Board can't cancel services the Governing Documents require
rules.statement: The {{board}} may modify or cancel existing contracts for services only as the contract terms allow, and must not modify or cancel services the {{governing-documents}} require.

rules.title: Association complies with the UPD Permit and King County law
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must comply with the restrictions and requirements of the {{upd-permit}} and other applicable King County laws.

check.question: Do the Association and the Area of Common Responsibility comply with the restrictions and requirements of the UPD Permit and other applicable King County laws?

rules.title: Declarant implements the UPD Permit programs during initial development
rules.statement: During initial development of the Residential Community, the {{declarant}} must implement, maintain and enforce the conservation, education and other programs and requirements of the {{upd-permit}}.

rules.title: Association accepts and fulfills delegated UPD Permit responsibilities
rules.statement: The {{organization}}, or the committee concerned, must accept and fulfill any {{upd-permit}} responsibilities the {{declarant}} delegates or assigns to it.

rules.title: UPD Permit program costs are a Common Expense
rules.statement: The cost of the {{upd-permit}} conservation, education and other programs must be a Common Expense, though certain costs may be shared with other owners and occupants within or near Trilogy at Redmond Ridge under a {{covenant-to-share-costs}}.

rules.title: Tax-exempt organization expenses are a Common Expense
rules.statement: The Association's expenses for, and contributions to, a {{tax-exempt-organization}} established for activities within Trilogy at Redmond Ridge must be a Common Expense, though the {{organization}} may share them with other property owners under a {{covenant-to-share-costs}}.

rules.title: Base Assessments levied equally on every Unit
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must levy Base Assessments equally against all {{lot:plural}} subject to assessment.

rules.title: Last budget continues when none is ratified
rules.statement: If a proposed {{budget}} is disapproved or the {{board}} fails for any reason to determine the budget for a year, the budget most recently in effect continues in effect, and the Base Assessment must follow it, until a new budget is determined.

rules.title: Neighborhood Assessments levied equally on the Neighborhood's Units
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must levy Neighborhood Assessments equally against all {{lot:plural}} in the {{neighborhood}} subject to assessment, unless a portion must be levied by benefit.

rules.title: Structure costs levied by benefit when required
rules.statement: If the Supplemental Declaration so specifies or a petition of a majority of the {{owner:plural}} in the {{neighborhood}} so directs, the {{organization}} must levy the portion of a Neighborhood Assessment for maintaining, insuring or reserving for particular structures on the benefited {{lot:plural}} in proportion to the benefit received, or in the other reasonable manner the Supplemental Declaration sets.

rules.title: Last year's Neighborhood budget continues when none is ratified
rules.statement: If a {{neighborhood}}'s proposed {{budget}} is disapproved or the {{board}} fails for any reason to determine it for a year, the budget in effect for the immediately preceding year continues, and the Neighborhood Assessment must follow it, until a budget is determined.

rules.title: Board prepares and reviews reserve budgets
rules.statement: The {{board}} must prepare, and periodically review, a reserve budget for the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} and for each {{neighborhood}} whose capital items the Association maintains as a Neighborhood Expense.

check.question: Has the Board prepared, and periodically reviewed, a reserve budget for the Area of Common Responsibility and for each Neighborhood whose capital items the Association maintains as a Neighborhood Expense?

rules.title: No Declarant liability for inadequate reserves set in good faith
rules.statement: If the {{board}} acts in good faith in determining the amount to be collected as reserves, no one may hold the {{declarant}} or its {{affiliate:plural}} liable to the {{organization}} or any Member because the reserves prove inadequate for the periodic maintenance, repair and replacement they were meant to fund.

check.question: Did the Board fail to act in good faith in determining the amount to be collected as reserves?

rules.title: Special Assessments on the membership or a Neighborhood
rules.statement: The {{organization}} may levy a Special Assessment to cover unbudgeted expenses or expenses over budget, against the entire membership if for Common Expenses, or against the {{lot:plural}} in a {{neighborhood}} if for its Neighborhood Expenses.

rules.title: Specific Assessments for services cover only their costs
rules.statement: A Specific Assessment the {{organization}} levies against a {{lot}} for services provided on the {{owner}}'s request under a menu of special services, or otherwise provided to fewer than all Owners under the Declaration or a {{supplemental-declaration}}, may cover only the costs of providing them, including overhead and administrative costs; it may be levied in advance of the service.

rules.title: Cost of bringing a Neighborhood into compliance
rules.statement: After prior written notice to the {{owner:plural}} in a {{neighborhood}} and an opportunity for them or the Neighborhood Committee to be heard, the {{board}} may levy a Specific Assessment against the Neighborhood's {{lot:plural}} for the costs of bringing it into compliance.

rules.title: Assessments start when the first levy or submission comes, whichever is later
rules.statement: The obligation to pay assessments on a {{lot}} starts in the later of the month the {{board}} first determines a budget and levies assessments and the month the Unit is submitted to the {{declaration}}; the {{organization}} must not charge a Unit for any earlier period.

rules.title: The first annual assessment is prorated by months remaining
rules.statement: The first annual Base Assessment and any Neighborhood Assessment levied on a {{lot}} must be adjusted according to the number of months remaining in the fiscal year when assessments commence on it.

rules.title: All assessments due at once on delinquency
rules.statement: If an {{owner}} is delinquent in paying any {{assessment}} or other charge levied on the {{lot}}, the {{board}} may require the outstanding balance on all assessments to be paid in full immediately.

rules.title: Assessments paid in advance at closing when the Board requires
rules.statement: When the {{board}} requires advance payment of assessments at closing of the transfer of title to a {{lot}}, they must be paid at the closing.

rules.title: Interest at 10 percent a year
rules.statement: An unpaid {{assessment}} bears interest from its due date at 10 percent a year, or a higher rate the Board sets within the limits of Washington law.

rules.title: Late charges set by Board resolution
rules.statement: An unpaid {{assessment}} incurs the late charges the {{board}} sets by resolution, within the limits of Washington law.

rules.title: Costs of collection and attorneys' fees
rules.statement: The {{owner}} of an unpaid {{assessment}} owes the costs of collection and reasonable attorneys' fees.

rules.title: A grantee is liable for assessments due at the transfer
rules.statement: On a transfer of title to a {{lot}}, the grantee is jointly and severally liable for any assessments and other charges due at the time of conveyance.

rules.title: Owners keep paying when the Board fails to fix assessments
rules.statement: If the {{board}} fails to fix assessments or to send an assessment notice, each {{owner}} must keep paying Base and Neighborhood Assessments on the same basis as during the last year for which an assessment was made, until a new assessment is levied.

rules.title: Certificate processing fee must be reasonable
rules.statement: The {{organization}} may require advance payment of a processing fee for an assessment payment certificate, but the fee must be reasonable.

check.question: Is any processing fee the Association requires in advance for the certificate reasonable?

rules.title: A payment certificate is conclusive evidence of payment
rules.statement: An assessment a certificate from the {{organization}} states has been paid is conclusively paid; it can't be collected from the {{owner}} as unpaid.

rules.title: Lien for delinquent assessments
rules.statement: The {{organization}} has a lien on the {{lot}} for a delinquent {{assessment}}, with interest, late charges and costs of collection, including use and consumption fees and facilities membership fees.

rules.title: Suit and foreclosure for delinquent assessments
rules.statement: The {{organization}} may enforce a delinquent assessment lien by suit, judgment and judicial or nonjudicial foreclosure, or sue for the unpaid amounts without foreclosing.

rules.title: Other Units share a foreclosed Unit's assessment
rules.statement: While the {{organization}} owns a {{lot}} after foreclosure, each other Unit must be charged, besides its usual assessment, its pro rata share of the assessment the Association-owned Unit would have been charged.

rules.title: Recreational facilities conditioned on paying fees
rules.statement: The {{board}} may condition use of the {{common-area}}'s {{recreational-facility:plural}} on payment of use and consumption fees or facilities membership fees.

rules.title: First Mortgage foreclosure extinguishes the lien for earlier installments
rules.statement: Foreclosure of the first Mortgage extinguishes the assessment lien for installments that fell due before the foreclosure.

rules.title: Assessments extinguished by foreclosure become Common Expenses
rules.statement: Assessments on a {{lot}} that the foreclosure of its first Mortgage extinguished must be treated as Common Expenses collectible from the {{owner:plural}} of all Units subject to assessment, including the acquirer.

rules.title: The working capital contribution isn't an advance on assessments
rules.statement: A working capital contribution under Section 8.10 doesn't count as an advance payment of any {{assessment}}.

rules.title: No refund of the working capital contribution
rules.statement: No one may claim a refund of a working capital contribution paid under Section 8.10.

rules.title: The reserve contribution isn't an advance on assessments
rules.statement: A reserve contribution under Section 8.11 doesn't count as an advance payment of any other {{assessment}}.

rules.title: No refund of the reserve contribution
rules.statement: No one may claim a refund of a reserve contribution paid under Section 8.11.

rules.title: Declarant annexes only Exhibit B property
rules.statement: A {{supplemental-declaration}} by which the {{declarant}} subjects additional property to the Declaration may cover only property described in Exhibit "B".

rules.title: Declarant annexation needs the property owner's consent
rules.statement: A {{supplemental-declaration}} by which the {{declarant}} subjects additional property needs the consent of the {{annexed-property-owner}}, if other than the Declarant, and of no other Person.

rules.title: Declarant's annexation right expires after 20 years
rules.statement: The {{declarant}}'s right to subject additional property expires when all property described in Exhibit "B" has been subjected or 20 years after the Declaration is Recorded, whichever is earlier, so its {{supplemental-declaration}} must be Recorded before then.

rules.title: Annexation right transferred only to a developer
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} may transfer or assign its right to subject additional property only to a Person who is the developer of at least a portion of the property described in Exhibit "A" or "B", and only before the right expires.

rules.title: Annexation right transferred by a Recorded instrument
rules.statement: A transfer of the {{declarant}}'s right to subject additional property must be memorialized in a written, Recorded instrument the Declarant executes.

mustState: the transfer or assignment of the Declarant's right to subject additional property
evidence that it was Recorded, such as its recording number and date

rules.title: Association annexation needs more than half the Class "A" votes
rules.statement: A {{supplemental-declaration}} by which the {{organization}} subjects additional property to the Declaration needs the affirmative vote of {{members}} holding more than 50 percent of the Class "A" votes, not just of the votes cast.

rules.title: Association annexation needs the property owner's consent
rules.statement: A {{supplemental-declaration}} by which the {{organization}} subjects additional property needs the written consent of the {{annexed-property-owner}}, who signs it.

rules.title: Association annexation needs the Declarant's consent while it owns property
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibit "A" or "B", a {{supplemental-declaration}} by which the {{organization}} subjects additional property also needs the {{declarant}}'s written consent, given by signing it.

rules.title: President and Secretary sign an Association annexation
rules.statement: A {{supplemental-declaration}} by which the {{organization}} subjects additional property must be signed by the Association's {{president}} and {{secretary}}.

rules.title: Added covenants need the property owner's signed consent
rules.statement: A {{supplemental-declaration}} by which the {{declarant}} subjects property someone else owns to additional covenants and easements needs the consent of the {{annexed-property-owner}}, evidenced by its execution of the Supplemental Declaration.

rules.title: Withdrawal only while the Declarant owns Exhibit property
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} may amend the Declaration to withdraw property only while it or an {{affiliate}} owns property described in Exhibit "A" or "B".

rules.title: Withdrawal can't unreasonably violate the development scheme
rules.statement: The {{declarant}}'s {{property-withdrawal}} must not unreasonably violate the overall scheme of development for the {{master-plan}}.

check.question: Is the withdrawal consistent with the overall scheme of development for the Master Plan, without unreasonably violating it?

rules.title: Withdrawal needs the property owner's consent
rules.statement: A {{property-withdrawal}} needs the consent of the {{withdrawn-property-owner}}, if other than the {{declarant}}, and of no other Person.

rules.title: Withdrawal needs any required King County approval
rules.statement: A {{property-withdrawal}} needs any approval {{king-county}} or other Jurisdictions require.

rules.title: Association acts to effect a Common Area withdrawal
rules.statement: If withdrawn property is {{common-area}}, the {{organization}} must take whatever action is required to effect the {{property-withdrawal}}.

rules.title: Public sites designated only while the Declarant owns Exhibit property
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} may make a {{site-designation}} only while it or an {{affiliate}} owns property described in Exhibit "A" or "B".

rules.title: Association permits the use of designated Common Area
rules.statement: If a {{site-designation}} includes {{common-area}}, the {{organization}} must take whatever action is required to permit the use, including dedicating or conveying the site if the {{declarant}} so directs.

rules.title: Declarant and Builders may keep sales signs on their Units
rules.statement: While they're selling Units, the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}} and {{authorized-builder:plural}} may maintain advertising, identification and directional signs on the {{lot:plural}} they own or lease, notwithstanding the {{use-restrictions}} on placing things outside a Unit and the {{residential-design-guidelines}}.

rules.title: Declarant and Builders may place sales offices and model homes on their Units
rules.statement: The {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}} and {{authorized-builder:plural}} may place sales and leasing offices, management and construction offices, a design center, model homes and parking areas on the {{lot:plural}} they own or lease, in the number, size and locations the {{declarant}} deems appropriate, notwithstanding the {{use-restrictions}} on placing things outside a Unit and the {{residential-design-guidelines}}.

rules.title: No fees for the Declarant's use of sales facilities
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must not charge the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}} or {{authorized-builder:plural}} fees or rental charges for access to and use of the sales, management and construction facilities, the clubhouse and the recreational facilities that 10.3 lets them maintain and use.

rules.title: Declarant's development work on Common Area fits its permitted uses
rules.statement: The {{declarant}}'s and its {{affiliate:plural}}' work, storage and other development activities on the {{common-area}} must not be inconsistent with the permitted uses and purposes of the Common Area defined in the {{upd-permit}}.

rules.title: Recorded covenants need the Declarant's consent while it owns property
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} owns property described in Exhibit "A" or "B", no Person may Record a {{covenant-instrument}} affecting any portion of the Residential Community without the Declarant's review and written consent; one Recorded without it is void unless the Declarant later approves it in a Recorded consent document.

rules.title: Recorded covenants need the Board's consent afterwards
rules.statement: Once neither the {{declarant}} nor an {{affiliate}} owns property described in Exhibit "A" or "B", no Person may Record a {{covenant-instrument}} affecting any portion of the Residential Community without the {{board}}'s consent; one Recorded without it is void unless the Board later approves it in a Recorded consent document.

rules.title: Changes to the Use Restrictions or Design Guidelines need the Declarant's approval
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibit "A" or "B", no amendment to or modification of the {{use-restrictions}} or the {{residential-design-guidelines}} takes effect without prior notice to and the written approval of the {{declarant}}.

rules.title: Community Systems and Services user fees are reasonable
rules.statement: A fee the {{declarant}}, or anyone it permits to provide Community Systems and Services, charges individual users for them must be reasonable.

check.question: Are the fees charged to individual users of Community Systems and Services reasonable?

rules.title: Community Systems and Services user fees within the legal maximum
rules.statement: A fee charged to individual users of Community Systems and Services must not exceed the maximum allowable charge for the service, where the laws, rules and regulations of the relevant government authority define one.

rules.title: Owners pay the provider for services they request
rules.statement: If particular services or benefits are provided to particular {{owner:plural}} or {{lot:plural}} at their request, the benefited Owners must pay the service provider directly, unless the {{organization}} assesses the costs as a Specific Assessment.

rules.title: Declarant contracts with service providers are bona fide
rules.statement: Any contract or agreement between the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} and a provider of Community Systems and Services must be bona fide and commercially reasonable.

check.question: Is every contract or agreement between the Declarant or an Affiliate and a provider of Community Systems and Services bona fide and commercially reasonable?

rules.title: Declarant rights transferred by a Recorded instrument
rules.statement: A transfer or assignment of the {{declarant}}'s special rights and obligations to a {{declarant-rights-grantee}} is effective only in a Recorded instrument the Declarant signs, unless the Declarant only permits the Person to exercise a right on a one-time or limited basis without intending to transfer it entirely.

mustState: the Declarant's rights and obligations transferred or assigned
evidence that it was Recorded, such as its recording number and date

rules.title: A transfer can't reduce an obligation or enlarge a right
rules.statement: A transfer of the {{declarant}}'s special rights and obligations to a {{declarant-rights-grantee}} must not reduce an obligation, nor enlarge a right, beyond what the Declarant has under the Declaration or the {{by-laws}}.

rules.title: A transfer of Declarant rights is consistent with the UPD Permit
rules.statement: A transfer of the {{declarant}}'s special rights and obligations to a {{declarant-rights-grantee}} must not be inconsistent with the {{upd-permit}}.

rules.title: Declarant enters a Unit only after reasonable notice
rules.statement: Except in an emergency, the {{declarant}} and others exercising its easement to inspect and correct may make an {{entry}} onto a {{lot}} only after reasonable notice.

rules.title: Declarant enters a structure only at an agreed time
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} or its {{affiliate:plural}} may enter a structure on a {{lot}} only after notifying the {{owner}} and agreeing with the Owner on a reasonable time to enter.

rules.title: Easement entry onto a Unit only after notice to the Owner or occupant
rules.statement: A {{person}} exercising the {{declarant}}'s easement or right of entry to inspect and correct may make an {{entry}} onto a {{lot}} only after reasonable notice to the {{owner}} or {{occupant}}.

rules.title: Inspection and correction don't unreasonably interfere with a Unit
rules.statement: The exercise of the {{declarant}}'s easement to inspect and correct must not unreasonably interfere with the use of any {{lot}}.

check.question: Did the entry avoid unreasonably interfering with the use of the Unit?

rules.title: Repair damage from inspection and correction at the exerciser's expense
rules.statement: Any {{property-damage}} to a {{lot}} or the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} from exercising the {{declarant}}'s easement or right of entry to inspect and correct must be repaired by, and at the expense of, the {{person}} exercising it.

rules.title: Repair damage from inspection and correction promptly
rules.statement: Any {{property-damage}} to a {{lot}} or the {{area-of-common-responsibility}} from exercising the {{declarant}}'s easement or right of entry to inspect and correct must be repaired promptly.

check.question: Has the damage been repaired promptly?

rules.title: Declarant and Builder notified before an expert inspects
rules.statement: No one may retain an expert to inspect the design or construction of structures or improvements for a potential or pending {{claim}} unless the {{declarant}} and any {{builder}} involved have first been notified in writing and given an opportunity to meet with the {{owner}} and conduct their own inspection.

rules.title: The Declarant complies with law in exercising its Article 10 rights
rules.statement: In exercising its rights under Article 10, the {{declarant}} must comply with all applicable laws, including obtaining any franchise, special use or permit approval needed.

rules.title: Board may suspend recreational facilities while a charge is delinquent
rules.statement: While any charge against an {{owner}}'s {{lot}} remains delinquent, the {{board}} may suspend the {{owner}}'s right to use the Common Area recreational facilities.

rules.title: Board may suspend recreational facilities for a delinquent charge, after notice and a hearing
rules.statement: While any charge against an {{owner}}'s {{lot}} remains delinquent, the {{board}} may, after notice and a hearing under the {{by-laws}}, suspend the {{owner}}'s right to use the Common Area recreational facilities.

rules.title: Board may suspend recreational facilities up to 30 days for a violation
rules.statement: After notice and a hearing under the {{by-laws}}, the {{board}} may suspend an {{owner}}'s right to use the Common Area recreational facilities for a period not to exceed 30 days for a single violation of the {{governing-documents}}.

rules.title: Board may suspend recreational facilities longer for a continuing violation
