rules.statement: After notice and a hearing under the {{by-laws}}, the {{board}} may suspend an {{owner}}'s right to use the Common Area recreational facilities for longer than 30 days while a violation of the {{governing-documents}} continues.

rules.title: A leasing Owner's Common Area use rights pass to the lessee
rules.statement: An {{owner}} who leases the {{lot}} is deemed to have assigned the right to use and enjoy the {{common-area}} to the {{tenant}} for the period of the {{lease}}, and doesn't hold it meanwhile.

rules.title: Board regulation of extended use rights must be reasonable
rules.statement: The {{board}}'s regulation of an {{owner}}'s extension of the right to use and enjoy the {{common-area}} to family members, lessees and social invitees must be reasonable.

check.question: Is the Board's regulation of Owners extending their Common Area use rights to family members, lessees and social invitees reasonable?

rules.title: No utility installation over, under or through an existing dwelling
rules.statement: Whoever exercises the {{declarant}}'s utility {{easement}} must not construct or install any system, facility or utility over, under or through an existing dwelling on a {{lot}}.

rules.title: Easement holder repairs damage to a Unit at its own expense
rules.statement: Any {{property-damage}} to a {{lot}} resulting from the exercise of the {{declarant}}'s utility {{easement}} must be repaired by, and at the expense of, the {{person}} exercising it.

rules.title: Declarant complies with law and obtains permits for easement work
rules.statement: In exercising its utility {{easement}}, the {{declarant}} must comply with all applicable laws, including obtaining any special use, right-of-way or other permit approvals needed.

rules.title: Easement holder repairs damage to a Unit promptly
rules.statement: Any {{property-damage}} to a {{lot}} resulting from the exercise of the {{declarant}}'s utility {{easement}} must be repaired promptly.

check.question: Has the damage to the Unit been repaired promptly?

rules.title: Installing or relocating utilities needs the Declarant's prior written consent
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibit "A" or "B", no one other than the {{declarant}} or a {{governmental-entity}} may do {{utility-work}} in the Residential Community without the {{declarant}}'s prior written consent.

rules.title: Installing or relocating utilities needs the Board's consent
rules.statement: Once neither the {{declarant}} nor an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibit "A" or "B", no one other than the {{declarant}} or a {{governmental-entity}} may do {{utility-work}} in the Residential Community without the {{board}}'s consent first.

rules.title: A specific easement's location needs the burdened owner's written approval
rules.statement: The location of a specific {{easement}} the {{declarant}} grants needs the written approval of the {{burdened-property-owner}}, except on property owned by a {{governmental-entity}}.

rules.title: Burdened owner doesn't unreasonably withhold, delay or condition approval
rules.statement: The {{burdened-property-owner}} must not unreasonably withhold, delay or condition approval of the location of a specific {{easement}} the {{declarant}} grants.

check.question: Did the owner of the burdened property act on the Declarant's request to approve the easement's location without unreasonably withholding, delaying or conditioning approval?

rules.title: Easement work minimizes interference with the burdened property
rules.statement: All work in exercising a utility, Community Systems or specific {{easement}} must be performed so as to minimize interference with the use and enjoyment of the property it burdens.

check.question: Was the work under the easement performed so as to minimize interference with the use and enjoyment of the burdened property?

rules.title: Restore the burdened property after easement work
rules.statement: On completing work under a utility, Community Systems or specific {{easement}}, the {{person}} exercising it must restore the property, to the extent reasonably possible, to its condition before the work.

check.question: Has the Person who exercised the easement restored the property, to the extent reasonably possible, to its condition before the work?

rules.title: Easement holders don't enter structures on a Unit
rules.statement: Exercising a utility, Community Systems or specific {{easement}} doesn't permit an {{entry}} into the structures on a {{lot}}.

rules.title: Easement use doesn't unreasonably interfere with a Unit
rules.statement: Exercising a utility, Community Systems or specific {{easement}} must not unreasonably interfere with the use of any {{lot}}.

check.question: Was the easement exercised without unreasonably interfering with the use of any Unit?

rules.title: Easement holders enter a Unit only after reasonable notice, except in an emergency
rules.statement: Except in an emergency, an {{entry}} onto a {{lot}} in exercising a utility, Community Systems or specific {{easement}} must be made only after reasonable notice to the {{owner}} or {{occupant}}.

rules.title: Declarant answers for Common Area damage from development
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} and its successors and assigns are responsible for any {{property-damage}} to the {{common-area}} caused by their actions in connection with development.

rules.title: Declarant agrees to share maintenance costs for outside property
rules.statement: If the development {{easement}} grants permanent access to property not submitted to the {{declaration}}, the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}} or its successors or assigns must enter into an agreement with the {{organization}} to share the cost of the maintenance the Association provides for the easement holder's benefit.

mustState: the Declarant, an Affiliate, or a successor or assign shares the cost of the maintenance the Association provides for the benefit of the easement holder

rules.title: The maintenance cost-sharing agreement is reasonable
rules.statement: The agreement the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}} or its successors or assigns enter into with the {{organization}} to share the cost of the maintenance the Association provides for the benefit of a development {{easement}} holder with permanent access to property not submitted to the {{declaration}} must be reasonable.

check.question: Is the agreement to share the cost of the maintenance the Association provides for the easement holder's benefit reasonable?

rules.title: Association entry onto a Unit after notice, except in an emergency
rules.statement: Except in an emergency, the {{organization}} may enter a {{lot}} only after notice to the {{owner}}.

rules.title: Association entry onto a Unit during reasonable hours
rules.statement: Except in an emergency, the {{organization}} may enter a {{lot}} only during reasonable hours.

check.question: Was the entry onto the Unit made during reasonable hours?

rules.title: Owners repair damage from entering a neighbor's property to maintain a structure
rules.statement: An {{owner}} who enters an adjacent {{lot}} or the {{common-area}} to maintain, repair or replace an approved fence, wall or other structure must promptly restore or repair any {{property-damage}} it causes, at the {{owner}}'s expense.

check.question: Has the Owner who exercised the easement promptly restored or repaired the damage, at the Owner's own expense?

rules.title: Owners maintain paving in a Private Roadway and Utility Easement
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must maintain, repair and replace, to the {{community-wide-standard}}, all paving improvements within the Private Roadway and Utility {{easement}} on the {{owner}}'s {{lot}}.

check.question: Are the paving improvements within the Private Roadway and Utility Easement on the Unit maintained, repaired and replaced in keeping with the Community-Wide Standard?

rules.title: Owners maintain private utility lines in a Private Roadway and Utility Easement
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must maintain, repair and replace, to the {{community-wide-standard}}, the private sanitary sewer lines, water lines, storm drain pipes and other utility improvements within the Private Roadway and Utility {{easement}} on the {{owner}}'s {{lot}} that no utility company maintains.

check.question: Are the private sanitary sewer lines, water lines, storm drain pipes and other utility improvements within the Private Roadway and Utility Easement on the Unit, other than those a utility company maintains, maintained, repaired and replaced in keeping with the Community-Wide Standard?

rules.title: Owners served by a shared utility line share its maintenance cost equally
rules.statement: When a sanitary sewer line, water line or storm drain pipe serves more than one {{lot}}, the {{owner:plural}} of all the Units it serves must share the cost of maintaining it equally.

rules.title: An Owner who damages a Private Roadway and Utility Easement repairs it
rules.statement: An {{owner}} whose act damages or destroys an improvement or utility line within a Private Roadway and Utility {{easement}} must rebuild and repair it without cost to the other {{owner:plural}}.

check.question: Has the Owner whose act caused the damage rebuilt and repaired the improvement or utility line, without cost to the other Owners?

rules.title: Golfers retrieve balls at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner
rules.statement: A {{golfer}} may come upon the {{common-area}} and the exterior of a {{lot}} to retrieve an errant golf ball only at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner.

check.question: Did the golfer come upon the property at a reasonable time and in a reasonable manner, only to retrieve an errant golf ball?

rules.title: Golfers enter a fenced or walled Unit only with the Owner's permission
rules.statement: A {{golfer}}'s {{entry}} onto a fenced or walled {{lot}} to retrieve a golf ball needs the {{owner}}'s permission.

rules.title: No liability for errant golf balls or the golf easement
rules.statement: No one may hold the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}}, the {{organization}} or its {{members}} (as such), a golf course's owner, operator or lessee or their assigns, a {{builder}} or {{contractor}} (as such), a {{governmental-entity}} or {{public-utility}}, or any employee, officer, director or partner of any of them, liable for damage, nuisance, injury or death resulting from errant golf balls or the exercise of the golf easement.

rules.title: No liability for golf course irrigation overspray
rules.statement: No one may hold the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}}, the {{organization}}, or a golf course's owner or operator liable for damage or injury resulting from overspray of water from the golf course's irrigation system or the exercise of the overspray easement.

rules.title: Easement holders comply with law and obtain permits
rules.statement: Exercising a right under an {{easement}} Article 11 grants or reserves must comply with all applicable law, including obtaining any franchise, authorization, building permit or other permit approval from a {{governmental-entity}} with an ownership interest in, or jurisdiction over, the affected property.

rules.title: Limited Common Area costs charged only to the Units it's assigned to
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must allocate the costs of maintaining, repairing, replacing and insuring a {{limited-common-area}} among the {{owner:plural}} of the {{lot:plural}} it's assigned to.

rules.title: The Declarant may later assign Limited Common Area to more Units
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} owns property described in Exhibit "A" or "B", the Declarant may later assign use of a {{limited-common-area}} to additional {{lot:plural}} or {{neighborhood:plural}} without the {{board}}'s approval or a vote of the {{members}}.

rules.title: Assigning Limited Common Area needs the Board's approval
rules.statement: Assigning Common Area as {{limited-common-area}}, or reassigning it, needs the approval of the {{board}}.

rules.title: Assigning Limited Common Area needs a majority of the Class "A" votes
rules.statement: Assigning Common Area as {{limited-common-area}}, or reassigning it, needs the vote of {{members}} holding a majority of all the Class "A" votes, not just of the votes cast.

rules.title: Assigning Limited Common Area needs a majority of the affected Neighborhoods' votes
rules.statement: Assigning Common Area as {{limited-common-area}}, or reassigning it, needs a majority of the Class "A" votes within the {{neighborhood:plural}} the assignment affects.

rules.title: Others use a Limited Common Area only with its Owners' approval
rules.statement: Letting {{owner:plural}} of other {{lot:plural}} use a {{limited-common-area}}, for reasonable user fees, needs the approval of a majority of the {{owner:plural}} of the Units it's assigned to.

rules.title: Limited Common Area user fees offset its expenses
rules.statement: User fees the {{organization}} collects from {{owner:plural}} of other {{lot:plural}} for using a {{limited-common-area}} must be used to offset the expenses attributable to that Limited Common Area.

rules.title: Owners sharing a party structure share repair costs equally
rules.statement: Unless a {{supplemental-declaration}} provides otherwise, the {{owner:plural}} sharing a {{party-structure}} must share the cost of its necessary or appropriate repairs and maintenance equally.

rules.title: Owners sharing a party structure share uninsured restoration costs equally
rules.statement: When an {{owner}} restores a {{party-structure}} destroyed or damaged by fire or other casualty, the other {{owner:plural}} sharing it must contribute equally to the restoration cost that insurance doesn't cover.

rules.title: Association lawsuits need 67 percent of Class A votes
rules.statement: After the Class "B" Control Period, a {{vote}} authorizing the {{organization}} to commence a judicial or administrative proceeding needs the approval of {{members}} holding at least 67 percent of the {{community.total-voting-power}}.

rules.title: Enforcement, collection and some other proceedings need no vote
rules.statement: The {{organization}} may bring an action to enforce the {{governing-documents}}, collect assessments, challenge ad valorem taxes, counterclaim, or sue a contractor or vendor under its contract without a vote of the {{members}}.

rules.title: Amending 14.1 needs 67 percent of Class A votes
rules.statement: An amendment to Section 14.1 needs the approval of {{members}} holding at least 67 percent of the {{community.total-voting-power}}, by the same procedures as approving a proceeding.

rules.title: Claimant gives written Notice of the Claim
rules.statement: A {{claimant}} must notify each {{respondent}} in writing of the {{claim}}, stating plainly and concisely its nature, the Persons involved and the Respondent's role, its legal basis, the proposed remedy, and that the Claimant will meet to discuss resolving it in good faith.

mustState: the nature of the Claim, including the Persons involved and the Respondent's role in it
the legal basis of the Claim: the specific authority out of which it arises
the Claimant's proposed remedy
that the Claimant will meet with the Respondent to discuss in good faith ways to resolve the Claim

rules.title: Submit to mediation within 30 days after negotiations end
rules.statement: If a {{claim}} isn't resolved by the {{dispute.negotiations-terminated-on}}, the {{claimant}} must submit it to mediation within 30 more days, or the Claim is deemed waived.

rules.title: A mediated settlement is written and signed
rules.statement: A settlement of a {{claim}} through mediation must be documented in writing by the mediator and signed by the {{claimant}} and the {{respondent}}.

mustState: the terms on which the Parties settle the Claim

rules.title: No suit on a Claim until mediation ends
rules.statement: A {{claimant}} must not file suit or start administrative proceedings on a {{claim}} until the mediator has issued a Termination of Mediation.

rules.title: Parties meet and confer to negotiate a Claim in good faith
rules.statement: The Parties to a {{claim}} must make every reasonable effort to meet in person and confer to resolve it by good faith negotiation.

check.question: Did each Party make every reasonable effort to meet in person and confer to resolve the Claim by good faith negotiation?

rules.title: Mediate under a King County dispute resolution center or an agreed agency
rules.statement: A {{claimant}} must submit a {{claim}} to mediation under the auspices of a King County dispute resolution center or, if the Parties agree, an independent agency providing dispute resolution services in the area.

rules.title: Appear for mediation, or the Claim is waived
rules.statement: A {{claimant}} who submits a {{claim}} to mediation must appear for the mediation, or is deemed to have waived the Claim, and the {{respondent}} is released from liability to the Claimant on it.

rules.title: Take part in mediation in good faith, or the Claim is waived
rules.statement: A {{claimant}} who submits a {{claim}} to mediation must participate in good faith in the mediation, or is deemed to have waived the Claim, and the {{respondent}} is released from liability to the Claimant on it.

check.question: Did the Claimant participate in good faith in the mediation?

rules.title: Each Party bears its own negotiation and mediation costs
rules.statement: Each Party to a {{claim}} must bear its own costs of negotiation and mediation, including attorneys' fees.

rules.title: Parties share the mediator's fees equally
rules.statement: The Parties to a {{claim}} must share equally all fees charged by the mediator.

rules.title: Suing to enforce an agreed resolution skips the procedures
rules.statement: If a Party fails to abide by a resolution of a {{claim}} agreed through negotiation or mediation, a complying {{bound-party}} may sue to enforce it without repeating the procedures in Section 14.4, and recovers its costs and attorneys' fees.

rules.title: Owners assume the risks of a nearby golf course or Private Amenity
rules.statement: No {{owner}} of a {{lot}} near a golf course or other {{private-amenity}} may hold anyone liable for noise, personal injury, death or property damage caused by the maintenance and operation of the Private Amenity, including the risks listed in 15.3/p1 (a) to (h), whose risk the Owner assumed by buying the Unit.

rules.title: Owners indemnify for claims about proximity to a Private Amenity
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must indemnify and hold the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}} and agents, and the {{organization}} harmless against any {{claim}} by the Owner's visitors, tenants and others on the {{lot}} related to the Unit's proximity to the golf course or another {{private-amenity}}.

rules.title: No liability for a Unit's proximity to a golf course or Private Amenity
rules.statement: No {{owner}} or other {{person}} may hold the {{declarant}}, the {{organization}}, any {{private-amenity-owner}}, or the Declarant's {{affiliate:plural}} or agents liable, including strictly or for their own negligence, for any loss or damage related to a {{lot}}'s proximity to the golf course or another {{private-amenity}}.

rules.title: Private Amenity parking only around its events, when its own parking is short
rules.statement: Members, guests and invitees of a {{private-amenity}} may park on the community's roads only before, during and after tournaments and other member or public functions held by or at it, only to the extent its own parking is insufficient for their vehicles, and subject to applicable parking restriction laws.

rules.title: Private Amenity parking only at reasonable times around its events
rules.statement: Members, guests and invitees of a {{private-amenity}} may park on the community's roads for its tournaments and other member or public functions only at reasonable times before, during and after them.

check.question: Was the vehicle parked at a reasonable time before, during or after the Private Amenity's function?

rules.title: Amendments affecting a Private Amenity need its owner's approval
rules.statement: An amendment to Article 15, or one in derogation of a provision benefiting a {{private-amenity}}, needs the written approval of the affected {{private-amenity-owner}}.

rules.title: Declarant amendments need no Private Amenity approval
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} may amend provisions benefiting a {{private-amenity}} without its owner's approval.

rules.title: Use Restrictions affecting a Private Amenity need its owner's prior written consent
rules.statement: {{use-restrictions}} affecting activities on or use of a {{private-amenity}} need the affected {{private-amenity-owner}}'s prior written consent.

rules.title: The Association reasonably assists the Private Amenities
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must reasonably assist each {{private-amenity}} in upholding the {{community-wide-standard}} as it pertains to maintenance, and the {{residential-design-guidelines}}.

check.question: Has the Association reasonably assisted the Private Amenity in upholding the Community-Wide Standard as it pertains to maintenance, and the Residential Design Guidelines?

rules.title: Each Private Amenity reasonably assists the Association
rules.statement: Each {{private-amenity-owner}} must reasonably assist the {{organization}} in upholding the {{community-wide-standard}} as it pertains to maintenance, and the {{residential-design-guidelines}}.

check.question: Has the Private Amenity owner reasonably assisted the Association in upholding the Community-Wide Standard as it pertains to maintenance, and the Residential Design Guidelines?

rules.title: Notify Eligible Holders of a condemnation loss
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must give each {{eligible-holder}} written notice of any condemnation loss that affects a material portion of the {{community}} or a {{lot}} on which the Eligible Holder holds, insures or guarantees a first {{mortgage}}.

rules.title: Notify Eligible Holders of a casualty loss
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must give each {{eligible-holder}} written notice of any casualty loss that affects a material portion of the {{community}} or a {{lot}} on which the Eligible Holder holds, insures or guarantees a first {{mortgage}}.

rules.title: Notify Eligible Holders of a condemnation loss in time
rules.statement: The written notice the {{organization}} gives each {{eligible-holder}} of a condemnation loss that affects a material portion of the {{community}} or a {{lot}} on which the Eligible Holder holds, insures or guarantees a first {{mortgage}} must be timely.

check.question: Was the Association's written notice to each Eligible Holder of every such condemnation loss timely?

rules.title: Notify Eligible Holders of a casualty loss in time
rules.statement: The written notice the {{organization}} gives each {{eligible-holder}} of a casualty loss that affects a material portion of the {{community}} or a {{lot}} on which the Eligible Holder holds, insures or guarantees a first {{mortgage}} must be timely.

check.question: Was the Association's written notice to each Eligible Holder of every such casualty loss timely?

rules.title: Notify Eligible Holders of 60-day delinquencies
rules.statement: When an {{assessment}} on a {{lot}} with an {{eligible-holder}} has been delinquent for 60 days, the {{organization}} must give the Eligible Holder timely written notice.

check.question: Did the Association give each Eligible Holder of a first Mortgage on the Unit timely written notice of the delinquency?

rules.title: Notify Eligible Holders of violations uncured after 60 days
rules.statement: When a {{violation}} relating to a {{lot}} with an {{eligible-holder}}, or to its {{owner}} or {{occupant}}, isn't cured within 60 days, the {{organization}} must give the Eligible Holder timely written notice.

check.question: Did the Association give each Eligible Holder of a first Mortgage on the Unit timely written notice of the uncured violation?

rules.title: Notify Eligible Holders of a lapse or change in Association insurance
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must give each {{eligible-holder}} written notice of any lapse, cancellation or material modification of an {{insurance-policy}} it maintains.

rules.title: Notify Eligible Holders of a lapse or change in Association insurance in time
rules.statement: The written notice the {{organization}} gives each {{eligible-holder}} of a lapse, cancellation or material modification of an {{insurance-policy}} it maintains must be timely.

check.question: Was the Association's written notice to each Eligible Holder of the policy's lapse, cancellation or material modification timely?

rules.title: Notify Eligible Holders of actions needing their consent
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must give every {{eligible-holder}} timely written notice of a proposed action that needs the consent of a percentage of Eligible Holders.

check.question: Did the Association give every Eligible Holder timely written notice of the proposed action?

rules.title: No Owner priority over a first Mortgagee in Common Area proceeds
rules.statement: In distributing to an {{owner}} insurance proceeds or condemnation awards for losses to or a taking of the {{common-area}}, the {{organization}} must not give the Owner priority over the rights of the first {{mortgagee}} of the Owner's {{lot}}.

rules.title: Owners name their Mortgage holders on request
rules.statement: When the {{organization}} asks, an {{owner}} must furnish the name and address of the holder of each {{mortgage}} on the {{lot}}.

rules.title: A Mortgagee's silence for 30 days is approval
rules.statement: A {{mortgagee}} the {{board}} asks in writing, by certified or registered mail with return receipt requested, to respond to or consent to an action is deemed to have approved it unless the Association receives its written response within 30 days of the request.

rules.title: No objection to changes in use or density of undeveloped property
rules.statement: Every {{person}} who acquires an interest in Trilogy at Redmond Ridge must not protest, challenge or otherwise object to changes in the uses or density of undeveloped property within it.

rules.title: No objection to Master Plan changes for property outside the community
rules.statement: Every {{person}} who acquires an interest in Trilogy at Redmond Ridge must not protest, challenge or otherwise object to changes in the {{master-plan}} as they relate to property outside Trilogy at Redmond Ridge.

rules.title: No liability for inadequate or ineffective security
rules.statement: No one may hold the {{organization}}, the {{declarant}} or its {{affiliate:plural}} liable, including strictly, for any loss or damage by reason of a failure to provide adequate security or the ineffectiveness of security measures undertaken.

rules.title: Owners tell tenants and occupants the Association isn't an insurer
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must inform the {{tenant:plural}} and all {{occupant:plural}} of the {{lot}} that the {{organization}}, its {{board}} and committees, the {{declarant}} and its {{affiliate:plural}} are not insurers, and that each {{person}} using the {{community}} assumes the risk of injury, loss or damage from acts of third parties.

rules.title: Users of the community assume the risk of third parties' acts
rules.statement: No {{person}} using the {{community}} may hold the {{organization}}, its {{board}} and committees, the {{declarant}} or its {{affiliate:plural}} liable as insurers for personal injury or loss of or damage to property, including {{lot:plural}} and their contents, resulting from acts of third parties, whose risks each such Person assumes.

rules.title: No Declarant liability for Community Systems and Services interruptions
rules.statement: No one may hold the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}}, or their successors or assigns liable, including strictly, for any interruption in Community Systems and Services, whether or not it's caused by reasons within the service provider's control.

rules.title: No refund or offset in fees for Community Systems and Services interruptions
rules.statement: No user of Community Systems and Services may claim a refund, rebate, discount or offset in applicable fees for any interruption in them, whether or not it's caused by reasons within the service provider's control.

rules.title: Owners indemnify for claims about proximity to natural areas
rules.statement: Each {{owner}} must indemnify and hold the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}} and agents, and the {{organization}} harmless against any {{claim}} by the Owner's visitors, tenants and others on the {{lot}} related to the Unit's proximity to the natural areas.

rules.title: Owners, tenants and residents assume the risk of indigenous animals
rules.statement: No {{owner}}, {{tenant}} or {{occupant}}, nor their families, invitees or licensees, may hold anyone liable for the presence of, or danger from, animals indigenous to the area, whose risk they assume.

rules.title: No liability for a Unit's proximity to the natural areas
rules.statement: No {{owner}} or other {{person}} may hold the {{declarant}}, the {{organization}}, or the Declarant's {{affiliate:plural}} or agents liable, including strictly or for their own negligence, for any loss or damage related to a {{lot}}'s proximity to the natural areas.

rules.title: Owners, tenants and residents assume the risks of the Bodies of Water
rules.statement: No {{owner}}, {{tenant}} or {{occupant}}, nor their families, invitees or licensees, may hold anyone liable for the nuisance, inconvenience, disturbance, damage or possible injury to persons that 17.6 says the {{body-of-water}} may cause, whose risks they assume.

rules.title: No liability for the existence of the Bodies of Water
rules.statement: No {{owner}}, {{tenant}} or {{occupant}}, nor their families, invitees or licensees, may hold the {{declarant}}, its {{affiliate:plural}}, the {{organization}}, or any director, {{officer}}, agent or employee of the Association liable for claims or damages resulting, directly or indirectly, from the existence of the {{body-of-water}}.

rules.title: No personal liability of the Declarant beyond its interest in the community
rules.statement: No one may hold the {{declarant}} (or an assignee of its interest), or any {{affiliate}}, partner, officer, director or shareholder of the Declarant, personally liable under or in connection with the {{declaration}} or the {{organization}}, except the Declarant to the extent of its interest in the {{community}}; and no execution on a judgment may be sought against, or become a lien on, the judgment debtor's other assets.

rules.title: Notify the Board 7 days before a transfer
rules.statement: An {{owner}} other than the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} must give the {{board}} written notice of a {{title-transfer}} at least 7 days before title transfers.

rules.title: The transfer notice names the buyer and the date
rules.statement: The {{transfer-notice}} must state the name and address of the purchaser or transferee, the date of the transfer, and other information the {{board}} reasonably requires.

mustState: the name and address of the purchaser or transferee
the date of the transfer of title

rules.title: The new Owner confirms the information within 7 days
rules.statement: Within 7 days of taking title, the new {{owner}} must confirm that the information the transferor gave the {{board}} is complete and accurate.

rules.title: Give TRRS new Owners' contact information on request
rules.statement: When {{trrs}} asks, the {{organization}} must give it the name, address, telephone number and e-mail address of each new {{owner}} and the forwarding address of the former Owner.

rules.title: A transferor stays liable until the Board receives the transfer notice
rules.statement: After a transfer of title, the {{transferor}} remains jointly and severally responsible with the transferee for all obligations of the {{owner}} of the {{lot}}, assessments included, until the date the {{board}} receives the {{transfer-notice}}.

rules.title: Conveying Common Area under threat of condemnation needs 67 percent
rules.statement: The {{board}}'s conveyance of {{common-area}} in lieu of and under threat of condemnation needs the written direction of {{members}} holding at least 67 percent of the {{community.total-voting-power}}.

rules.title: Conveying Common Area under threat of condemnation needs the Declarant
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibit A or B, conveying {{common-area}} in lieu of condemnation also needs the Declarant's written direction.

rules.title: Owners notified in writing of a taking before the award is disbursed
rules.statement: The {{organization}} must give each {{owner}} written notice of a taking of {{common-area}}, or its conveyance in lieu of condemnation, before disbursing any award or proceeds from it.

rules.title: Not restoring taken improvements needs 67 percent
rules.statement: An agreement not to restore improvements on taken {{common-area}} needs {{members}} holding at least 67 percent of the {{community.total-voting-power}}; otherwise the {{organization}} restores them.

rules.title: Not restoring taken improvements needs the Declarant
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibit A or B, an agreement not to restore improvements on taken {{common-area}} also needs the Declarant's agreement.

rules.title: Decide not to restore within 60 days of the taking
rules.statement: An agreement not to restore improvements on taken {{common-area}} needs to be reached within 60 days after the taking.

rules.title: Association restores improvements on taken Common Area
rules.statement: When a taking of {{common-area}} involves improvements, the {{organization}} must restore or replace them on the remaining Common Area to the extent available, unless the {{declarant}} and the {{members}} agree otherwise within 60 days.

check.question: Has the Association restored or replaced the improvements on the taken Common Area on the remaining Common Area, to the extent land is available?

rules.title: Restoration follows Board-approved plans
rules.statement: Restoring or replacing improvements on taken {{common-area}} must follow {{plans}} the {{board}} approved.

rules.title: No partition suit without every Owner's and Mortgagee's written consent
rules.statement: No one may bring an action to partition any portion of the {{common-area}} without the prior written consent of all {{owner:plural}} and {{mortgagee:plural}}.

rules.title: Declarant conveys Common Area within a year
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} or its {{affiliate:plural}} must convey each {{common-area}} to the {{organization}} within one year after the improvements on it are completed.

rules.title: The Common Area includes an 11.5-acre park
rules.statement: The {{common-area}} must include a community park totaling at least 11.5 acres.

rules.title: Common Area may go to a government without an Owner vote
rules.statement: The {{organization}} may transfer, dedicate or grant easements over portions of the {{common-area}} to {{king-county}} or another {{governmental-entity}} without a vote of the {{owner:plural}}.

rules.title: Declarant may amend for any purpose before the first sale
rules.statement: Until a {{lot}} is first conveyed to a Person other than an {{affiliate}} or a {{builder}}, the {{declarant}} may amend the {{declaration}} alone, for any purpose.

rules.title: Declarant may make amendments that law or lenders require
rules.statement: The {{declarant}} may amend the {{declaration}} alone when the amendment is necessary to comply with law, to enable title insurance, to enable mortgage lenders, purchasers, insurers or guarantors to deal in mortgage loans on the Units, or to satisfy a governmental agency.

rules.title: Required amendments can't impair title without consent
rules.statement: A {{declarant}} amendment made for a required purpose after the first sale that adversely affects the title to a {{lot}} needs its {{owner}}'s written consent.

rules.title: No unilateral amendment impairs title without consent
rules.statement: An amendment the {{declarant}} makes alone under 20.1's first paragraph that adversely affects the title to a {{lot}} needs its {{owner}}'s written consent.

rules.title: Declarant may amend for any purpose while it owns property
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibit A or B for development, the Declarant may amend the {{declaration}} alone for any other purpose.

rules.title: Declarant amendments with a material adverse effect need the Owner's consent
rules.statement: An amendment the {{declarant}} makes alone for any other purpose that has a material adverse effect on a right of an {{owner}} needs that Owner's written consent.

rules.title: Amendments need 67 percent of all Class A votes
rules.statement: An amendment to the {{declaration}} needs the affirmative vote or written consent of {{members}} holding at least 67 percent of the {{community.total-voting-power}}, not just of the votes cast.

rules.title: Amendments need 67 percent of non-Declarant Class A votes
rules.statement: An amendment to the {{declaration}} also needs at least 67 percent of the {{community.non-declarant-votes}}.

rules.title: Amendments need the Declarant's consent while it owns property
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibit A or B, an amendment to the {{declaration}} also needs the Declarant's consent.

rules.title: Amending a clause needs at least the clause's own percentage
rules.statement: An amendment to a clause needs at least the percentage of affirmative votes that the clause requires for action under it, counted against the {{community.total-voting-power}}.

rules.title: Changing the Declarant's rights needs its written consent
rules.statement: An amendment that removes, revokes or modifies a right or privilege of the {{declarant}} needs the Declarant's written consent.

rules.title: Changing the Class "B" Member's rights needs its written consent
rules.statement: An amendment that removes, revokes or modifies a right or privilege of the {{class-b-member}} needs the written consent of the Class "B" Member or of the {{class-b-rights-assignee}}.

rules.title: Changing a UPD Permit condition needs King County
rules.statement: An amendment that removes, revokes, modifies or contravenes a {{upd-permit}} condition or requirement needs the express approval of {{king-county}}.

rules.title: Challenge an amendment's adoption within six months
rules.statement: A procedural challenge to an amendment needs to be made within six months after the amendment is Recorded, or the amendment is presumed validly adopted.

rules.title: Termination needs 67 percent of all Class A votes
rules.statement: Terminating the {{declaration}} needs the affirmative vote or written consent of {{owner:plural}} holding at least 67 percent of the {{community.total-voting-power}}.

rules.title: Termination needs 67 percent of non-Declarant Class A votes
rules.statement: Terminating the {{declaration}} also needs at least 67 percent of the {{community.non-declarant-votes}}.

rules.title: Termination needs the Declarant's consent while it owns property
rules.statement: While the {{declarant}} or an {{affiliate}} owns property in Exhibit A or B, terminating the {{declaration}} also needs the Declarant's consent.

rules.title: Termination needs first Mortgagees of Units with 67 percent of all votes
rules.statement: Terminating the {{declaration}} also needs the approval of the holders of first {{mortgage:plural}} on Units whose {{owner:plural}} hold at least 67 percent of the {{community.total-voting-power}}.

rules.title: Termination needs 67 percent of first Mortgagees, by their Units' votes
rules.statement: Terminating the {{declaration}} also needs the approval of first {{mortgagee:plural}} on Units holding at least 67 percent of the {{community.mortgaged-unit-votes}}.

rules.title: Board Records a signed Certificate of Termination
rules.statement: Once terminating the {{declaration}} has the votes and consents it needs, the {{board}} must Record a {{certificate-of-termination}} signed by the President or Vice President and attested by the Secretary or Assistant Secretary, with their signatures acknowledged.

mustState: an acknowledgment of the signatures of the officers who signed and attested it

rules.title: Exterior changes need DRC approval before work begins
rules.statement: Any {{work}} that changes the exterior of a {{lot}} needs the {{committee}}'s approval, on a written {{application-form}}, before it begins, unless the guidelines note otherwise; a change the guidelines don't cover, or one where it's doubtful how to comply, still needs it.

rules.title: COMPLIANCE ONLY work needs no pre-approval
rules.statement: {{work}} under a guideline noted COMPLIANCE ONLY must comply with it but doesn't need the {{committee}}'s pre-approval.

rules.title: A PROHIBITED guideline can't be approved away
rules.statement: The {{committee}} must not approve {{work}} that deviates from a guideline noted PROHIBITED; such a condition may not be violated.

rules.title: Consult the neighbors the work may affect
rules.statement: An {{owner}} should consult any {{neighbor}} who may be affected by the {{work}} they intend to perform.

rules.title: Disclose the change to neighbors when the Reviewer requires
rules.statement: When the {{committee}} requires it, the proposed change must be disclosed to the affected {{neighbor:plural}}.

rules.title: Applications generally reviewed within 30 days
rules.statement: In general, the {{committee}} reviews an {{architectural-application}} within 30 days of receiving it.

rules.title: Applications are reviewed only once complete
rules.statement: An {{architectural-application}} must be complete before the {{committee}} reviews it.

check.question: Is the application complete, with every item the guidelines require for the proposed Work?

rules.title: Owner notified of an approval within 5 business days
rules.statement: When an {{architectural-application}} is approved, the {{organization}} must notify the {{owner}} in writing within 5 business days.

rules.title: Disapproval delivered within 5 business days
rules.statement: When the DRC disapproves an {{architectural-application}}, {{managing-agent}} must deliver the notification to the {{applicant}} within five business days.

rules.title: Disapproval delivered by hand, mail or electronic transmission
rules.statement: {{managing-agent}} must deliver the notification of a disapproval by hand, mail, or electronic transmission, including facsimile or electronic mail.

rules.title: A disapproval notice explains the appeal
rules.statement: The notification of a disapproval must include the instructions, required dates and times, and forms, if any, needed for the appeal, which {{managing-agent}} develops.

mustState: The instructions needed for the appeal
The required dates and times for the appeal
The forms needed for the appeal, if any

rules.title: Owners obtain King County and other outside permits and approvals
rules.statement: The {{owner}} is solely responsible for the permits, approvals and requirements of {{king-county}} and other jurisdictions outside the {{organization}} that the {{work}} needs.

rules.title: Applications must not propose what may violate other documents or law
rules.statement: An {{architectural-application}} must not propose anything that, in the {{committee}}'s determination, may violate the community's other Governing Documents or applicable laws or regulations, since the Reviewer has no authority to approve it; approval doesn't assure compliance with King County Code.

check.question: Is the application free of anything that, in the Reviewer's determination, may violate the community's other Governing Documents or applicable laws or regulations?

rules.title: Final approval waits for King County where its approval appears needed
rules.statement: When the {{committee}} determines an {{architectural-application}} appears to require a {{king-county}} approved variance or permit, it's reviewed for architectural value only and held; final approval, and the start of the project, wait for {{king-county}}'s approval or guidance that it isn't required.

rules.title: Submissions should include photos
rules.statement: An {{owner}}'s submission should include {{photo:plural}}.

rules.title: Plans and drawings accurate
rules.statement: The {{plans}} and drawings an {{owner}} submits must be accurate in all their information, such as the location of the {{lot}}'s boundaries, easements and drainage as shown on the recorded plot plan or another instrument.

check.question: Is all the information in the plans and drawings accurate, including the location of the Unit's boundaries, easements and drainage as shown on the recorded plot plan or any other instrument?

rules.title: Owner advised in writing before an inspection
rules.statement: The {{organization}} may inspect the {{work}} before, during and after construction, and must advise the {{owner}} in writing before it does.

rules.title: Impervious surface calculations with work that adds impervious surface
rules.statement: An application for {{work}} that adds to the impervious surface of a {{lot}} must include {{impervious-surface-calculation:plural}}.

rules.title: Impervious coverage at most 74 or 62 percent by Unit type (should)
rules.statement: A {{lot}}'s {{lot.impervious-coverage}} should be at most 74 percent for a Lakes or Port Collection {{lot.unit-type}}, and at most 62 percent for an Island, Forest or Estate Collection {{lot.unit-type}}.

rules.title: Impervious coverage at most 74 or 62 percent by Unit type (required)
rules.statement: A {{lot}}'s {{lot.impervious-coverage}} must be at most 74 percent for a Lakes or Port Collection {{lot.unit-type}}, and at most 62 percent for an Island, Forest or Estate Collection {{lot.unit-type}}.

rules.title: Reviewer may change the coverage percentages
rules.statement: The {{committee}} may increase or decrease the maximum {{lot.impervious-coverage}} for a {{lot}}.

rules.title: The Board decides variances from shall and shall-not guidelines
rules.statement: Deviating from a guideline that says shall or shall not needs a variance, and the {{board}}, as Reviewer for variances, decides it: the DRC may request one it believes justified, or deny the request itself. The homeowner may appeal a DRC decision to the {{board}}.

rules.title: Reviewer may waive or vary any procedure or standard
rules.statement: The {{committee}} may, at its sole discretion, waive or vary any procedure or standard in the guidelines; its approval doesn't relieve the {{applicant}} of governmental requirements.

rules.title: Reviewer may waive or vary the review procedures
rules.statement: The {{committee}} may, at its sole discretion, waive or vary the review procedures of Article 3; a guideline that says shall or shall not needs a variance from the {{board}} instead.

rules.title: Consult the Association Staff about a fence
rules.statement: An {{owner}} planning a {{fence-run}} should consult the {{association-staff}}.

rules.title: Like-for-like fence replacements need DRC approval
rules.statement: Replacing a {{fence-run}} on a like for like basis needs the {{committee}}'s approval; the approval doesn't assure compliance with King County Code.

rules.title: Like-for-like gate replacements need DRC approval
rules.statement: Replacing a {{gate}} on a like for like basis needs the {{committee}}'s approval.

rules.title: Wood fences: vertical boards, horizontal rails and post caps
rules.statement: A wood {{fence-run}} must consist of vertical boards, horizontal rails and post caps; horizontal boards aren't permitted.

rules.title: Wood gates: vertical boards, horizontal rails and post caps
rules.statement: A wood {{gate}} must consist of vertical boards, horizontal rails and post caps.

rules.title: No tall, consecutive lattice sections as wood fencing
rules.statement: Tall, consecutive sections of lattice must not be used as a material or style for a wood {{fence-run}}.

check.question: Is the wood fence free of tall, consecutive sections of lattice used as its material or style?

rules.title: Wood fences in an approved style
rules.statement: A wood {{fence-run}} must be one of the approved wood fence styles of Exhibits K, L and M: {{fence-style.wood-tall-solid}}, {{fence-style.wood-low-open}} or {{fence-style.wood-low-open-scallop}}.

rules.title: Composite fences in K style
rules.statement: A composite {{fence-run}} should be {{fence-style.k-style}}.

rules.title: Composite fences in the Exhibit K style
rules.statement: A composite {{fence-run}} should be in the style of Exhibit K, {{fence-style.wood-tall-solid}}.

rules.title: Other composite styles case by case
rules.statement: The {{committee}} may consider other styles of composite {{fence-run}} case by case.

rules.title: Metal fences: 2-rail or 3-rail open metal view
rules.statement: A metal {{fence-run}} must be 2-rail or 3-rail open metal view fencing, or 3-rail with closer pickets in the bottom half, as Exhibit N shows; no other alternatives will be considered.

rules.title: Metal fence pickets at most 4 inches apart
rules.statement: A metal {{fence-run}} must have a {{fence-run.picket-spacing}} of at most 4 inches.

rules.title: Metal gates: 2-rail or 3-rail open metal view
rules.statement: A metal {{gate}} must be 2-rail or 3-rail open metal view, or 3-rail with closer pickets in the bottom half; no other alternatives will be considered.

rules.title: Metal gate pickets at most 4 inches apart
rules.statement: A metal {{gate}} must have a {{gate.picket-spacing}} of at most 4 inches.

rules.title: No invisible underground fences
rules.statement: An {{fence-style.invisible-underground}} isn't permitted.

rules.title: No horizontal style fences
rules.statement: A {{fence-style.horizontal}} {{fence-run}} isn't permitted.

rules.title: Wood, composite or open metal view fences only
rules.statement: A {{fence-run}} enclosing a yard or creating privacy must be wood, composite or open metal view fencing; no other material, including vinyl, is permitted.

rules.title: Wood fence posts, stringers and K-Banding of cedar or pressure-treated wood
rules.statement: A wood {{fence-run}}'s posts, stringers and K-Banding must be cedar or pressure-treated material.

rules.title: Composite fences built to the manufacturer's guidelines
rules.statement: A composite {{fence-run}}, including its posts, must be built to the {{product-specification}}.

check.question: Is the composite fence, including its posts, built to the manufacturer's recommended construction guidelines?

rules.title: Composite fences from an approved manufacturer
rules.statement: A composite {{fence-run}} must come from Trex, Frame It All or Neoline.

rules.title: Other composite manufacturers case by case
rules.statement: The {{committee}} may consider a composite {{fence-run}} from another {{fence-run.manufacturer}} case by case.

rules.title: Metal fences of fabricated tubular metal, black powder coated
rules.statement: An open metal view {{fence-run}} must be constructed of fabricated tubular metal with a {{fence-coating.black-powder-coat}} finish.

rules.title: New and replacement wood fences stained
rules.statement: All above grade portions of a newly installed or replacement wood {{fence-run}} must be stained.

rules.title: Replaced wood fence sections match the rest
rules.statement: When only some sections of a wood {{fence-run}} are replaced, they must match the other sections for uniformity.

check.question: Do the replaced fence sections match the fence's other sections?

rules.title: Wood fences in solid or semi-transparent stain
rules.statement: A wood {{fence-run}}, when stained or re-stained, must use a solid or semi-transparent stain; transparent stains aren't allowed.

rules.title: Wood fence stain colors by manufacturer
rules.statement: A wood {{fence-run}} must be stained, or re-stained, in one of these colors from its {{fence-run.stain-brand}}: Behr Cedar (SC-146) or Drift Gray (SC-137); Benjamin Moore Natural Cedar tone (ES-45) or Alexandria Beige (HC-77); Sherwin Williams Cedar (SW-3034) or Kings Canyon (SW-3026).

rules.title: Other brown and grey stains case by case
rules.statement: The {{committee}} may consider other brown and grey tones for a wood {{fence-run}} case by case.

rules.title: A sample of an unlisted stain color
rules.statement: An application for a wood {{fence-run}} in another brown or grey tone must include a {{color-sample}}.

rules.title: A picture of the house with an unlisted stain color
rules.statement: An application for a wood {{fence-run}} in another brown or grey tone must include a {{photo}} of the house.

mustState: Shows the house

rules.title: The wood treatment identified on the application
rules.statement: The application for a wood {{fence-run}} must identify the specific wood treatment.

mustState: Identifies the specific wood treatment for the fence

rules.title: Wood fences stained on both sides
rules.statement: A wood {{fence-run}} must be stained on both sides.

rules.title: Lattice and arbors on a wood fence match its color
rules.statement: Any lattice or arbor on a wood {{fence-run}} must match the fence's {{fence-run.stain-color}}.

rules.title: Gates on a wood fence match its color
rules.statement: A {{gate}} on a wood {{fence-run}} must match the fence's {{fence-run.stain-color}}.

rules.title: Composite colors by manufacturer
rules.statement: A composite {{fence-run}} must use a {{fence-run.color}} its {{fence-run.manufacturer}} offers on this list: Trex in Winchester Grey or Saddle, Frame It All in River Birch or Teak, Neoline in Honey Oak or Desert Sage.

rules.title: The composite color identified on the application
rules.statement: The application for a composite {{fence-run}} must identify its specific {{fence-run.color}}.

mustState: Identifies the specific color of the composite fence

rules.title: Lattice and arbors on a composite fence match its material and color
rules.statement: Any lattice or arbor on a composite {{fence-run}} must match the fence's {{fence-run.material}} and {{fence-run.color}}.

rules.title: Gates match a composite fence's material
rules.statement: A {{gate}} on a composite {{fence-run}} must match the fence's {{fence-run.material}}.

rules.title: Gates match a composite fence's color
rules.statement: A {{gate}} on a composite {{fence-run}} must match the fence's {{fence-run.color}}.

rules.title: Posts match a composite fence's color
rules.statement: A composite {{fence-run}}'s {{fence-run.post-color}} must match its {{fence-run.color}}.

rules.title: Metal fences in flat black powder coat
rules.statement: An open metal view {{fence-run}} must have a {{fence-coating.flat-black-powder-coat}} finish.

rules.title: Boundary and return fences at most 72 inches
rules.statement: A wood or composite {{fence-run}} on or along a {{lot}} boundary line, or a {{return-fence}}, must have a {{fence-run.height}} of at most 72 inches (6 feet).

rules.title: Wood and composite fences at least 40 inches
rules.statement: A wood or composite {{fence-run}} must have a {{fence-run.height}} of at least 40 inches.

rules.title: Every fence at least 40 inches
rules.statement: Any {{fence-run}} on a {{lot}} must have a {{fence-run.height}} of at least 40 inches.

rules.title: Lattice at most 18 inches
rules.statement: The lattice on any {{fence-run}} must have a {{fence-run.lattice-height}} of at most 18 inches.

rules.title: Fence plus lattice at most 90 inches
rules.statement: A {{fence-run}}'s {{fence-run.height}} plus its {{fence-run.lattice-height}} must be at most 90 inches (7½ feet).

rules.title: Only standard 2-inch square or diagonal lattice
rules.statement: Lattice on a {{fence-run}} must be standard 2-inch diagonal or square lattice, the styles of Exhibit O.

rules.title: Fence, lattice and arbor at most 96 inches
rules.statement: A {{fence-run}} with an arbor on top must have a {{fence-run.height}}, {{fence-run.lattice-height}} and {{fence-run.arbor-height}} totaling at most 96 inches (8 feet).

rules.title: Metal boundary fences 4 to 6 feet
rules.statement: A metal {{fence-run}} on or along a {{lot}} boundary, including one shared with the golf course, must have a {{fence-run.height}} between 4 feet and 6 feet.

rules.title: Metal height variations considered
rules.statement: The {{committee}} may consider variations from the metal fence height for specific circumstances.

rules.title: Side and rear boundary fences on the line or just inside it
rules.statement: A side or rear yard {{boundary-fence}} must be placed either on the boundary line that separates it from a neighboring {{lot}} or Common Area, or along the boundary line but totally within the {{lot}}.

rules.title: Neighbor approval for fences on a shared boundary
rules.statement: A side or rear yard {{fence-run}} on the boundary line with a neighboring {{lot}}, or attached to a fence on another {{lot}}, needs the {{neighbor}}'s approval in the {{application-form}}, approving its placement, height and materials and agreeing that it's a party structure the {{owner}} will partly maintain and repair.

mustState: The neighboring Unit Owner approves the placement and height of the fence and the materials to be used

The neighboring Unit Owner understands and agrees that the fence constitutes a party structure as described in Declaration 13.1 and that the Owner will be responsible for maintenance and repair of a portion of the fence

rules.title: Neighbor agrees to joint maintenance of an attached fence
rules.statement: A {{fence-run}} that attaches to a fence on another {{lot}} needs the {{neighbor}}'s agreement that it will attach to the existing fence and may require joint maintenance among the Owners.

mustState: The neighboring Unit Owner understands and agrees that the new fence will attach to an existing fence and may require joint maintenance responsibility among the Owners

rules.title: Neighbor agrees to joint maintenance for every shared-boundary fence
rules.statement: Every {{fence-run}} that needs the {{neighbor}}'s approval also needs the neighbor's agreement that it will attach to the existing fence and may require joint maintenance among the Owners.

mustState: The neighboring Unit Owner understands and agrees that the new fence will attach to an existing fence and may require joint maintenance responsibility among the Owners

rules.title: Non-Boundary Line Fences entirely within the Unit
rules.statement: When a neighbor doesn't approve a fence on the boundary line, the {{owner}} may build it alongside the boundary line as a {{non-boundary-line-fence}}, all of whose elements must be entirely within the {{owner}}'s {{lot}}.

rules.title: A Non-Boundary Line Fence's packet stipulations
rules.statement: The {{application-form}} for a {{non-boundary-line-fence}} must stipulate that the fence isn't a party structure and that the {{owner}} will maintain and repair both sides of it.

mustState: The fence is not a "party structure" as described in Declaration 13.1
The Owner will be responsible for maintenance and repair of both sides of the fence

rules.title: Front yard fences compatible with the streetscape
rules.statement: A front yard {{fence-run}} must be compatible with the overall appearance of the streetscape.

check.question: Is the front yard fence compatible with the overall appearance of the streetscape?

rules.title: Front yard fences consider curved streetscapes
rules.statement: A front yard {{fence-run}}'s placement should consider curved streetscapes and other aesthetic details.

check.question: Does the front yard fence's placement take account of curved streetscapes and other aesthetic details?

rules.title: Front yard fences keep drivers' view clear
rules.statement: A front yard {{fence-run}} must not interfere with a driver's ability to see objects in the roadway.

check.question: Does the fence leave a driver a clear view of objects in the roadway?

rules.title: Front and return fences set back 5 feet
rules.statement: A front yard {{fence-run}}, or one between a side yard fence and the house, should be placed no less than 5 feet behind the nearest front corner of the house.

rules.title: Other setbacks for windows and utilities, case by case
rules.statement: Windows and utilities may require other setbacks for a front or return {{fence-run}}, and the {{committee}} considers others case by case.

rules.title: Association-maintained areas stay accessible
rules.statement: Any areas the {{organization}} maintains should remain accessible with a front yard {{fence-run}} in place.

check.question: Do the areas the Association maintains remain accessible with the fence in place?

rules.title: Open metal view fences on the golf course boundary
rules.statement: A {{fence-run}} on or along a boundary line between a {{lot}} and the golf course must be an open metal view fence.

rules.title: Side yard fences open metal view for 10 feet from the golf course
rules.statement: A side yard {{fence-run}} on a {{lot}} that abuts the golf course must be open metal view fencing from the point where the {{lot}} abuts the golf course to at least 10 feet from the golf course boundary; the {{committee}} may require a greater distance for view corridors.

rules.title: Owners verify Unit boundary lines before building a fence
rules.statement: Before building a {{fence-run}}, the {{owner:plural}} building it are solely responsible for verifying the location of the {{lot}}'s boundary lines.

rules.title: No fence in a utility easement where a recorded plat or document prohibits it
rules.statement: An {{owner}} may build a {{fence-run}} within a utility {{easement}} only where no recorded plat or other recorded document prohibits it.

rules.title: Owners pay for removing a fence a utility needs out of its easement
rules.statement: If a utility company requires a {{fence-run}} within a utility {{easement}} to be removed or altered to exercise its rights under the easement, the removal or alteration is at the {{owner}}'s sole expense.

rules.title: Examine plot plans for sight line restrictions
rules.statement: Before building a {{fence-run}}, the {{owner}} should examine the plot plans for driver or pedestrian sight line restrictions.

check.question: Did the Owner examine the plot plans for driver or pedestrian sight line restrictions?

rules.title: No adverse impact on driver visibility
rules.statement: A proposed {{fence-run}} must not adversely affect driver visibility; an adverse impact may require changing the application or lead to its denial.

check.question: Does the proposed fence avoid an adverse impact on driver visibility?

rules.title: Gates coordinate with the adjacent wood or composite fence
rules.statement: A {{gate}} on a wood or composite {{fence-run}} must coordinate with the adjacent fence type.

check.question: Does the gate coordinate with the type of the adjacent fence?

rules.title: Gates on wood or composite fences about as tall as the fence
rules.statement: A {{gate}} on a wood or composite {{fence-run}} must be substantially the same height as the adjoining fence.

check.question: Is the gate substantially the same height as the adjoining fence?

rules.title: Wood or composite gates at most 90 inches with lattice
rules.statement: A wood or composite {{gate}} without an arbor, with any lattice on top, must have a total height of at most 7.5 feet (90 inches).

rules.title: Wood or composite gates with an arbor at most 96 inches
rules.statement: A wood or composite {{gate}} with an arbor on top must have a total height of no more than 8 feet (96 inches).

rules.title: Gates on metal fences match the fence's material and color
rules.statement: A {{gate}} on a metal {{fence-run}} must match the fence's {{fence-run.material}} and {{fence-run.coating}}.

rules.title: Gates on metal fences about as tall as the fence
rules.statement: A {{gate}} on a metal {{fence-run}} must be substantially the same height as the adjoining fence.

check.question: Is the gate substantially the same height as the adjoining fence?

rules.title: Courtyard entry gates of open view metal
rules.statement: A front courtyard entry {{gate}} must be Open View Metal fencing (Exhibit N).

rules.title: Other metal courtyard gates reviewed individually
rules.statement: The {{committee}} reviews other metal options for a front courtyard entry {{gate}} on an individual basis.

rules.title: Courtyard gates suited to the home's style
rules.statement: A front courtyard entry {{gate}}'s size and style are considered in relation to the style of the home.

check.question: Are the courtyard gate's size and style suited to the style of the home?

rules.title: No new gates in fences between a Unit and Common Area
rules.statement: An {{owner}} must not alter a fence between a {{lot}} and Common Area to install a {{gate}}.

rules.title: Screens not on a property line
rules.statement: A {{screen}} must not be on a property line.

rules.title: Screens approved by the Association Staff or the DRC before applying
rules.statement: An {{owner}} must get the approval of the {{association-staff}} or the {{committee}} for a {{screen}} before submitting a proposal and application.

rules.title: Screens of wood, composite or metal
rules.statement: A {{screen}} must be constructed with wood, composite or metal materials.

rules.title: Screen colors follow the fence color guidelines
rules.statement: A {{screen}}'s colors must follow the fence color guidelines of Article 5.4.

check.question: Do the screen's colors follow the fence color guidelines of Article 5.4 for its material?

rules.title: Screens at most 16 feet long and 8 feet tall
rules.statement: A {{screen}} must be at most 16 feet in {{screen.length}} and 8 feet in {{screen.height}}.

rules.title: Screen size exceptions considered
rules.statement: The DRC must consider exceptions to a {{screen}}'s maximum length and height based on the {{lot}}, the size of the house or surrounding properties.

rules.title: Horizontal screen planks only under 16 feet
rules.statement: A wood or composite {{screen}} may use horizontal planks only if it's under 16 feet in {{screen.length}}; beyond 16 feet it must use vertical planks.

rules.title: Garbage cans screened from view
rules.statement: Garbage cans must be screened by fencing or landscaping so they aren't visible from neighbors, the street or the golf course.

check.question: Are the garbage cans screened by fencing or landscaping so they aren't visible from neighbors, the street or the golf course?

rules.title: Utility screens not forward of the house's front corner
rules.statement: A {{utility-screen}} must not be placed forward of the front corner of the house on a typical {{lot}}.

rules.title: Exceptions where the house's placement is a unique challenge
rules.statement: The {{committee}} may consider exceptions where the placement of the house on a {{lot}} poses a unique challenge.

rules.title: Total concealment from the street from all angles
rules.statement: A {{utility-screen}}, shrubbery included, must totally conceal what it screens from the street view, from all angles.

check.question: Does the screening totally conceal the equipment from the street view, from all angles?

rules.title: Wooden utility screens stained to Article 5.4 or the house body color
rules.statement: A small wooden {{utility-screen}} must be stained with a stain that complies with Article 5.4, or a solid or semi-transparent color that matches the body color of the house.

rules.title: Wooden utility screens may be stained to Article 5.4 or the house body color
rules.statement: A small wooden {{utility-screen}} may be stained with a stain that complies with Article 5.4, or a solid or semi-transparent color that matches the body color of the house; metal and composite materials will be considered.

rules.title: Screening devices compatible with the home
rules.statement: A {{utility-screen}}'s materials and design must be compatible with the home.

check.question: Are the screening device's materials and design compatible with the home?

rules.title: No screening around public utilities
rules.statement: Screening around {{screened-equipment.public-utility}} is prohibited.

rules.title: Detached structures and gazebos need approval
rules.statement: A {{detached-structure}} or gazebo needs the {{committee}}'s approval; approval doesn't assure compliance with King County Codes.

rules.title: Meet the Association Staff before applying
rules.statement: Before applying for a {{detached-structure}}, the {{owner}} should meet with the {{association-staff}}, and research King County codes.

rules.title: Structures compatible with the residence and conservative
rules.statement: A proposed {{detached-structure}} must be compatible with the materials and color of the {{residence}} and be conservative in color, design and scale.

check.question: Is the structure compatible with the materials and color of the residence, and conservative in color, design and scale?

rules.title: Plans showing a structure's materials, colors, dimensions and elevations
rules.statement: An application for a {{detached-structure}} must include {{plans}} showing its materials, colors, dimensions and elevations.

mustState: The structure's materials
The structure's colors
The structure's dimensions
The structure's elevations

rules.title: A site plan locating the structure
rules.statement: An application for a {{detached-structure}} must include a {{site-plan}} showing its location and its distances to any boundary lines and other structures on the property.

mustState: The location of the structure
The distances to any boundary lines
The distances to other structures on the property

rules.title: Structure materials and design compatible with the home
rules.statement: A {{detached-structure}}'s materials and design should be compatible with the home.

check.question: Are the structure's materials and design compatible with the home?

rules.title: Examples of the proposed material
rules.statement: An application for a {{detached-structure}} should include a {{material-sample}}; one is usually required.

rules.title: Wood preferred for structures
rules.statement: A {{detached-structure}} should be wood.

rules.title: Other structure materials considered
rules.statement: The {{committee}} will consider other materials for a {{detached-structure}}.

rules.title: No solid walls on structures
rules.statement: A {{detached-structure}} must not have solid walls, including glass; screening will be considered.

rules.title: Screened walls on structures considered
rules.statement: The {{committee}} considers case by case a {{detached-structure}} whose walls are enclosed with screening.

rules.title: Patios, porches and decks within the impervious coverage maximum
rules.statement: A {{outdoor-living-area}} must not take its {{lot}}'s {{lot.impervious-coverage}} over the maximum for its {{lot.unit-type}}: 74 percent for a Lakes or Port Collection, 62 percent for an Island, Forest or Estate Collection.

rules.title: Decks not anchored in the wall easement
rules.statement: A {{deck}} that extends into the 5-foot easement from an engineered wall should avoid anchoring within the easement area.

rules.title: Decks cantilevered over the wall easement
rules.statement: A {{deck}} within the 5-foot easement from an engineered wall should cantilever over the easement area.

rules.title: Patio and deck covers compatible with the residence
rules.statement: A {{patio-cover}} attached to a {{residence}} must be compatible with the materials and colors of the {{residence}}.

check.question: Is the patio or deck cover compatible with the materials and colors of the residence?

rules.title: Patio and deck covers conservative in color, design and scale
rules.statement: A {{patio-cover}} should be conservative in color, design and scale.

check.question: Is the patio or deck cover conservative in color, design and scale?

rules.title: Plans showing a cover's materials, colors and elevations
rules.statement: An application for a {{patio-cover}} must include {{plans}} showing its materials, colors and elevations.

mustState: The cover's materials
The cover's colors
The cover's elevations

rules.title: A site plan locating the cover
rules.statement: An application for a {{patio-cover}} must include a {{site-plan}} showing its location and distances to the {{lot}}'s boundary lines and other structures on the {{lot}}.

mustState: The location of the patio or deck cover
The distances to the Unit's boundary lines
The distances to other structures on the Unit

rules.title: Patio floors of concrete, pavers, brick or mortared rock
rules.statement: A {{patio}} floor must be concrete, pavers, brick, or rock set in a full mortar base; a concrete floor may be coated with cool decking.

rules.title: Patio floors should be concrete, pavers, brick or mortared rock
rules.statement: A {{patio}} floor should be concrete, pavers, brick, or rock set in a full mortar base, the appropriate materials; a concrete floor may be coated with cool decking.

rules.title: Decks recommended in wood or composite
rules.statement: A {{deck}} should be constructed of wood or composite materials.

rules.title: Deck color complements the residence
rules.statement: A {{deck}}'s color should complement the {{residence}} color.

check.question: Does the deck's color complement the residence color?

rules.title: No solid walls on patio and deck enclosures
rules.statement: A {{patio-enclosure}} must not have solid walls, including glass; screening will be considered.

rules.title: Screened walls on patio and deck enclosures considered
rules.statement: The {{committee}} considers case by case a {{patio-enclosure}} whose walls are enclosed with screening.

rules.title: Screen under decks more than 6 feet up
rules.statement: The open area under a {{deck}} more than 6 feet above the ground should be screened with landscaping or lattice.

rules.title: Deck lattice in an Exhibit O style
rules.statement: Lattice installed under a {{deck}} must conform to the styles of Exhibit O.

rules.title: Additional screening provisions the Reviewer requires
rules.statement: When the {{committee}} requires additional provisions to reduce the visual impact of a {{deck}}'s lattice screening, the deck must include them.

rules.title: Porch railings of metal, wood or composite, with vertical balusters
rules.statement: A front or back porch {{railing}}, posts and balusters included, must be metal, wood or a composite material, with vertical balusters.

rules.title: Metal porch railings black
rules.statement: A metal porch {{railing}} or handrail must be black.

rules.title: Wood and composite porch railings match the home's body or trim
rules.statement: A wood or composite porch {{railing}}'s stain or material must match the body or trim exterior color of the home.

check.question: Does the railing's wood stain or composite material match the body or trim exterior color of the home?

rules.title: Deck railings of metal, wood, tempered glass or composite
rules.statement: A {{railing}} on a {{deck}} at the back or side of the home, posts and balusters included, must be metal, wood, tempered glass or composite material.

rules.title: Deck railings in a wood-color stain matching the deck and house
rules.statement: A {{railing}} on a {{deck}} at the back or side of the home must be finished in a wood-color stain that matches or is compatible with the deck color and the house color palette.

check.question: Is the railing finished in a wood-color stain that matches or is compatible with the deck color and the house color palette?

rules.title: Black metal balusters on wood deck railings considered
rules.statement: The {{committee}} will consider black metal balusters supporting a wood deck {{railing}} that complement the surrounding materials and wood color.

rules.title: Arched and scalloped gates allowed on solid wood fences
rules.statement: A {{gate}} in an {{fence-style.arched}} or {{fence-style.scalloped}} style may be used on a {{fence-style.wood-tall-solid}} fence.

rules.title: Tall solid wood fences 5 feet 2 inches to 6 feet
rules.statement: A {{fence-style.wood-tall-solid}} {{fence-run}} must have a {{fence-run.height}} of at least 62 and at most 72 inches.

rules.title: Gates on tall solid wood fences have a self-closing latch
rules.statement: A {{gate}} on a {{fence-style.wood-tall-solid}} fence must have a self-closing latch.

rules.title: Gates on tall solid wood fences clear at least 3 feet
rules.statement: A {{gate}} on a {{fence-style.wood-tall-solid}} fence must have a {{gate.clearance}} of at least 36 inches (3 feet).

rules.title: Low open wood fences 40 to 48 inches
rules.statement: A {{fence-style.wood-low-open}} {{fence-run}} must have a {{fence-run.height}} of at least 40 and at most 48 inches.

rules.title: Gates on low open wood fences are self-latching
rules.statement: A {{gate}} on a {{fence-style.wood-low-open}} fence must be self-latching.

rules.title: Gates on low open scallop wood fences are self-latching
rules.statement: A {{gate}} on a {{fence-style.wood-low-open-scallop}} fence must be self-latching.

questions.question: Does "the restrictions on lease terms set forth in this paragraph" in 3.1(c) exempt Units the Declarant or its Affiliates own from only the six-month minimum term, or from every requirement in the paragraph (a written lease, the minimum term and the Governing Documents clause)?

options.label: Only the six-month minimum term
Every requirement in the paragraph

questions.question: Does Exhibit C (a)(xii) ("gardens, planters, and flower beds are permitted if neatly maintained") free them from the Article 4 approval that (a)(x) requires for things on the outside of a Unit, or must they be approved and also kept neat?

options.label: Permitted without Article 4 approval if neatly maintained
Still need Article 4 approval, and must also be neatly maintained

questions.question: 7.4(a)/p2(i) lists towing as an example of emergency self-help. May the Board tow any vehicle that violates the parking rules without notice or a hearing, or only in an emergency?

options.label: Any vehicle in violation of the parking rules
Only in an emergency

questions.question: When must a Neighborhood budget be sent under 8.2/p3 ("Within 30 days prior to the beginning of the fiscal year after the adoption of a final budget")?

options.label: Within the 30 days before the fiscal year begins
At least 30 days before the fiscal year begins
Within 30 days after adoption, as 8.1 says for the Common Expense budget

questions.question: In 11.1(iv)(B), does "after notice and a hearing pursuant to the By-Laws" apply to suspending recreational facilities for a delinquent charge, or only to suspensions for violating the Governing Documents? (7.4(a)(iii) requires notice and an opportunity for a hearing for this suspension, except no hearing once the Owner is more than 30 days delinquent.)

options.label: Only to violations: a delinquent charge alone allows the suspension
To both: a delinquent charge allows the suspension only after notice and a hearing

questions.question: Does termination need first Mortgage holders on Units with 67 percent of all Class "A" votes, or 67 percent of the votes of the Units that have a first Mortgage?

options.label: Of all Class "A" votes, as written
Of the votes of mortgaged Units

questions.question: Does the proviso that a Declarant amendment mustn't adversely affect a Unit's title without its Owner's consent cover only the amendments for the purposes in (a) to (d), or also the any-purpose amendments made before the first Unit is sold?

options.label: Only amendments for the purposes in (a) to (d)
Every unilateral amendment under 20.1's first paragraph

questions.question: 3.5.3 calls the impervious coverage percentages "required" but says Owners "should" follow them, while 7.14.1 says an Owner "must" stay within them for patios, porches and decks. For other Work, is the maximum binding or advice?

options.label: Advice for other Work; binding only for patios, porches and decks
Binding for all Work

questions.question: 3.6/p2 lets the Reviewer waive or vary "any of the procedures or standards", while 3.6/p1 says a guideline that says shall or shall not needs a variance the Board grants. May the DRC waive any guideline, or only the review procedures, leaving shall and shall-not guidelines to a Board variance?

options.label: Any guideline
Only the review procedures; shall and shall-not guidelines need the Board's variance

questions.question: 5.5.1(i) sits under "Wood and Composite Fence Height Limitations" but sets a minimum of 40 inches for "any fence constructed on a Unit". Does the 40-inch minimum apply to wood and composite fences only, or to every fence, metal included?

options.label: Wood and composite fences only
Every fence

questions.question: 5.6.1(i)(c) has the neighboring Owner agree that "the new fence will attach to an existing fence". Is that stipulation needed only for a fence that attaches to a fence on another Unit, or for every fence 5.6.1(i) covers?

options.label: Only for a fence attached to a fence on another Unit
For every fence that needs the neighbor's approval

questions.question: 5.2.2 says a composite fence "should be a K style". Does K style mean the style of Exhibit K (Wood Fence & Gate: Tall - Solid), or a composite style the guidelines don't define?

options.label: A style the guidelines don't define
The style of Exhibit K

questions.question: Exhibits K to N draw the approved fence styles with dimensions (Exhibit L: 40" minimum, 48" maximum for the low open wood fence). Do the drawn dimensions bind, or do the exhibits only show the styles, leaving heights to Article 5's text?

options.label: Only the styles
The drawn dimensions bind too

questions.question: 7.14.4 says appropriate materials for patio floors "include" concrete, pavers, brick, or rock set in a full mortar base. Is that the list of permitted materials, or examples of appropriate ones?

options.label: The permitted materials
Examples: other materials are advisory findings

questions.question: 5.11.3 says small wooden screening devices "can be stained" with an Article 5.4 stain or a color matching the house's body color. Are those the only finishes allowed, or options among others?

options.label: The only finishes allowed
Options among others
